Employment becomes de-materialised and fragmented, bargaining power shifts to capital, and a new labour aristocracy faces a digital proletariat. Yang argues that each Western remedy collides with capital's pursuit of a higher rate of surplus value. Shorter hours cut surplus labour time, while the tax rises needed to fund basic income erode competitiveness. Fragmented employment also undermines social security and trade unions.

Yang contends that under public ownership with the state sector in the leading role, and under Party leadership, these paradoxes can be resolved. State capital returns can fund a basic income that is a form of "capital income" rather than welfare, supplement flexible workers' social insurance, and support working-time reduction and wage consultation. Yang adds that a state fund for creative work could address alienated labour and promote people's free and all-round development. Policy proposals include socialising new AI means of production, universal basic income, and a shift from profit to social value. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy account of AI and inequality that defends a socialist alternative against Western technology-centred analyses.
quoteEn: The problem of income distribution in the age of AI cannot be blamed on AI technology itself; it is closely tied to the nature of the relations of production.
quoteZh: 人工智能时代的收入分配问题，不能归咎于人工智能技术本身，而是与生产关系的性质密切相关。

glossary.explanation: A term for the spread of AI-based systems through production, organisation and management. The article contrasts capitalist and socialist forms of it.
Ownership of the means of production by the whole people or collectives. In China's socialist market economy it is described as the main body of the system, with the state sector in the leading role.
A Marxist ideal of the full development of each individual's physical and intellectual capacities. Chinese Party texts link it to common prosperity.

t: The civilisational significance of building a community with a shared future for mankind and the path to putting it into practice
zh: 构建人类命运共同体的文明意蕴及践行理路
paras: Drawing on Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, Liu Yang asks what kind of world is to be built and how, and argues that a community with a shared future for mankind is best understood as a project of civilisational renewal. In Liu's reading, its purpose is to move beyond the modern civilisation shaped by Western-centrism and to plan the course of twenty-first-century human civilisation as a whole. The article treats this as the deeper aim behind the concept, beyond its role in global governance.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the background: the "changes of the world, of the era and of history" and the intellectual sources of the concept, namely Marx's thought on civilisation and the Chinese tradition of "all under heaven as one family". The second compares the concept with Western civilisation on five dimensions: nature, values, content, mode of interaction and goals. The third turns to practice and proposes five "communities" to be built through the four global initiatives (on development, security, civilisation and governance).

Liu's central contrast is between what the article calls a "deconstructive" Western civilisation and a "constructive" one. Western civilisation is described as driven by capital and marked by universalism, uniformity, hierarchy and short-termism. It is said to rest on a "centre–periphery" order and on the "end of history" thesis. Against this, the community with a shared future for mankind is credited with mutual learning among civilisations, shared human values of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom, balanced development across economic, political, cultural and ecological fields, and equal participation in governance. Liu presents this as a sublation of Western civilisation and as the basis of a "new form of human civilisation". On the practical side, Liu proposes a community of ideas built on dialogue, a development community aimed at the unequal division of labour in global industrial chains, and a security community. Liu also proposes an ecological community resting on "common but differentiated" responsibility, and a cooperative community suited to the shift of power toward the Global South.

Liu concludes that capitalism is not the end point of civilisation and that the "end of history" has failed. The community with a shared future for mankind is presented as China's contribution to human civilisation and a banner for its direction in the twenty-first century. Its ultimate horizon is said to be the "association of free individuals". Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Marxist scholarship frames the concept as a civilisational alternative to the West, with a ready-made programme for implementing it.
quoteEn: Building a community with a shared future for mankind aims to transcend the modern civilisation dominated by Western-centrism and to draw up a fresh, comprehensive plan for the course of human civilisation in the twenty-first century.
quoteZh: 构建人类命运共同体，旨在超越西方中心论统治下的现代文明，对21世纪人类文明发展进程重新作出总体性谋划

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2012–13 for international relations based on shared interests, rights and responsibilities. It is now central to China's foreign policy and global governance discourse.

A formula Xi Jinping introduced in 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Official discourse presents it as an alternative to "universal values" promoted by the West.
A term for developing and emerging economies, used in Chinese official discourse to frame their collective role in reshaping global governance.

glossary.zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议、全球治理倡议
glossary.pinyin: quánqiú fāzhǎn chàngyì, quánqiú ānquán chàngyì, quánqiú wénmíng chàngyì, quánqiú zhìlǐ chàngyì
glossary.explanation: Four proposals announced by Xi Jinping between 2021 and 2025 on development, security, civilisation and governance. They are presented as ways of putting the idea of a community with a shared future into practice.
A phrase used in Party discourse for the civilisation said to be created by Chinese modernization, presented as an alternative to the Western path.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The civilisational narrative and political-cultural logic of building the Chinese national community
zh: 中华民族共同体建设的文明叙事与政治文化逻辑
paras: An Beijiang asks what historical and cultural meaning, and what practical logic, lie behind the building of the Chinese national community (zhonghua minzu gongtongti jianshe), which the article presents as a strategic task of the Party's ethnic work in the new era. Existing research, An says, approaches the topic from theory and practice and from many angles but seldom examines this historical-cultural dimension. The article argues that the project rests on the idea of great unification, takes cultural identity as its core, uses interaction, exchange and integration among ethnic groups as its practical path, and draws on cultural empowerment as its driver.

The article starts from the idea of great unification (dayitong) and traces a shift from the concept of "all under heaven" to a view of unity, from the Zhou enfeoffment system and Confucian and Mencian thought through the Qin-Han county system to the Tang, Yuan and Qing. It then discusses cultural identity and its ethical dimension, the Marxist theory of the nation, and the historical record of ethnic interaction. It ends with contemporary measures: ethnic embeddedness, a shared spiritual home and the mining of cultural resources.

An's central claim is that, unlike Western nation-state theory, great unification stresses historical continuity and political unity. In An's account, frontier and non-Han dynasties from the Northern and Southern Dynasties to the Liao, Jin, Western Xia and Yuan all claimed legitimate succession to "China" and adopted Han institutions and Confucianism, so that the community formed through institutional innovation and value reconstruction rather than simple assimilation or conquest. An reads Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin as treating the nation as a historical community whose formation depends on long interaction. The Party's term "interaction, exchange and integration" is said to avoid equating integration with assimilation, since integration does not erase differences.

An concludes that the project links past and present and offers a "Chinese approach" to governing a multi-ethnic state, achieving political integration without eliminating difference. An proposes embedded social structures and communities, regular education and publicity, preserving historical memory and heritage, and socialist core values as the basis for value consensus. An also calls for opposing narrow nationalism and for creative transformation of traditional culture under the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of borderland studies draws on dynastic history and Marxist nation theory to ground current ethnic policy.
quoteEn: Building the Chinese national community takes the idea of great unification as its foundation, cultural identity as its core, interaction, exchange and integration as its practical path, and cultural empowerment as its innovative driver.
quoteZh: 中华民族共同体建设以大一统思想为根基，以文化认同为内核，以交往交流交融为实践路径，以文化赋能为创新动力

glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese political idea, found in the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, of a single political order over a vast territory. The article treats it as the intellectual root of the modern national community.

glossary.en: interaction, exchange and integration among ethnic groups
glossary.explanation: A Party term for the deepening mixing of ethnic groups in social, economic and cultural life. Official usage distinguishes it from forced assimilation.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

t: Making good use of fine traditional Chinese culture to cultivate the political virtue of officials
zh: 善用中华优秀传统文化涵养为政之德
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how leading cadres can draw on fine traditional Chinese culture to cultivate zhengde, the political virtue of those who govern. Yang argues that traditional ideas such as "governing through virtue" and "the people as the foundation of the state" retain contemporary value. In Yang's view, they help officials form a correct view of performance and improve the modernization of national governance, in line with Xi Jinping's call to use traditional culture to "rectify the mind and clarify virtue".

The piece has three parts. The first sets out what traditional culture contains on political virtue, under three heads: governance of the state, benefit to the people, and self-cultivation. The second argues that these ideas still have vitality today. The third turns to practice and sets out how Party members and cadres should apply them.

Yang draws on Confucius, the Guanzi, Fan Zhongyan and other classical sources. The author claims these ideas match the Party's demands for loyalty to the people, practical and clean conduct, and fairness. After creative transformation, Yang says, they have merged with the core socialist values. They supply a moral foundation for national development, social stability and cadre self-discipline. The practical section lists four requirements: put the people first, favour practical work over formalism and bureaucratism, exercise power impartially and for the public good, and plan for the long term.

Yang concludes that cadres should draw on traditional wisdom on the principle of making the past serve the present while preserving what is sound and innovating. The aim is to sustain their bond with the people and strengthen their ability to carry out their duties. Yang holds up historical figures such as Bao Zheng and Yu Qian, and Party models such as Jiao Yulu and Yang Shanzhou, as mirrors for cadres. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present traditional culture as a resource for official ethics and cadre education.
quoteEn: These ideas closely link personal moral cultivation with the responsibilities of national governance, so that moral cultivation is no longer empty preaching but a guide to action running through the whole process of performing one's duties.
quoteZh: 这些理念把个人品德修养和国家治理的责任紧密联系，使道德修养不再是空洞说教，而是贯穿履职全过程的行动遵循。

glossary.explanation: The moral character expected of those who hold public office. Xi Jinping has urged leading cadres to "speak of political virtue", and the term draws on Confucian ideas of rule by moral example.
An official phrase for the parts of China's cultural heritage that the Party regards as worth drawing on. It is often paired with the idea of creative transformation and innovative development.
A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to modernizing the country's system and capacity for governance.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They cover national, social and individual levels.

t: Turning the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era into concrete practice
zh: 把新时代党的治藏方略转化为具体实践
paras: Writing at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026), Yao Yu asks how the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era should be understood and put into practice. The newspaper commentary argues that Xi Jinping's directives on Tibet work, centred on four major tasks (stability, development, ecology and strengthening the border), give Tibet's long-term stability and high-quality development a clear direction. Yao holds that these tasks should be pursued in close connection with Tibetan realities and with the aim of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first explains the strategy, summarised by Xi Jinping as the "ten musts", and the five principles Yao singles out. The second reviews what Yao describes as achievements in Tibet in each of the four areas, with figures for 2025. The third links the four tasks to the work of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and ends with four proposals.

Yao presents the five principles (governing Tibet by law, enriching the people and rejuvenating Tibet, long-term building of Tibet, winning hearts and minds, and strengthening foundations) as an interlocking system that provides a methodology for Tibet work. The article cites figures as evidence: regional GDP of 301.89 billion yuan... as reported, 303.189 billion yuan, growth of 7.0%, urban per capita disposable income at 104.1% of the national average, more than 50% of land placed under ecological red lines, and 12.52 million... as reported, 125,200 km of roads. Yao also reports public satisfaction with security above 99% and the development of border villages such as Yumai. Yao then argues that each of the four tasks is itself a concrete way of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. Stability enables exchange among ethnic groups, shared development gives a material basis, ecological protection serves the national community, and guarding the border expresses patriotism.

Yao proposes four lines of work: keep law at the centre and improve institutional safeguards, including integrating the sense of community into national, cadre and social education; use culture to build a shared spiritual home, drawing on the "old Tibet spirit" and the "two roads" spirit; promote mutual embedding through everyday contact, moving from shared space to shared hearts; and use the common cause of socialist modernization to bring all ethnic groups into local economic construction and its benefits. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Tibet policy is framed in 2026, with the statistics and policy language used to present it.
quoteEn: Getting the four major tasks of stability, development, ecology and border consolidation right is precisely the concrete practice of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 抓好稳定、发展、生态、强边四件大事，正是铸牢中华民族共同体意识的具体实践。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: casting firm the consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A slogan designating the main thread of the Party's ethnic work since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It stresses national identity shared by all ethnic groups.
Xi Jinping's formulation of priorities for Tibet work: stability, development, ecology and strengthening the border.
Official term for an economic development model stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed alone.
Xi Jinping's summary of the Party's Tibet strategy at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work (2020), a set of ten principles.

keywords: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation

t: The ethical dimension of AI governance in the new era
zh: 新时代人工智能治理的伦理向度
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (23 March 2026), Lu Xiangfeng takes up the question of how artificial intelligence should be governed ethically. Opening with Xi Jinping's call to improve AI regulatory mechanisms and keep the initiative in AI development and governance, Lu argues that AI governance has moved beyond technology into a core issue of global governance. The article's thesis is that ethical construction, ethical governance and ethical innovation must be combined if AI is to develop in a beneficial direction.

The piece has three main sections: building ethical norms for AI governance, the ethical essence of AI governance, and ethical innovation. Lu traces a line of theory from Asimov's three laws of robotics, through Wiener, to the 'value alignment' associated with Meinel and others. The article also lists three routes to implementation: top-down norm-coding, bottom-up learning from experience, and a hybrid of the two. It cites international documents since 2024, including the Beijing AI Safety International Consensus and the Shanghai Declaration on Global AI Governance.

Lu contends that value alignment, which treats human values as static, is insufficient and should give way to 'value symbiosis', in which humans and machines adjust and evolve together. Lu names three underlying problems: blurred lines between self-interested and genuine altruism, with information capitalism concentrating data power and shifting risk onto the public; failure to translate humanity's highest spiritual values into principles machines can follow; and neglect of existential threats, including the erosion of human subjectivity. The article asks whether technology is driven by scientific autonomy or by capital and power, and warns that ethics confined to technical risk control will reproduce paradoxes such as 'using algorithms to prevent cheating'.

Lu proposes three innovations: a principle of shared risk, under which designers and manufacturers bear risks such as information and responsibility asymmetries; an 'endosymbiotic' human–AI structure to guide memetic mutation; and a 'coexistence' perspective that makes responsibility and survival risk the highest value. Lu calls for an emergency ethics that builds a dynamic, trustworthy ethical baseline for human–machine symbiosis, and for ethical theory to keep pace with technology. Read the original if you want a short example of how a Chinese Marxist ethics scholar frames AI governance in terms of capital logic, value symbiosis and shared responsibility.
quoteEn: Only when AI agents behave altruistically in their ethical design can the self-reflexive process of governing generative AI truly begin.
quoteZh: 只有人工智能体在伦理设计中表现为利他行为，自反性的生成式人工智能治理过程才能真正开启。

glossary.explanation: The AI-ethics idea that AI systems should be built to act in accordance with human values. Lu argues it treats those values as static and should be replaced by 'value symbiosis'.
Lu's term for a stage in which humans and machines reach shared understanding and adjust and evolve together, rather than machines simply matching fixed human values.
A biological metaphor Lu uses for a close, mutually dependent human–AI system that adjusts dynamically, rather than a simple subject–object relation.
Lu's perspective that makes shared responsibility and risk, and the prevention of existential risks to humanity, the highest value in AI ethics.

t: Understanding the scientific connotations and practical requirements of the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era
zh: 深刻理解新时代党的治藏方略的科学内涵与实践要求
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 23 March 2026, sets out how the author understands the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era. Cui Luchun, executive vice-president of the Tibet Autonomous Region Party School, argues that the strategy, summarised by Xi Jinping as the "ten musts", sums up and develops the Party's experience of governing, stabilising and developing Tibet. In Cui's account it is the concentrated expression of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era on Tibet work and supplies the basic guide for building a modern socialist "new Tibet".

The article has three parts. The first walks through each of the ten "musts", announced at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work in August 2020. The second reviews the results of the strategy in practice. The third sets out requirements for carrying it out, drawing on Xi's instructions of 20 August 2025.

In the first part, Cui presents the ten requirements as a framework covering Party leadership, the system of regional ethnic autonomy, safeguarding national unity, the principles of governing Tibet by law and enriching the people, linking domestic and international situations, ethnic exchange and mingling, the Sinicization of religion, ecological protection as the first priority, and Party building. The second part cites achievements in four areas. These are stability, with a reported security and satisfaction index above 99%; high-quality development, with a regional GDP of 303.189 billion yuan in 2025; an ecological security barrier; and border consolidation, including 624 completed border xiaokang villages. The third part calls for upholding the Party's overall leadership, forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation as the main thread, and guiding development by the "Three Bestowals and One Conducive To". It also calls for building a national ecological civilization highland and creating a demonstration zone for strengthening and enriching the border areas.

Cui concludes that Tibet should carry out the strategy in full, with progress sought within stability. Xi's "four major tasks" of stability, development, ecology and border strengthening are to guide the work. Cui treats this as the route to long-term stability and high-quality development. Read the original if you want an official Party-school account of how the ten "musts" are framed, and of the policy priorities and statistics presented for Tibet in 2026.
quoteEn: Adhering to the direction of the Sinicization of religion is the necessary path for actively guiding Tibetan Buddhism to adapt to socialist society.
quoteZh: 坚持宗教中国化方向，是积极引导藏传佛教与社会主义社会相适应的必由之路

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's August 2020 summary of the Party's approach to Tibet, presented as ten requirements. It is officially described as the core of the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era.

The constitutional system under which areas with concentrated minority populations set up autonomous organs of self-government within the unitary state. It is presented officially as a basic political institution.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A Party policy line since the 19th Party Congress (2017) that makes shared national identity the main thread of ethnic work.
Official policy that religions in China should adapt to Chinese culture and to socialist society, under Party leadership and state regulation.

glossary.pinyin: sān gè fùyǔ, yī gè yǒulìyú
glossary.en: Three Bestowals and One Conducive To
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for Tibet's development, used in the text as a general requirement for its economic and social work. The article does not spell out its content.

t: Safeguarding national economic security through information security
zh: 以信息安全保障国家经济安全
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 20 March 2026, asks how information security can underpin national economic security. Sun Zao and Wang Le start from the proposal in the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan to "safeguard national economic security". They argue that, as the digital economy grows and data becomes a core means of production, protecting information is a necessary condition for protecting the economy and a support for Chinese modernization.

The article is organised as a four-part policy agenda, set within the holistic approach to national security. The parts are a sound legal and regulatory system; talent training and technology research and development; stronger information security awareness; and participation in international information security cooperation. Each part is divided into specific measures.

On regulation, the authors call for detailed implementing rules under the Data Security Law and the Cybersecurity Law. They propose that key data stay within its domain, with sensitive data kept local; special rules for artificial intelligence, covering training-data checks, algorithmic discrimination and labelling of generated content; a "whitelist plus security assessment" system for cross-border data flows; and graded emergency response plans. On talent and technology, they urge interdisciplinary university programmes, joint training bases with firms, a national special fund, and wider use of technologies such as zero-trust architecture and data desensitisation. On awareness, they propose industry self-regulation bodies, annual compliance ratings, firm-level responsibility across the data life cycle, and public education.

On the international side, Sun and Wang call for involvement in standard-setting through the United Nations, the G20 and APEC, and for mutual recognition of security assessments for cross-border data. They also propose joint research, cooperation against cross-border cybercrime, and a service platform to protect Chinese firms abroad. For serious infringements such as data theft or cyberattack, they say reciprocal countermeasures should be taken in accordance with international rules. They conclude that a systematic layout across these four areas would lay a firm foundation for building China into a strong country and for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise inventory of the policy measures that Chinese economists link to data security and economic security under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Against the background of rapid global growth of the digital economy and of digital factors becoming a core means of production, safeguarding information security has become a necessary requirement for defending economic security.
quoteZh: 在全球数字经济高速发展、数字要素成为核心生产资料的时代背景下，保障信息安全已成为捍卫经济安全的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
A security concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats political, economic, cultural, technological, information and other fields of security as interlinked.
The national medium-term plan for 2026–2030, setting the main development goals and tasks for that period.
The transfer of data out of or into China, which Chinese law subjects to security assessment and regulation.

t: Capitalist states' self-diagnosis of the contemporary crisis: an analysis based on mainstream Anglo-American media
zh: 资本主义国家关于当代危机的自我诊断：基于英美等主流媒体的解析
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2025 no. 12
paras: Why have mainstream Anglo-American media and commentators begun publishing what Chen Huiyuan calls "pathology reports" on their own system, after the post-Cold War confidence of Fukuyama's "end of history"? Chen asks whether this self-diagnosis shows a capacity for self-repair or a structural collapse of neoliberalism. The article argues that the recurring themes of political paralysis, economic stagnation and cultural decay are not isolated ailments but projections of capitalism's basic contradiction between socialised production and private appropriation, in the age of financialisation and digitalisation.

Using 2020–2025 in-depth commentary from The Guardian, New York Times, Financial Times, The Economist and other outlets as "discourse samples", the article proceeds through four dimensions. It treats political governance failure and the loss of political identification (the US shutdown of 2025, French cabinet instability, European fragmentation, right- and left-wing populism, Mamdani's election); economic accumulation (long-term stagnation, financialisation, "digital feudalism", inequality, the squeezed middle class, education and deindustrialisation); culture and geostrategy (cultural fatigue, culture wars, strategic overload under Trump's second term); and a final theoretical synthesis. Each section pairs media evidence with theory from Habermas, Streeck, Harvey, Gramsci and Weber.

Chen's central move is to read the media's descriptions through Marxist political economy. Falling profit rates in the real economy, the article says, push capital from "productive" to rentier and predatory accumulation, which it interprets through Harvey's "accumulation by dispossession" turned inward on domestic society through debt, privatisation and digital enclosure. A second move uses Harvey's "spatial fix": Chen argues that multipolarity and geopolitical conflict have blocked the external outlets that once exported contradictions, so they now return to the core as polarisation and paralysis. Third, Chen draws on Gramsci, Habermas and Weber to argue that the "promise of growth" and the "promise of democracy" have both failed, producing a legitimacy implosion, a collapse of hegemonic consensus and culture wars as substitute mobilisation.

Chen concludes that Western crises stem from the internal limits of the capitalist model of modernisation, which neither policy fixes nor external shocks can explain. The spread of self-diagnosis is itself part of the crisis: it describes reality and concedes a loss of legitimacy, while old forms of ideological integration fail and new ones have not emerged. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of how Western media narrate decline, with extensive Anglo-American press examples from 2020–2025 set against critical theory.
quoteEn: The wave of "self-diagnosis" in Western public opinion is in essence a "self-anxiety" produced by this institutional system as it faces structural contradictions that it cannot overcome through its own mechanisms.
quoteZh: 西方舆论界兴起的“自我诊断”热潮，实质上是这一制度体系在面对无法通过自身机制克服的结构性矛盾时所产生的“自我焦虑”。

t: New problems in building an intelligent society and ways to resolve them
zh: 智能社会建设面临的新问题及破解思路
paras: Wang Wei asks how China can build an "intelligent society" (one organised around AI, the Internet of Things and blockchain) while managing the "growing pains" it brings. The article argues that this transition is a product of the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Wang contends that it is strategically necessary, but that it generates ethical, social, security and governance risks. These, in Wang's view, call for a response built on the rule of law, people-centred priorities, multi-party governance and innovation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why an intelligent society matters, drawing on Marx's remark about the hand-mill and the steam-mill, Xi Jinping's statements and examples such as smart factories, urban command centres, online medical services and assistive technologies. The second catalogues problems under three headings: ethics (algorithmic bias, privacy leakage, the weakening of human agency through algorithmic substitution), social structure (structural unemployment, the gig economy, the digital divide) and security and governance (cyberattacks, deepfakes, lagging regulation, public distrust). The third proposes four pathways: top-level design, value orientation, governance mechanisms and innovation.

Wang's central move is to treat these problems as technological alienation under unequal power relations rather than as neutral side effects. The author therefore calls for anti-monopoly enforcement, data-ownership rules and benefit-sharing, together with guarantees of people's rights to be informed, to choose and to opt out. Concrete proposals include tiered regulation with sandbox testing for high-risk fields and negative lists for low-risk ones, digital-literacy programmes, portable social-security accounts, a pilot of universal basic income and three-dimensional education reform. Governance, Wang argues, should rest on cooperation among government, enterprises, academia and the public, with ethics review built into research and an "ethics veto" for high-risk technologies. The author also stresses self-reliance in core technologies such as AI security, privacy computing and trustworthy blockchain.

Wang concludes that intelligent technology should serve human liberation and all-round development, in line with Marx's vision of a community in which each person's free development is the condition for all. The article presents its proposals as consistent with Xi Jinping Thought and Chinese modernization, and as a way to ensure that intelligence benefits the people, social progress and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a policy-oriented Chinese Marxist account of AI governance, with specific institutional proposals and the official sources it cites.
quoteEn: Technological innovation cannot pursue only efficiency and speed; it must also build ethics, security and sustainability into the whole process of research and development.
quoteZh: 技术创新不能仅追求效率与速度，更需将伦理、安全与可持续内化于研发全过程。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. Authors commonly cite it as the basis for policy positions.

t: A critique of the ideological logic of cognitive capitalism
zh: 认知资本主义的意识形态逻辑批判
paras: Deng Bojun asks how ideology operates under "cognitive capitalism", a concept taken from the French scholar Yann Moulier-Boutang and used for a capitalism in which knowledge, information and data replace material resources as the main means of production. Deng's thesis is that its ideology has shifted from visible repression to hidden production: capital no longer coerces workers from outside but makes them "voluntarily" accept domination. In this reading it remains, in essence, the dictatorship of the bourgeoisie in a new form.

The article first contrasts industrial and cognitive capitalism, then traces a lineage of ideology critique from Marx and Engels' "false consciousness" through Althusser's ideological state apparatuses to Foucault's technologies of the self. It then examines how the ideology is generated: the new form of the means of production (data, algorithms, intellectual property), changed labour forms such as "immaterial labour" and "play labour", and the role of knowledge production, algorithms and platforms. It goes on to "colonisation" in the economic, political and cultural spheres, and ends with strategies of resistance.

Deng's central claim is that the non-rival nature of data forces its monopolisation to be dressed in a rhetoric of knowledge sharing and liberation. Platforms, algorithmic management, user agreements and a "knowledge–power–capital" alliance with academia and the state then turn exploitation into self-exploitation. Deng treats algorithmic rent as surplus value from appropriated "general intelligence", producing real subsumption of cognitive production. The article describes platforms as "digital landlords" and creators as "digital tenants", and presents the new ideology as the "de-ideologisation of ideology", in which capital's logic appears as natural common sense.

Deng proposes a systematic "decolonisation" of the cognitive sphere. Its elements are public ownership of data, democratised algorithms, open collaboration, digital unions and cognitive-labour cooperatives. Legal measures include knowledge-commons legislation, cognitive-labour rights and rules for platform power. Technical proposals include decentralised data, algorithm and platform governance, plus cross-border cooperation against tax arbitrage and infrastructure monopolies. Deng frames this as proletarian class struggle in the cognitive domain, aimed at seizing control of cognitive means of production and moving toward socialism and communism. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist critique of data, algorithms and platforms that combines Marx, Althusser, Foucault and Heidegger with concrete legal and technical proposals.
quoteEn: The deeper logic by which cognitive capitalism makes subjects accept oppression voluntarily is not a \"benevolent turn\" in capital's rule. It is an upgrade by which bourgeois dictatorship, adapting to new forms of knowledge production, cognitive labour and digital technology, shifts its logic of domination from external coercion to cognitive internalisation.
quoteZh: 认知资本主义中让主体自愿被压迫的深层逻辑，并非资本统治的“仁慈化”,而是资产阶级专政为适应知识生产、认知劳动、数字技术的新形态，将统治逻辑从外部强制转向认知内化的升级。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Yann Moulier-Boutang for a phase of capitalism in which knowledge, information and immaterial labour become the main sources of accumulation. Deng uses it to analyse platform and data capitalism.
Maurizio Lazzarato's term for labour that produces the informational and cultural content of commodities. The article treats it as the typical labour form of cognitive capitalism.
A notion from Marx's Grundrisse for society's accumulated knowledge as a productive force. The article argues that capital appropriates it through algorithms and data.
A Marxist-Leninist term for bourgeois class rule over the state and society, whatever the formal political system. Deng uses it to characterise cognitive capitalism.

t: Better realising the strategic guiding role of national development plans on the track of the rule of law
zh: 在法治轨道上更好发挥国家发展规划的战略导向作用
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 17 March 2026, discusses the Law of the People's Republic of China on National Development Planning, adopted at the fourth session of the 14th National People's Congress. Li and Chen argue that the law is a milestone: it puts a long-standing governing method of the Party on a legal footing and, in their words, uses the stability of law to meet external uncertainty. They present it as an institutional guarantee for scientific plan-making and effective implementation as the 15th Five-Year Plan period begins.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the law is urgently needed for the modernization of state governance. The second explains the law's basic spirit and main provisions. The third turns to practical requirements for putting the law into effect. It leans throughout on quotations from Xi Jinping on planning, the rule of law and the socialist market economy.

On the need for the law, the authors give three reasons: it advances the construction of a law-based China, it improves the socialist market economy by giving firms stable expectations and drawing limits around government powers in planning, and it strengthens macroeconomic governance by keeping national goals from being diluted by administrative level or local interests. On the law's content, they stress four features: the Party's overall leadership written into the planning procedure; a planning system led by the national development plan, with spatial, sector-specific, regional and local plans beneath it; binding principles for plan-making, including public consultation under whole-process people's democracy and assessment of fiscal capacity and risk; and stronger review, approval and supervision, including the rule that a published plan may not be altered without legal procedure.

For implementation, the authors call for annual plans and all other plans to be linked to the national plan, with binding targets broken down year by year. They also call for consistency checks on fiscal, monetary, industrial and other policies, and for funds, land, credit and data to follow major projects, while projects that diverge from the plan are denied approval. They further urge local plans to follow higher-level ones, and full-cycle monitoring, mid-term and final evaluation, and accountability for formalism, illegal approvals and vanity projects. Read the original if you want an official account of how the new planning law is presented and what implementation measures Party-state commentary is advocating.
quoteEn: The Law on National Development Planning clearly defines the boundaries of government powers and responsibilities in drawing up and implementing plans, in effect setting a "red line" for public power and leaving ample room for the market to allocate resources.
quoteZh: 国家发展规划法明确界定政府在规划编制实施中的权责边界，实质上是为公权力划定“红线”，为市场配置资源留出充分空间。

glossary.explanation: The central medium- and long-term plan, in practice the Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development, which sets strategic goals for the country and guides lower-level plans.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019 to describe the Chinese political system as democratic across the full cycle of policy-making, including consultation and implementation.

t: Creating a sound rule-of-law environment to promote high-quality development
zh: 为推动高质量发展营造良好法治环境
paras: Writing in the People's Daily (13 March 2026), Feng Lixia takes up how law can support high-quality development. The commentary opens by noting that the Fourth Session of the 14th National People's Congress had just passed three laws at once: the Ecological Environment Code, the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, and the National Development Planning Law. Feng's thesis is that the socialist market economy is in essence a "law-based economy", and that building one is the way to create a good rule-of-law environment for high-quality development.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the socialist market economy is a law-based economy, drawing on Xi Jinping's statements from 2014 to 2024. The second follows the rule of law through four links of economic circulation: production, distribution, circulation and consumption. The third sets out practical paths for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), organised around legislation, law enforcement, the judiciary and law-abidingness.

Feng argues that markets operate through legal forms, so a socialist market economy needs law to protect property, secure fair competition and keep the economy circulating. Building a law-based economy depends on combining an "effective market" with a "capable government". Feng reads this as a government that does what the law requires and nothing the law has not authorised, and that uses law to mark the boundary between government and market. Feng adds that improving the business environment means unified market rules, enforcement standards and judicial criteria, and clearing away local rules that obstruct a unified national market. For each link of the economy Feng gives legal tasks: equal protection of property, including the Private Economy Promotion Law in force since 20 May 2025; distribution rules covering all three distributions; credit systems and action against local protectionism in circulation; and consumer-rights protection.

For the 15th Five-Year Plan period, Feng calls for higher-quality legislation in key, emerging and foreign-related fields, to support new quality productive forces. Feng also calls for service-oriented, standardised enforcement, and for the judiciary to avoid treating economic disputes as crimes. Feng also wants the Fengqiao experience developed in dispute mediation, and a culture of compliance and good faith among firms. Feng presents this as both a practical route to balancing development and security and a long-term task for modernising national governance by 2035. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary links Xi Jinping's economic thought and legal thought, and how it frames law for market regulation, property protection and enforcement.
quoteEn: The socialist market economy is a market economy under the socialist system and conforms to the general laws of market economies. It inherently requires law as an important support for economic operation, which determines that its essence is a law-based economy.
quoteZh: 社会主义市场经济是社会主义制度下的市场经济，符合市场经济的一般规律，内在地要求以法治作为经济运行的重要依托，这就决定了其本质就是一种法治经济。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's economic and legal thought holding that market economic activity must be governed by law. Xi has stated that the socialist market economy is in essence a law-based economy.
The official goal since around 2017 of shifting from fast growth to growth based on quality, innovation and efficiency.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
A model of community-level dispute mediation from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s. The Party has promoted it as a way to resolve conflicts locally.

t: Digital rentier capitalism: three manifestations, formation mechanism and internal contradictions
zh: 数字食利资本主义的三重表现、形成机理和内在矛盾
paras: Hao Ruilin and Han Wenlong ask what is new about the rentier character of capitalism in the digital age, how these changes arise, and how China should respond. Working from Marxist political economy, they argue that contemporary capitalism has produced a 'digital rentier capitalism' distinct from the industrial and financial capitalism of earlier eras. In their account it is driven by capital's own movement and produces contradictions that advanced capitalist states try to push outward onto the world.

The article first sets out three changes in the rentier economy: the mode of rent-seeking, the source of profit and the rentier class itself. It then explains the formation of this system through the rise of digital capital, platform accumulation, the merger of digital and financial capital, and the union of capital with political power. It goes on to analyse the contradictions and their external transfer, drawing mainly on US examples, and ends with proposals for China.

The authors contend that rent has shifted from financial speculation to technology patents, platform monopolies and data. Profit now draws on 'digital gig workers', whom platforms control by algorithm without employing them, and the rentier bloc has become a 'technology–finance–politics' alliance. They hold that digital capital arises as users' unpaid data labour and replicable digital products are turned into data commodities and then data capital. The central contradiction, in their reading, is between increasingly socialised production and private ownership of platforms, technology and data. They say this stifles innovation, depresses workers' consumption and breeds social anarchy. They add that it also drives de-globalisation, 'digital colonialism' and political interference abroad, which in turn split the imperialist camp and prompt resistance in developing countries.

Hao and Han argue that China's basic socialist economic system and its technological strengths put it in a favourable position to resist these pressures. They propose building a community of digital destiny through international technology cooperation and rule-making. They also call for regulating capital and guarding against its disorderly expansion, and for building new production relations. These would include rights protections for platform workers and clearer ownership, use and income rights over data. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist political-economy analysis of platform and data capitalism, and the policy conclusions it draws for China.
quoteEn: The formation of digital capital means that the channels of capital valorisation have begun to shift systematically towards digital rent.
quoteZh: 数字资本的形成意味着，资本增殖渠道开始系统地向数字租金转变。

glossary.explanation: The authors' term for a stage of capitalism in which tech giants, financial oligarchs and politicians extract income through technology, platforms and data rather than production. It builds on earlier 'rentier capitalism' arguments such as Guy Standing's.
Workers such as ride-hailing drivers, couriers and content creators who depend on platforms for work without a formal employment relationship with them.
An extension of the official 'community with a shared future for mankind' to the digital sphere, referring to international cooperation on digital infrastructure and governance.
In Marxist terms, the social relations (ownership, labour, distribution) that the authors say must be rebuilt to fit digital productive forces.

t: The Global Security Initiative: China's proposal for a security order in a multipolar world
zh: 全球安全倡议：构建多极世界安全秩序的中国方案
paras: The article asks what the Global Security Initiative, proposed by Xi Jinping in 2022, offers as an alternative to the Western-dominated security order. The authors argue that the Initiative is a comprehensive Chinese proposal that treats security and prosperity as global public goods. They hold that it reflects a shift from a unipolar to a multipolar order driven by China's rise, and that its success depends on the willingness of states to build security consensus and trust.

The text first sets out China's economic, technological and military rise and the Initiative's six core principles and five dimensions of security: political, economic, social, environmental and digital. It then places the Initiative in a non-Western tradition of international relations, drawing on the idea of tianxia, and contrasts it with NATO-style collective security. A third section describes implementation through the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, the Belt and Road Initiative and BRICS, and through bilateral defence dialogue, exercises and security assistance. The longest section turns to Latin America and the Caribbean.

The authors argue that the Initiative rests on three principles: sustainable security, interdependence and non-interference. They present these as distinct from Western approaches that separate security from development, bypass multilateral bodies and justify intervention through liberal interventionism and the "responsibility to protect". In their account, Latin American states find the Initiative congenial because it matches their own traditions of sovereignty and self-determination. They cite Nicaragua and Venezuela as endorsing it, and note that the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC)–China Forum documents and Chinese support for a Latin American zone of peace point the same way. Three cases illustrate practice: the Chinese deep-space station in Neuquén, Argentina, the ECU911 security system in Ecuador, and biotechnology cooperation with Cuba. The authors also say Latin American states are growing more cautious as they balance between China and the United States.

The authors conclude that the Initiative is a programmatic statement of a non-confrontational security philosophy that casts China as a guardian of stability and a development partner. They say that, in Latin America, aligning security concepts and interests could help root the Initiative in regional needs. Read the original if you want a Chinese-Cuban co-authored account of how the Initiative is presented to the Global South, especially the Latin American cases and the contrast drawn with Western security thinking.
quoteEn: China advances the Global Security Initiative in order to build a more peaceful and prosperous world, so that security becomes a global public good rather than the exclusive privilege of a few great powers.
quoteZh: 中国倡导全球安全倡议，旨在构建一个更加和平繁荣的世界，从而让安全成为全球公共产品而非少数大国专属特权。

glossary.explanation: A framework Xi Jinping announced in 2022, built on six principles including a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security outlook. A concept paper was later published to elaborate it.
A Chinese programme launched in 2013 for infrastructure, trade and financing links across Eurasia, Africa and Latin America.

A classical Chinese notion of "all under heaven", describing a harmonious political order beyond the nation-state. Some Chinese scholars use it as a source for non-Western international relations theory.

t: The jurisprudential logic of implementing the core socialist values in judicial adjudication
zh: 司法贯彻社会主义核心价值观的法理逻辑
source: Journal of Harbin Institute of Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 6
paras: Wang and Zhang ask how courts can apply the core socialist values in individual judgments without turning them into empty slogans or letting them displace legal rules. They argue that the values hold the position of a "quasi-source of law" (zhun fayuan). In their account, this status permits a supplementary role in legal reasoning, but never a role as the basis of a judgment, and needs a systematic method to be applied reliably.

The article starts from the policy trajectory since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the 2018 constitutional amendment and the Supreme People's Court's guidance documents. It then analyses six batches of model cases, 64 in total, issued by the Supreme People's Court, together with data on judgments published on the national court judgments website. Using these materials, it identifies recurring problems in current practice and proposes a reconstructed reasoning framework.

The authors find that only 13 of the 64 model cases mention the values in the "judgment result" section, and that in some of these the values made no real difference to the outcome. In ordinary judgments they identify three faults: equating the values' legal meaning with moral meaning, "rule escape" (citing the values where a clear statutory rule exists), and "label-sticking" citation without reasoning. Their remedy has three parts. First, the twelve keywords should be turned into a concrete pairing of "motive plus specific behaviour pattern". Second, judges should choose keywords step by step from the citizen level, through the social level, to the national level. Third, the traditional judicial syllogism should be recast as a "recursive four-step syllogism" (digui si duan lun), in which a values-based second minor premise is added and combined with comparison to similar cases.

The authors conclude that citing the values adds legitimacy and persuasiveness to judgments, but that vague invocation or substitution for legal norms undermines the stability and authority of law. They call for a complete methodology, along with regular revision and clearing of model and database cases, so that procedural fairness secures substantive fairness. Read the original if you study Chinese judicial practice, the legal status of ideological values, or the detailed analysis of Supreme People's Court model cases and the proposed reasoning model.
quoteEn: The integration of the core socialist values into judicial adjudication cannot be mere symbolic incorporation; it must take part in substantive fact-finding and legal judgment, in legal interpretation and legal reasoning, and enter into substantive argumentation.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观融入司法裁判，不能是简单的符号化融入，而应当参与实质的事实认定、法律判断;参与法律解释、法律推理，介入实质论证。

glossary.explanation: A twelve-word set of values first articulated at the 18th Party Congress in 2012: prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony (national level); freedom, equality, justice, rule of law (social level); patriotism, dedication, integrity, friendliness (citizen level).
The authors' label for the core socialist values' intermediate status in adjudication. They are not binding rules or principles, but they may be cited to support legal reasoning.
The authors' proposed reasoning model. It replaces the minor premise of the classic judicial syllogism with a recursive premise and adds a second minor premise based on a value keyword.
Cases selected, edited and published by the Supreme People's Court or Procuratorate to illustrate how the law and policy goals, here the core socialist values, should be applied.

t: The Global Governance Initiative offers Global South countries development opportunities and momentum for cooperation
zh: 全球治理倡议为全球南方国家提供发展机遇和合作动能
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 11 March 2026, argues that the Global Governance Initiative, which it presents as China's latest public good for the world after the "three major initiatives", gives the Global South new development opportunities and momentum for cooperation. Wang Bo contends that it helps move the international political and economic order in a more democratic, just and reasonable direction.

The piece first describes the case for reform: the Global South's growing weight, and a governance system that Wang says is still dominated by Western countries. It then sets out the initiative's five core principles, four ways it benefits the Global South, and China's own practice as a Global South member.

Wang cites figures that the Global South accounts for over 40% of world output and 80% of global growth contribution over the past 20 years. Against this, the author says the current system fails to reflect that shift and cannot handle problems such as climate change and public health crises amid unilateralism and protectionism. The five principles are sovereign equality, international rule of law, multilateralism, a people-centred approach and action orientation. The four benefits are practical development support, stronger solidarity and South-South cooperation, a higher status and voice that closes the "representation deficit", and greater mutual learning among civilizations.

Wang concludes that China is both proposer and practitioner, pointing to the Belt and Road Initiative, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the New Development Bank, the Paris Agreement and the Kunming-Montreal biodiversity framework. The author reports support from over 150 countries and organisations and a UN "Group of Friends" with over 40 founding members. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the initiative is presented to a domestic audience in official commentary.
quoteEn: The Global Governance Initiative promotes equal participation, equal decision-making and equal benefit for all countries in global governance, bridges the "representation deficit", makes the global governance architecture more balanced and effective, and injects more stability into international affairs.
quoteZh: 全球治理倡议推动各国在全球治理进程中平等参与、平等决策、平等受益，弥合“代表性赤字”，推动全球治理架构更为均衡有效，为国际事务注入更多稳定性。

glossary.explanation: A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping to build a more just and reasonable global governance system. The article presents it as following the Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives.
A term for developing and emerging countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to describe a group it says is rising collectively and counts China among.
A China-led initiative launched in 2013 for infrastructure and economic cooperation across Asia, Africa, Europe and beyond.

t: Advancing the building of the Chinese nation as a community and realising national rejuvenation
zh: 推进中华民族共同体建设 实现中华民族伟大复兴
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 12 March 2026, this commentary takes up the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee's (2025) recommendation for the 15th Five-Year Plan to "forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation" and advance the building of the Chinese nation as a community. Wang argues that this task is the core requirement of ethnic unity work in the coming five years. In Wang's account, it is also the mainline of the Party's ethnic work and a necessary condition of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Party's leadership of ethnic work from its founding through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second assesses the theoretical and practical strength of Xi Jinping's ideas on ethnic work, including their relevance for other countries. The third sets out five areas of work for the Chinese modernization drive.

Wang's central claim is that the idea of building the community is a product of the Two Integrations, which join Marxist ethnic theory with China's concrete realities and its fine traditional culture. In this reading, the path differs both from the Western "one nation, one state" model and from the ethnic governance of feudal dynasties. Wang cites results as evidence: 31.21 million people in ethnic minority areas lifted out of poverty, and the combined GDP of the five autonomous regions rising from 6,012.9 billion to 8,376.6 billion yuan between 2020 and 2024. Wang contrasts this with other states that, in the article's account, pursue forced assimilation, tolerate separatism or practise divide-and-rule, and presents China's approach as a model for global ethnic governance.

For future work, Wang calls for strengthening Party leadership and national security safeguards in ethnic affairs. Other proposals are to build a shared spiritual home through cultural identity, to speed high-quality development in ethnic areas, to promote interaction and mixing among ethnic groups through mutually embedded social structures, and to govern ethnic affairs by law, including a planned law on promoting ethnic unity and progress. Wang presents these as the way to gather strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of current Party discourse on ethnic policy, with the official statistics and policy priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.)
quoteEn: The great unity of the Chinese nation is the premise and foundation for comprehensively advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 中华民族大团结是以中国式现代化全面推进中华民族伟大复兴的前提和基础。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: cast firm the consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A slogan made the mainline of the Party's ethnic work under Xi Jinping. It stresses a shared national identity that takes priority over the identities of individual ethnic groups.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for the Party's model of national development, presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, usually targeted for 2049.

t: The holistic reconstruction of ecological civilization in the age of artificial intelligence
zh: 人工智能时代的生态文明整体性重构
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences), 2026 no. 1
paras: Li Juan asks what happens to ecological civilization when artificial intelligence stops being a mere tool and becomes a structural force. Existing research, the author says, mostly stresses technological empowerment and digital transformation of ecological governance. Li argues instead that AI, especially strong AI, acts as a quasi-subject, turning the human–nature relationship into a three-way structure of human, intelligent agent and nature. Ecological civilization therefore needs its basic structure re-examined, not just a technical upgrade.

The article, from a historical-materialist standpoint, first sets out the debate on whether AI has subjectivity, then argues for its quasi-subject status at the ontological, cognitive and practical levels. It then examines five areas of reconstruction: the goals and training of AI; technological ethics and ecological justice; AI hallucination and decision-making; hidden energy consumption; and the public's ecological awareness, ecological culture and environmental participation. It draws on Marx and Engels, and on Western writers such as Kate Crawford, Virginia Dignum and Lewis Mumford.

Li's core move is that AI learns from natural data, analyses connections among natural information, and adjusts its effects on nature toward set goals. This makes AI a new active element in ecosystems, though one whose abilities are bounded by human design. Li therefore calls for ecological goals to be built into all AI systems, with measurable indicators for value alignment. The author warns of algorithmic bias that marginalises fragile regions and endangered species, of hallucinations that distort environmental decisions, and of systemic high energy use. Li proposes data representativeness, bias correction, expert verification, accountability chains and full life-cycle environmental disclosure in response.

On the public side, Li calls for higher environmental literacy that reads "data nature" critically, for AI-assisted green lifestyles, and for the modern transformation of traditional Chinese ecological culture. Li also proposes recognising both explicit expression and implicit behavioural data as forms of participation, which the author links to whole-process people's democracy. Li concludes that AI's reconstruction of ecological civilization does not diminish humans, who remain the ultimate responsible subjects and must keep the quasi-subject within technological ethics and a framework of green AI governance. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist account of AI as an ecological actor, with concrete governance proposals on bias, hallucination and energy use.
quoteEn: As the ultimate responsible subject, humanity must understand AI's practical characteristics deeply and use them well, keeping this emerging "quasi-subject" within the bounds of technological ethics and building an AI governance framework oriented to green development.
quoteZh: 人类作为终极责任主体，必须深刻认识和善于运用人工智能的实践特性，引导这种新兴的“拟主体”始终保持在技术伦理规范的轨道上，建构面向绿色发展的人工智能治理框架。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official and theoretical concept for a form of civilization that balances human development with the protection of nature. It has been part of Party doctrine since the 2000s and appears in the Party constitution and state constitution.
The author's term for AI as an entity that is not a living, conscious subject but behaves in subject-like ways, such as learning, adapting and generating content.
An official concept, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, describing Chinese democracy as covering every stage of decision-making and not only elections.
A term from AI ethics for ensuring that AI systems pursue goals consistent with human intentions and values.

t: The Chinese nation's tradition of great unification thought and its modern development
zh: 中华民族大一统思想传统与现代发展
source: Journal of Peking University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2026 no. 1
paras: Zhu Hanmin asks how the tradition of "great unification" (da yitong) arose in Chinese thought and how it carries on in the present. The article argues that this tradition is a pluralistic-yet-unified body of ideas. It took shape among the pre-Qin philosophers, was fixed in the Western Han, and has been continued and developed in Xi Jinping's cultural thought. Zhu proposes reading that thought through the continuity and development of Chinese civilization.

The first half looks at the Spring and Autumn and Warring States thinkers, the classifications of them by Sima Tan and Ban Gu, and the Gongyang commentary's use of the term "great unification". It then turns to Dong Zhongshu's synthesis in the Han. The second half moves to the modern period: Liang Qichao's 1902 concept of the "Chinese nation", Sun Yat-sen's "five-race republic" and the failed attempts to rebuild unity. It ends with the People's Republic and Xi Jinping's statements on modern governance, national community consciousness and modern Chinese civilization.

Zhu's central claim is that the philosophers' pluralism did not split Chinese civilization. In Zhu's account, the schools shared an origin in Three Dynasties civilization, and each hoped to unify the realm in its own way: Confucian "unity", Mohist "agreeing with the superior", Legalist centralised law, Daoist unity in the "Way". Dong Zhongshu then absorbed Mohist, Legalist, Huang-Lao Daoist and Yin-Yang ideas into a Confucian-centred system joined to centralised rule. Zhu adds that the ideal of "following the ways of antiquity" let the tradition change form with circumstances, and that it parallels the formation of a many-in-one Chinese nation, citing Fei Xiaotong.

Zhu concludes that the PRC's system inherits this tradition while drawing on modern institutional achievements. The article names the single-state form, regional ethnic autonomy and the people's congress system. Citing Xi Jinping, Zhu presents Chinese modernization, the forging of a strong sense of community among the Chinese nation, and the Second Integration (of Marxism with traditional culture) as continuations of great unification. Zhu holds that unity and diversity are dialectically linked in modern Chinese civilization. Read the original if you want a Chinese intellectual-historical account of how the idea of great unification is tied to current official theory on national unity and civilization.
quoteEn: The dialectical unity of great unification and plurality in Chinese civilization is precisely a salient feature of the civilizational form of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 中华文明的大一统与多元性的辩证统一，恰恰也是中国式现代化文明形态的突出特征。

glossary.explanation: A term first found in the Gongyang commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals. It came to mean political, cultural and intellectual unity of the realm under one authority.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, ideology and civilization, formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought.
The official name for China's development path, said to combine universal features of modernization with Chinese conditions.
Xi Jinping's formulation, put forward in 2023, of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture.

glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept stressing that all 56 ethnic groups belong to one Chinese nation. Party documents call for "forging" (zhulao) it.

t: Chinese modernization and Africa's path of development
zh: 中国式现代化和非洲发展之路
paras: Xu Xiuli and Li Xiaoyun ask why most African states have struggled to modernize since independence and what Chinese modernization can offer them. Opening with Xi Jinping's remark that there can be no global modernization without that of China and Africa, the authors argue that Africa's difficulties come down to the choice of development concept and path. In their view modernization does not mean Westernization, and China's experience is drawing growing attention in Africa.

The piece begins with data on Africa's mixed record this century. It cites Ethiopia's 10.3% average growth in 2004–2019, Rwanda's fall in poverty and rising intra-African trade. Against these it sets sub-Saharan poverty of around 45%, life expectancy of about 62.5 years and hunger affecting over 20% of Africans in 2024. The authors then identify three challenges, sketch China's trajectory, and draw three lessons for Africa from their nearly twenty years of grassroots cooperation in Tanzania.

The three challenges are as follows. First, colonialism cut off indigenous development, imposing monocrop economies and a dual structure of commercial and smallholder sectors that later reappeared as 'comparative advantage' and locked countries into the low end of value chains. Second, colonial legacies left political, economic and social structures out of step, so that elites diverged and donor projects fragmented villages into separate 'project units'. Third, agendas, funding and institutions came from outside, which the authors say pushed some states into neoliberal reforms. They contrast this with China, where Communist Party leadership, independence and self-reliance, five-year plans and an opening-up guided by the principle of serving China's own needs turned outside resources into domestic capability.

The authors propose three lessons: secure development autonomy, with foundational industry and infrastructure, stable public finances and the African Continental Free Trade Area; strengthen strategic coordination, with employment and industrial policy, cross-departmental mechanisms and policy feedback; and achieve 'creative transformation' by designing cooperation so that it builds local capacity and sustainable financing. They stress that Africa should not copy any model but draw on others to form its own. They add that Chinese modernization offers experience to countries that want faster development while keeping their independence, and that the 70th anniversary of China–Africa diplomatic relations opens new space for the Global South. Read the original if you want an official-journal view of how Chinese scholars present Chinese modernization as a reference for African development.
quoteEn: Africa's modernization predicament ultimately comes down to a question of development concepts and the choice of path.
quoteZh: 非洲现代化的困境归根到底是发展理念与路径选择的问题。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as an alternative to the Western model.
China's medium-term national development plans, issued since the 1950s, which set economic and social goals for each five-year period.
A term for developing countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse uses to frame solidarity and shared development interests.
A long-standing principle of Chinese Communist Party policy, stressing that development should rest on the country's own strength and decisions rather than on dependence on outside powers.

t: The rich connotations and theoretical contributions of humanistic economics in the new era
zh: 新时代人文经济学的丰富内涵和理论贡献
paras: Sang Mingxu asks how countries pursuing modernization should handle the relationship between economy and culture, and between material and spiritual life. The article argues that humanistic economics in the new era, a proposition Xi Jinping raised in 2023 using the Suzhou–Hangzhou region as an example, deepens understanding of how economic development and cultural construction interact. In Sang's account it offers scientific guidance for coordinating material and spiritual civilization within Chinese modernization.

Published in Qiushi, the piece has three parts. The first sets out the historical and global background: the Western path to modernization and mainstream economics, the Party's approach since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and present global development difficulties. The second explains the content of humanistic economics through five themes: the human being, material and spiritual civilization, culture's effect on the economy, the cultural industry, and the discipline's "humanistic return". The third turns to tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Sang contends that Western modernization is a capital-centred modernization of things, and that mainstream economics, built on the "rational economic man", loses sight of people and cannot explain polarisation, ecological crisis or spiritual poverty. Humanistic economics, described as a product of Xi Jinping's economic thought and cultural thought and an innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, puts people at the centre and treats growth as a means, not an end. It is said to resolve the "humanistic paradox" of development by combining material abundance with spiritual richness. Sang also holds that culture supports high-quality development, citing the cultural industry's 2024 value added of 6.2094 trillion yuan, or 4.61% of GDP.

Sang concludes that research in this field is still at an early stage. The author calls for a self-reliant body of knowledge built on Marxist standpoint and method, on traditional Chinese culture and on case studies of Chinese modernization. In practice, Sang proposes putting the people first, giving more weight to spiritual and cultural needs, integrating culture with technology, and developing cultural industries and culture-tourism integration through an effective market and an enabling government. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official theory of humanistic economics is framed and what research and policy agenda it sets for the coming five-year period.
quoteEn: The most distinctive feature of humanistic economics in the new era is its adherence to the people-centred development philosophy: it puts "the human being" at the core of development and stresses that economic development is itself a means, not an end, with people's free and all-round development as its ultimate aim, which will surely give strong impetus to the "humanistic return" of economics.
quoteZh: 新时代人文经济学最鲜明的特征就是坚持以人民为中心的发展思想，将“人”置于发展的核心位置，强调经济发展本身是手段而不是目的，人的自由全面发展才是经济发展的最终追求，这必将有力推动经济学的“人文回归”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from the Western model.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing project of combining Marxist theory with Chinese conditions and contemporary demands.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to efficiency, innovation and balance.
A theoretical proposition tied to Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on culturally developed regions with strong economies. It concerns the mutual reinforcement of culture and economic development.

glossary.zh: 物质文明和精神文明相协调
glossary.pinyin: wùzhì wénmíng hé jīngshén wénmíng xiāngxiétiáo
glossary.literal: material civilization and spiritual civilization coordinated
glossary.explanation: A long-standing official pairing, in which economic prosperity and cultural-ethical development are meant to advance together.

t: The generative logic of signature concepts
zh: 标识性概念的生成逻辑
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 9 March 2026, asks how the "signature concepts" (标识性概念) called for in building an autonomous Chinese system of philosophy and social science are actually produced.
