Wen Xueping argues that such concepts cannot be conjured by will or imagination. They have an objective generative logic, which the article sets out in four steps. The starting point is Xi Jinping's call to refine signature concepts and create new categories and formulations that the international community can readily understand and accept.

The article opens by situating concepts within the theory of knowledge, then proceeds through four headed sections. These deal with the multiple elements that combine to form signature concepts, the refinement of concepts as a "revolution in terminology", the role of answering new questions of the era as the driving force of thought, and the Two Integrations as the basic guide. Wen draws on Engels, Marx, Hegel's distinction between abstract and concrete concepts, and Xi Jinping's formulations throughout.

Wen first argues that a concept arises from three elements: a sign, a thought and a referent. A signature concept is also the trunk of a knowledge system, one that supports and shapes it and condenses propositions, principles, data and auxiliary concepts. Second, citing Engels, Wen holds that a new term matters only when it accompanies original theory. Smith, Ricardo and the Physiocrats renamed the price of production without a terminological revolution, because only Marx's labour theory of value and theory of surplus value clarified its difference from value. Such a revolution combines critique and construction, and the signature concept is the result of research, not its starting point. Third, concepts answer genuine problems of the age. Wen distinguishes real from false problems and "universal" or "principal" problems from those without intellectual content, and treats Xi's questions of China, the world, the people and the times as the former.

Wen concludes that the Two Integrations supply the essential guidance, because concrete practice, theoretical guidance and traditional resources form the three-dimensional space of reasons for any concept. Following Marx's path from the sensuous concrete through abstraction to the "concrete in thought", the author argues that signature concepts are not low-level abstract concepts but concrete concepts that synthesise many determinations, and that this form already embodies the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese academic commentary links Xi Jinping's call for an autonomous knowledge system to Marxist epistemology and Hegelian logic.
quoteEn: The establishment of a signature concept is not the starting point of research but its result.
quoteZh: 标识性概念的确立不是研究工作的起点，而是研究工作的结果。

glossary.explanation: A term in Xi Jinping's discourse on building China's knowledge system. It refers to core concepts that mark a discipline's original theory and are meant to be recognisable internationally.
Xi Jinping's formula for a Chinese system of philosophy and social science built on its own concepts and theories, instead of relying on Western frameworks.
Official formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It has been prominent in Party theory since 2021–2023.
Phrase drawn from Engels's preface to the English edition of Capital, Volume I. The article uses it to argue that new scientific insights transform a discipline's technical vocabulary.

t: Identifying concepts of an autonomous knowledge system
zh: 自主知识体系的标识性概念
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 9 March 2026, Sun Zhengyu asks what makes a knowledge system "autonomous" and answers that its autonomy is marked by its "identifying concepts" (标识性概念). Sun argues that such concepts are more than original terms with new intellectual, epochal and civilizational content. They are the explanatory principle that builds the system, the "universal light" that illuminates it and the "living soul" that drives its development. Distilling them is, in Sun's view, the soul of accelerating the construction of China's autonomous system of philosophy and social sciences.

The piece is organised in three parts, one for each of these three roles. Sun draws mainly on Marx, taking "practice" in Marxist philosophy and "capital" in Capital as two model cases. Sun then turns to post-reform-era Chinese philosophy, and finally to "Chinese modernization" as the identifying concept of China's current autonomous knowledge system.

Sun's central move is that a knowledge system is a logically organised system of concepts, and its subjectivity and originality depend on the basic idea and explanatory principle behind the whole conceptual framework. In Sun's reading, Marx used "practice" to criticise all earlier materialism and idealism and to shift philosophy from interpreting the world to changing it. Marx used "capital" to reveal human relations behind the "fantastic form" of relations between things, and this lit up the whole of Capital. Drawing on Hegel, Sun holds that a genuinely autonomous system unites the "freedom of the whole" with the "necessity of its moments", so that every subordinate concept carries the principle of the identifying concept. Sun adds that such a concept must be produced by turning names into concepts, lists into generalisations, narration into argument and explanation into thought.

Sun says that since reform and opening up, "practice" has served Chinese philosophy as such a concept: it reframed the history of philosophy, the subject–object relation, and the response to major real-world problems. Sun names "Chinese modernization" as the identifying concept of China's autonomous system, covering the new development philosophy, a new view of civilization, a new worldview built on a community with a shared future for mankind, and the Four-sphere Confidence. Sun concludes that only by treating Chinese modernization as the "universal light" and "living soul" of every discipline can a vigorous, original system be built. Read the original if you want a short Chinese statement of how Marxist philosophy is used to justify the search for core concepts in the autonomous knowledge system project.
quoteEn: The "soul" of accelerating the construction of China's autonomous knowledge system of philosophy and social sciences is to distil its "identifying concepts".
quoteZh: 加快构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系，其“灵魂”是提炼出“标识性概念”。

glossary.explanation: A slogan in current Chinese policy and academic discourse, calling for Chinese philosophy and social sciences to develop their own concepts, theories and discourse rather than relying on Western frameworks.
In Sun's usage, original concepts that mark out a knowledge system and condense its basic idea and explanatory principle.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official formula of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, promoted by China since 2012–13.
Official formula of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Using the third historical resolution as the guide for high-quality use of red resources
zh: 以第三个历史决议为遵循高质量用好红色资源
source: Studies on Mao Zedong Thought, 2025 no. 5
paras: Zhou Yun asks how the protection, development and use of "red resources" (revolutionary museums, memorials, Party history halls, martyrs' memorial sites and former revolutionary sites) can be done well. The article argues that the Party's third historical resolution, adopted in 2021, should be the main benchmark. In Zhou's view, this is the way to keep such work politically correct and historically accurate.

The article begins from the Regulations on Party History Study and Education, which call for studying the three historical resolutions and the leaders' statements on Party history. It briefly summarises the contents of the 2021 resolution: periodisation, tasks, achievements, historical significance, experience, guiding thought and the great founding spirit. It then sets out three reasons the resolution matters, surveys five shortcomings in current practice, and ends with proposals. It cites Ministry of Culture and Tourism figures of 283 million red-tourism visits in 2023, with revenue of 77.759 billion yuan.

Zhou presents the resolution as the authoritative reference for narrating and evaluating major events and figures, and as a tool against historical nihilism. It also broadens the content of red resources and needs to be publicised through them. The author finds that many sites have not yet adopted the resolution's four-period division of Party history, its emphasis on the great founding spirit, or its summary of achievements and experience. Some sites are also said to commercialise or trivialise history for profit, and others contain factual errors, misplaced scenes or evaluations that depart from the resolution.

Zhou calls for red resources to treat education as their core value and to follow the resolution strictly in exhibitions and guided tours, which the author calls an "iron discipline". Displays should centre on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the Party's leading role, be reorganised into the four historical periods, and give much more space to the new era, including poverty alleviation and ecological civilization. They should also present the major achievements, the "ten adherences" of experience, and the great founding spirit and the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage. Read the original if you want to see how Party-history doctrine is translated into concrete rules for museums, memorial sites and red tourism.
quoteEn: This should become an iron discipline in the development and use of red resources.
quoteZh: 这应该成为红色资源开发利用的铁的纪律。

glossary.explanation: A collective term for sites, relics and memorial institutions tied to the history of the Communist Party and its revolution, such as museums, former headquarters and martyrs' memorials. They are used for education and for "red tourism".
Official Party resolutions that assess Party history. The third was adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in November 2021, following those of 1945 and 1981.
In official discourse, a label for views that question or negate the Party's official account of its history and of revolutionary figures.
A formulation, set out officially in 2021, of the values attributed to the Party's founders. It is treated as the source of the Chinese Communists' "spiritual lineage".

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing. The 2021 resolution presents it as the theme of the Party's century of struggle.

t: Autonomous modernization of the Global South: meaning, logic and development path
zh: 全球南方自主现代化：内涵、逻辑与发展路向
paras: Tian Wei asks how the Global South can escape dependence on Western modernization and build its own path, and why that path must be "autonomous". The article argues that existing scholarship on Global South modernization (classical modernization, dependency, world-systems and latecomer-advantage theories) mostly criticises the West. In Tian's account, it neglects the South's own agency and has not produced a self-constructed discourse. Tian proposes a theory of autonomous modernization that would move the South from being theorised by others to theorising itself.

The article first reviews the literature and its limits. It then defines autonomous modernization and treats the Global South in three dimensions: as an economic, a political and a cultural category. It next sets out the internal logic of autonomous modernization in five pairs: lawfulness and purposiveness, diachronic and synchronic, autonomy and commonality. The final sections discuss multilateralism, a shared theoretical narrative, and a "new form" of world modernization. A closing section places Chinese modernization within this framework.

Tian defines autonomous modernization as modernization that fits national conditions, balances universality with difference and independence with inclusiveness, and builds its own discursive power. Drawing on Marx's analysis of capital, the author traces the North–South divide to the capitalist mode of production. Tian holds that neoliberalism, debt and premature deindustrialisation deepened dependence, and that decolonisation turned the South into a political category of collective resistance. The cultural category rests on a shared identity of the marginalised. Tian argues that the South has moved from being forced into Western modernization, to criticising it, to shaping its own. It should pursue strategic autonomy and avoid both wholesale Westernisation and closed-door exclusion of the West.

Tian concludes that there is no genuine world modernization without Global South modernization, and that the South must unite development with autonomy through multilateralism. Proposals include strengthening BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, the Belt and Road Initiative and the "G77 plus China" format, plus a Global South research centre. They also include a joint theoretical narrative that rejects capital-centred, polarising and expansionist modernization. China, as a Global South member, is said to offer new models through Chinese modernization and the four global initiatives. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar builds a theory of Global South modernization and links it to Chinese foreign policy.
quoteEn: Autonomous modernization of the Global South is modernization that fits its own national conditions, balances universality with difference and independence with inclusiveness, and follows a path of independent development.
quoteZh: 全球南方自主现代化是符合自身国情、兼顾普遍性与差异性、兼顾独立性和包容性、走独立自主发展道路的现代化

glossary.explanation: A term for developing countries, often those with a shared history of colonialism and a marginal place in the world economy. Chinese official discourse uses it widely and counts China as a member.
The official name for China's path of development under Party leadership, presented since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as an alternative to Western modernization.
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013 and linking Asia, Africa and Europe.
Four Chinese proposals on global development, security, civilisation and governance, presented by Xi Jinping as contributions to international cooperation.

t: On the divergence of digital governance under capitalism and socialism
zh: 论资本主义与社会主义两种制度下数字治理的分野
paras: Wei Shiguo asks whether the present split between "Chinese governance" and "Western disorder" in the digital field is a passing difference in policy or the product of two fundamentally different historical logics. The article argues for the second answer. In Wei's account, digital capitalism arose as a crisis-driven rescue plan for capitalism after 2008 and is heading towards extraction, monopoly and alienation. China's socialist digital governance, by contrast, is presented as a conscious adjustment of the relations of production to new productive forces.

Wei says existing scholarship either criticises Western digital capitalism at the level of phenomena (surveillance business models, antitrust remedies) or lists the strengths of Chinese digital governance, and lacks a unified Marxist comparative framework. The article first sets out a historical-materialist framework in which data and digital platforms are the key means of production, with "data reification" and "data fetishism" as updates of Marx's commodity fetishism. It then analyses digital capitalism, drawing on Shoshana Zuboff, Nick Srnicek and Yanis Varoufakis, and illustrates it with the Google and EU Digital Markets Act cases, Cambridge Analytica and the gig economy. It then turns to China's institutional practice and closes with a comparative table.

Wei's central move is to treat ownership and control of data and platforms as the decisive question. Under digital capitalism, private capital monopolises them, and network effects leave the state a passive, belated regulator. Wei cites the 2024 US ruling against Google, whose remedies were later limited, and the EU's fines on Apple and Meta, which Wei calls small relative to global revenue. For China, the article cites the National Data Administration (2023), public data authorised operation (such as Beijing's financial data zone) and the digital yuan (e-CNY) as a mutually supporting system. Wei contrasts "the logic of capital" with "the logic of the people" across five dimensions: core logic, data ownership, institutional actors, value realisation and systemic consequences.

Wei concludes that the digital-field divergence reflects the logic of the people sublating (surpassing) the logic of capital. The article defines a "new form of socialist digital civilization" by three features: a public-led, public-ownership-based set of production relations, a shift in value goal from extracting profit to creating social value, and governance that moves beyond the state–market opposition. Wei adds that China's exploration offers Global South countries a way to avoid becoming "data colonies". Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar frames a capital-versus-people comparison of digital governance, including the specific cases and policy documents it uses.
quoteEn: This shows that once private capital has built up "digital sovereignty", the state's attempts to regain some control through elaborate bureaucratic procedures have lost much of their effect and force, and this is precisely a portrait of the failure of Western digital governance.
quoteZh: 这说明，在私人资本已经构建起“数字主权”之后，国家权力试图运用繁复的官僚程序来夺回部分的控制权，其效果和力度已经大打折扣，而这恰恰就是西方数字治理失灵的一个写照。

glossary.explanation: The author's counterpart to "the logic of capital": a development logic oriented to the public interest, common prosperity and the all-round development of the person.
A Chinese state body established in October 2023 to coordinate data infrastructure, data property rights, circulation and digital planning.

A mechanism in which government-held public data is made available under authorisation to enterprises and institutions for use, under security controls. Local governments in China have piloted various forms.
China's central bank digital currency, in pilot use in a number of provinces. The article treats it as a tool of monetary sovereignty and public payment infrastructure.
A term for developing countries, widely used in Chinese official discourse to denote China's partners.

t: The scientific content, value and means of promoting the correct view of the history of the Second World War
zh: 论正确二战史观的科学内涵、价值意蕴与弘扬路径
paras: Eighty years after the end of the Second World War, Ma and Zhang argue, some states use narratives of the war as a political tool of hegemonism, distorting the history that underlies the post-war international order. The article sets out what it calls the correct view of the history of the Second World War, a formulation it traces to Xi Jinping's statements and to the May 2024 China–Russia joint statement. Its thesis is that this view is scientifically grounded in historical materialism, has concrete political and normative value, and should be actively promoted through historical scholarship, international exchange and digital communication.

The article is organised in four parts. It first sets out the scientific content of the view, built on three principles: objectivity, the people as the subject of history, and systematic or holistic method. It then lists the erroneous views it rejects: Western-centrism, historical nihilism and historical revisionism. Next it discusses the view's value for the international order and for global governance. It ends with three practical paths of promotion: a fact-based narrative system, multi-level international exchange platforms, and digital communication.

The authors argue that the correct view answers each erroneous view in turn. Western-centrist accounts, they say, sideline the Chinese and Soviet theatres. The authors counter with figures such as over 35 million Chinese and over 27 million Soviet casualties, and the claim that over 77.5% of German and allied forces were consumed on the Soviet–German front. Nihilist claims, such as that the Chinese Communist Party fought only evasively, are rejected as undermining the justice of the victory and the Party's legitimacy. Revisionist claims, such as the 'Japan as victim' thesis and denial of the Nanjing Massacre, are described as dissolving responsibility for aggression. The authors further hold that the correct view supports the United Nations system and the Global Governance Initiative, which they contrast with the failed Versailles–Washington system.

Ma and Zhang conclude that the view should build a historical consensus: oppose war and cherish peace, those who love war will perish while justice prevails, and seek common ground while shelving differences. They call for cross-checked archival evidence, interdisciplinary and global research paradigms, and narratives that include civilian memory. They also propose using the United Nations, UNESCO, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, BRICS, academic bodies and civil groups, plus short video, immersive technology and flagship media, to counter deepfake and algorithm-driven distortions. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese scholars link Second World War memory to current diplomacy and global governance and to communication strategy.
quoteEn: By restoring the record of fascism's crimes of aggression, the correct view of Second World War history guides countries to build a firm historical consensus of 'opposing war and cherishing peace'.
quoteZh: 正确二战史观通过还原法西斯主义的侵略罪行，引导世界各国筑牢“反对战争、珍爱和平”的历史共识。

glossary.en: the correct view of the history of the Second World War
glossary.literal: correct Second World War historical outlook
glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted by Xi Jinping and in the May 2024 China–Russia joint statement. It stresses the roles of China and the Soviet Union and defence of the post-war order, in contrast to Western-centrist, nihilist and revisionist accounts.
In Chinese official discourse, a label for interpretations seen as denying or distorting established historical conclusions, especially about the Party and revolutionary history.

A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2025, presented as a call for sovereign equality, multilateralism and a more just and reasonable global governance system. The article counts it among the 'four global initiatives'.

t: Constructing the false legitimacy of ideology: how American cultural hegemony is built, and its crisis
zh: 建构意识形态的虚假正当性：美国文化霸权的建构方式及其危机
paras: Ye Rurong asks how the United States has built a "false legitimacy" for its ideology, which epistemological traps keep reproducing it, and how current "America First" policies erode it. The article argues that US cultural hegemony rests on a carefully constructed false legitimacy. In Ye's account, that legitimacy is now unravelling under the pressure of systemic capitalist crisis and a shifting global balance of power.

The article draws on Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony, supplemented by Raymond Williams, David Harvey, John B. Thompson, Edward Said and Samuel Huntington. It begins by clarifying the concept of legitimacy and argues that the Chinese "zhengdangxing" (legitimacy in a moral sense) renders "legitimacy" better than "hefaxing" (legality). It then examines how the US constructs this legitimacy, through liberal ideology, consumer culture and asymmetric media communication. Next it turns to the cognitive traps involved, and finally to the erosion of legitimacy in the Trump era.

Ye identifies three traps. The first is an illusion of "identical" interests, in which the particular interests of the hegemon and of property owners are presented as shared by subordinate groups and countries. The second is "value-neutral" discourse, produced by a new stratum of "organic intellectuals" (media, public relations and cultural workers), which hides the politics behind culture. The third is a false universality, in which "universal values" are said to be Western capitalist ideology repackaged. Ye then argues that as US material strength declines, Washington has shifted from leadership by consent to "non-legitimate" domination. It has moved from "identical interests" to "America First", from depoliticisation to "pan-politicisation" (cultural decoupling, visa limits, platform restrictions, technology blockades), and from universal values to "American exceptionalism", shown in tariffs and withdrawals from international agreements.

Ye concludes that these shifts have not rescued US hegemony. In the article's view they have accelerated the collapse of its false legitimacy and produced a structural crisis of cultural hegemony. The author suggests this ends the long Western monopoly on global discourse and offers China a window to step outside Western-set frameworks and build its own autonomous discourse system. Read the original if you want a Gramscian, China-based critique of US soft power and "universal values" that ties cultural hegemony to Trump-era policy.
quoteEn: By constructing the false legitimacy of liberal ideology, the United States has achieved its hegemonic position in culture.
quoteZh: 美国通过建构自由主义意识形态的虚假正当性，实现了其在文化上的霸权地位。

glossary.explanation: Gramsci's idea that ruling classes or states secure domination through consent, by shaping values, education and media, rather than through force alone.
The article uses this term for "legitimacy" in the sense of moral and social acceptance of authority. It distinguishes it from "hefaxing" (legality).
A Gramscian concept for intellectuals who emerge from and articulate the worldview of a particular class. The article applies it to US media, PR and cultural workers.
Values such as freedom and democracy presented as valid for all societies. Chinese official discourse often criticises the term as a cover for Western ideology.
The slogan of US foreign and economic policy, prominently associated with Donald Trump, which prioritises US national interests.
The belief that the US is unique and holds a special role in the world. The article presents it as a doctrine placing the US above international rules.

t: Maritime frontier governance and the evolution of the sense of community of the Chinese nation
zh: 海疆治理与中华民族共同体意识演进
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2026, asks how governance of China's maritime frontier relates to the development of the sense of community of the Chinese nation. Lin and Xia note that existing work on frontier governance and national community consciousness mostly starts from land borders. They argue that maritime governance and the evolution of that consciousness have been closely linked and have reinforced each other throughout history.

The article follows three historical stages. It covers dynastic governance of the coast from the pre-Qin period to the early Qing, the maritime crisis from the Opium War of 1840 through the War of Resistance against Japan, and maritime construction since 1949, including the new era.

Lin and Xia contend that in imperial times, administrative control of the coast, maritime trade and migration encouraged integration between coastal and inland peoples, and that this made the early forms of a shared consciousness appear. In their account the modern crisis, marked by unequal treaties and naval defeats, awakened that consciousness as coastal and inland peoples united against foreign aggression, moving the Chinese nation from a state of being 'in itself' to one of self-awareness. Since 1949 they cite the creation of the People's Navy, the establishment of Sansha City, the strategy of 'strengthening the country through the sea', the Belt and Road Initiative, and advances in marine technology as having strengthened coastal–inland ties and the identification of overseas Chinese with the homeland.

The authors conclude that maritime governance supplies the practical basis for the sense of community of the Chinese nation, while that sense gives maritime governance spiritual motivation. They hold that it also makes people more conscious in defending national unity and territorial integrity and in building a maritime power. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese scholarship is extending frontier-studies themes from land borders to the sea.
quoteEn: Maritime governance has provided the practical foundation and real-world support for the development of the sense of community of the Chinese nation, while that sense has in turn infused maritime governance with powerful spiritual impetus and ideological assurance.
quoteZh: 海疆治理为中华民族共同体意识的发展提供了实践基础和现实支撑，而中华民族共同体意识则为海疆治理注入了强大的精神动力和思想保障。

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A key concept in Party ethnic policy, which stresses that all ethnic groups belong to one national community. Official texts speak of 'forging a strong sense' (铸牢) of it.
The administration and management of China's land and maritime border regions, treated in Chinese scholarship as an academic field and a policy area.
A national goal, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), of developing China's marine economy, naval strength, technology and maritime rights.
A programme of infrastructure and economic cooperation launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, including a maritime Silk Road.

keywords: sense of community of the Chinese nation

t: Intelligent computing as an aid to building China's independent knowledge system
zh: 智能计算助力构建中国自主的知识体系
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 4 February 2026
paras: Tong Dezhi takes up a task the Party has set for philosophy and the social sciences: building an independent knowledge system. Citing Xi Jinping's 2022 remarks and the recommendations on the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), Tong argues that existing research remains mostly theoretical and that the task is hard. The article's thesis is that intelligent computing, meaning big data and artificial intelligence, is the most scientific and feasible way to carry it out.

The short commentary first explains the difficulty. China's knowledge system grew over some 5,000 years and has absorbed Western learning since modern times, so the task is not one of building from nothing. It then sets out four ways intelligent computing can help: systematising the Party's innovative theory, identifying signature concepts, integrating original theories, and organising human–machine collaboration.

Tong holds that the system rests on a vast body of literature, citing 10 million copyright registrations in 2024 and over 60,000 CSSCI papers a year. Only computational methods can sift this body to extract signature concepts and original theories. Tong contends that concept identification has so far relied on subjective judgement, which produced misreadings and ambiguity. Bibliometrics and large language models could define concepts from the literature instead. Knowledge graphs and clustering could then move from concepts and practical propositions to theory, and help track and forecast change in the system.

Tong also names risks: models avoid sensitive topics, and they fabricate sources and data ("AI hallucination"). Tong proposes knowledge bases, prompt design and ethical alignment as remedies, and stresses that Chinese scholars, not models, remain the builders of the system. Tong concludes that, with rapidly advancing AI, the project is no longer an "impossible task". Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics link AI methods to the Party's knowledge-system agenda.
quoteEn: Traditionally, the signature concepts of Chinese philosophy and social sciences have been identified mostly through researchers' subjective judgement.
quoteZh: 传统上，中国哲学社会科学的标识性概念更多依靠研究者的主观判断来识别。

glossary.explanation: A slogan of Xi Jinping-era policy, stressed from 2022, calling for Chinese philosophy and social sciences to rest on their own disciplines, scholarship and discourse rather than on Western frameworks.
Distinctive concepts, often coined in China, that are meant to represent Chinese scholarship and theory internationally.
Official term for the Party's latest theoretical achievements, centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
Computing based on big data, artificial intelligence and large language models, used here as a research method for the humanities and social sciences.

t: Using AI to study AI: the intelligent turn in social science research
zh: 以AI研究AI：社会科学研究的智能化转向
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in February 2026, asks how artificial intelligence is changing social science and what direction China should take. Meng Tianguang argues that AI is driving a new research paradigm, "AI for Science" (AI4S), and that its application to the social sciences (AI4SS) opens a path of paradigm innovation in which AI is both the object of study and the method of study.

The piece begins with the shift from AI4S to AI4SS and cites a State Council opinion on the "AI Plus" initiative that calls for human-machine collaboration in philosophy and social science research. It then sets out what "using AI to study AI" means for measurement, inference and prediction. A third section surveys efforts in the United States, the EU, Japan, the UK, Canada and Germany, and the final section proposes a Chinese approach in four areas: research infrastructure, discipline building, talent training and academic ecology.

Meng's central claim is that large language models change each stage of research, from problem finding to data analysis. For measurement, they classify text through natural-language instructions without large labelled datasets. For inference, they allow "silicon samples", simulated respondents with set social attributes, which can ease the time, cost and scale limits of surveys and experiments. For prediction, multi-agent simulation may capture the complexity of social evolution. Meng sees three combinations of theory-driven, data-driven and model-driven paradigms, ending in intelligent automation of the whole research process. Globally, Meng notes tensions over black-box algorithms, data openness versus privacy, and the gap between the speed of innovation and governance capacity.

Meng argues that China has particular advantages: large-scale behavioural data, an institutional capacity to concentrate resources, domestic open-source large models and rich governance settings. The author calls for a national AI4SS research platform, interdisciplinary programmes, "social science + data science + AI ethics" talent, ethics guidelines for silicon samples and generated outputs, and incentives for open code and models, so as to build China's own system of knowledge. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented overview of how a Chinese computational social scientist frames AI-driven research methods and institutional priorities.
quoteEn: "Using AI to study AI" stresses that in the social sciences artificial intelligence has the dual character of being both an object of research and a research method.
quoteZh: “以AI研究AI”强调人工智能在社会科学中同时具有研究对象与研究方法的双重属性。

glossary.explanation: A national initiative to integrate AI into the economy, society and research. The State Council issued an opinion on implementing it in depth, which the article cites.
Simulated respondents created by prompting a large language model to act as people with specified social attributes. They are used for pre-testing, experiment design and effect testing.
An official aim of building Chinese philosophy and social science with its own concepts and theories, rather than relying on Western frameworks.

t: Accelerating the building of national security capabilities in the field of artificial intelligence
zh: 加快人工智能领域国家安全能力建设
paras: Zhang Wei, a professor at Sichuan University, argues in this newspaper commentary that artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology reaching into economic management, public services and social governance, and that this changes what national security means and how it is achieved. Citing the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), Zhang contends that national security capabilities in AI must be built up quickly, with security requirements written into research, deployment and governance from the start.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the historical logic for the task, then turns to the technical foundations of such capabilities, and finally to the institutional safeguards needed to keep them running. It draws on Xi Jinping's statements and the holistic approach to national security.

Zhang's core argument is that security is shifting from passive defence against single events to continuous monitoring and forward-looking guidance. On the technical side, Zhang says controllability is not a brake on development but a structural capacity: mastery of core algorithms, computing power, data and basic software, with systems that are predictable, traceable and verifiable. On the institutional side, Zhang calls for clear boundaries among government oversight, corporate responsibility, industry self-discipline and public scrutiny, plus cross-department coordination and information-sharing. Zhang also proposes adaptive tools such as regulatory sandboxes, advance standard-setting and tiered compliance, which the author says do not lower the security baseline.

Zhang concludes that embedding security into the AI lifecycle will turn the technology's uncertainty into something governable and support the modernization of the national security system and capabilities in the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official-academic commentary frames AI governance as a national security task.
quoteEn: This institutional embedding does not mean starting from scratch; it forms stable interfaces within the existing governance system, so that AI security requirements keep operating in everyday decision-making, implementation and oversight, and gradually become a routine governance capacity.
quoteZh: 这种制度嵌入并非另起炉灶，而是在既有治理体系中形成稳定接口，使人工智能安全要求能够在日常决策、执行和监督过程中持续发挥作用，从而逐步转化为常态化的治理能力。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's security doctrine, introduced in 2014, which treats security as spanning politics, economy, technology, society and other fields, and stresses a systemic approach.

glossary.zh: 国家安全体系和能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā ānquán tǐxì hé nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization of the national security system and capabilities
glossary.explanation: A policy goal in Party documents of upgrading China's security institutions and capacities to meet new risks.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.
A regulatory approach in which new technologies are tested in a controlled, limited setting under supervisors' watch before wider rules are fixed.

t: New developments in the theory of state sovereignty in the digital age
zh: 数字时代国家主权理论的新演进
paras: This is a written expert roundtable published in Guangming Daily on 13 February 2026, hosted by two of the paper's reporters, Ji Wenya and Wang Jin. It asks how traditional state sovereignty has evolved into "cyber sovereignty" as networks, artificial intelligence and other technologies reshape international competition. The editors' note frames the topic through Xi Jinping's repeated calls to respect cyber sovereignty and to build a community with a shared future in cyberspace.

Four scholars take part: Huang Zhixiong (Wuhan University Law School), Han Na (People's Public Security University of China), Lu Chuanying (Tongji University) and Xu Yuan (Beijing Institute of Technology). The discussion has four parts: the definition of cyber sovereignty and its relation to traditional sovereignty; how new technologies enlarge its boundaries; the "glass house dilemma" in international governance; and the principle of respecting cyber sovereignty alongside the community with a shared future in cyberspace.

The speakers broadly treat cyber sovereignty as an extension of state sovereignty into cyberspace. Huang distinguishes it from territorial, maritime and air sovereignty by its mix of the physical and virtual, its layered character and its rapid evolution; Lu adds that it is dynamic, differentiated and balanced. On technology, the panel describes competition over computing power, algorithms and data, and the growing power of large technology firms. Huang cites trends of securitisation, bloc formation and weakened regulation, while Han and Xu discuss "algorithmic power" and the "digital walls" built through technical means. Huang's "glass house dilemma" holds that states, more dependent on networks, are both able to harm others and exposed themselves, so that Western powers now seek to reshape sovereignty and non-intervention rules. Panellists also say rules lag behind AI, and that a gap in capability separates developed from developing countries.

The panel concludes that cyber sovereignty does not mean closing off or splitting cyberspace. Huang argues that some states, citing the US treatment of TikTok as an example, misuse the concept, and that respecting cyber sovereignty (coexistence) and building a community with a shared future in cyberspace (cooperation) are dialectically united. Han and Lu present the community concept as a Chinese approach built on the four principles and five proposals for global internet governance, which they contrast with cyber hegemony and zero-sum thinking. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese legal and international-relations scholars define cyber sovereignty and frame AI-era cyberspace governance.
quoteEn: Cyber sovereignty is in essence the product of "grafting" the long-established principle of state sovereignty onto virtual cyberspace.
quoteZh: 网络主权本质上是历史久远的国家主权原则“嫁接”到虚拟网络空间的产物。

glossary.explanation: The idea that a state holds supreme authority within its borders and independence abroad over network infrastructure, actors, conduct and data. China promotes it in global internet governance, and a 2023 World Internet Conference document set out this definition.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future in cyberspace
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's proposal, an application of the broader idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, that states jointly govern cyberspace through cooperation. It is usually presented alongside respect for cyber sovereignty.
Huang Zhixiong's image of states that depend heavily on networks. Each can throw stones at others' glass houses but fears the same in return.

t: Theoretical leap and implementation paths of integrated urban–rural development
zh: 城乡融合发展的理论跃迁与实现路径
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2026, Cao Dongbo and Zhang Jinhua take up the 2026 No. 1 Central Document's call to give priority to agriculture and rural areas and to pursue integrated urban–rural development. They argue that the Party's understanding of the urban–rural relationship has deepened in step with practice, and that "integration" marks a theoretical advance over earlier concepts.

The short commentary opens with Marx, Engels and the Communist Manifesto on urban–rural relations. It then traces Party thinking from the worker–peasant alliance, through the urban–rural dual structure of the planned period, to reform-era shifts and the 19th Party Congress (2017) formulation. A second half sets out priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The authors say the shift from "coordination" to "integrated development" moved beyond managerial and spatial thinking, treating city and countryside as a complementary organic whole. They name three advances over the dual-economy model: ontological (the countryside as an equal pillar of modernization), methodological (two-way empowerment) and axiological (equivalent quality of life, with people's all-round development as the measure). For the 15th Five-Year Plan period they hold that the premise lies in cities, the foothold in the countryside, and the key in integration, with counties as the main link.

They conclude that integration is a necessary requirement of Chinese modernization and a basis of common prosperity. Their proposals include metropolitan-area planning, hukou and land reform, turning rural resources into assets, a unified construction-land market, equal public services based on resident population, and benefit-sharing between firms and farmers. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official line on urban–rural integration at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Thus urban–rural integration is no longer a "by-product" of economic transformation, but a necessary requirement of Chinese modernization and an important foundation for achieving common prosperity.
quoteZh: 由此，城乡融合不再是经济转型的“副产品”，而是中国式现代化的必然要求，是实现共同富裕的重要根基。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth, emphasised in Party policy under Xi Jinping.
A policy concept put forward at the 19th Party Congress (2017) that treats cities and villages as complementary parts of one whole, with free flow of factors between them.

t: Grasping the regular patterns behind expanding domestic demand
zh: 深刻把握扩大内需的规律性认识
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2026, asks what the Party's strategy of expanding domestic demand rests on and how it should be pursued in the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Mao argues that the strategy applies Marxist political economy to the actual conditions of China's economy. In the author's account, it has yielded a set of regular patterns that policy must grasp.

The piece opens by citing the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference and Xi Jinping's remarks since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then moves through six themes: balancing aggregate supply and demand, domestic demand as the leading force, consumption, investment, the four links of social reproduction, and institutional mechanisms.

Mao's central claim is that supply and demand stand in a dialectical relationship, each able to generate the other. The author contends that China's socialist economic system can overcome the capitalist contradiction between unlimited production and the limited paying demand of working people. Demand-side management should therefore be joined with supply-side structural reform. Consumption is described as the basis of growth and investment as the key factor, including investment in people as well as in things. Drawing on the Marxist account of production, distribution, exchange and consumption, Mao holds that production is the starting point and the dominant link. The success of the strategy therefore depends ultimately on the level of production, while income distribution, circulation systems and consumption must be connected with it.

Mao proposes institutional reform: raising household income's share of national income and labour remuneration's share of primary distribution, improving social security, equalising basic public services and removing unreasonable consumption restrictions. The aim is a domestic circulation that is the mainstay and interacts with international circulation. Read the original if you want a concise Party-aligned academic statement of the theory behind China's domestic demand policy for 2026.
quoteEn: The development of production directly determines the extent to which domestic demand can be supplied and satisfied, and whether the strategy of expanding domestic demand succeeds ultimately depends on the level of production.
quoteZh: 生产的发展直接决定内需的被供给能力与满足程度，实施扩大内需战略能否成功最终取决于生产的发展水平。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Chinese economic policy that seeks to make growth rely more on domestic consumption and investment than on exports. The Party's 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations call it the strategic foundation of economic work.
A policy line introduced around 2015 that aims to improve the quality and structure of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity and upgrading industry.
The idea that China's economy should run mainly on internal production, distribution and consumption, while interacting with international markets. It is part of the 'dual circulation' formulation.
China's medium-term national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030.

t: The historical revisionism behind Takaichi's fallacies
zh: 高市谬论背后的历史修正主义思想
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 30 January 2026, examines the erroneous remarks on Taiwan made by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae. Zhang argues that they express a long-held historical revisionism: denial of Japan's aggressive character in the Second World War, rejection of postwar reflection, and a push towards remilitarisation. In Zhang's reading, the remarks only seem reckless and in fact serve deliberate political aims.

The article first reviews Takaichi's record of promoting revisionist views through media appearances, publications and institutional change. It then analyses her characteristic political method and its goals, and closes by linking her Taiwan remarks to earlier Japanese justifications for expansion.

Zhang cites several examples: Takaichi's 2013 claim that the postwar constitution did not reflect the free will of the nation, her 2021 pledge to rename the Self-Defense Forces a "national defence force" and revise Article 9, and her visits to Yasukuni Shrine. Zhang also describes her 2025 visit to a Japanese military cemetery in Kuala Lumpur and her long campaign, with groups such as the New History Textbook compilation association, to change the term for wartime "comfort women" in textbooks, which the Japanese cabinet and education ministry accepted in 2021. Her method, Zhang says, is to throw out a provocative position, rally extreme conservatives, win over some centrists, and then secure government decisions, while creating an appearance of broad support.

Zhang concludes that Takaichi aims to consolidate conservatives, raise support for constitutional revision and build backing for stronger security, and that long tenure could pull Japanese politics further in this direction, which Asian countries should watch. The article likens her Taiwan arguments to Yamagata Aritomo's "line of interest" and Japan's 1933 claims over Northeast China. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese academic view of how Takaichi's historical positions are interpreted in the dispute over her Taiwan remarks.
quoteEn: History should not be forgotten, still less distorted; for both China and Japan, the warning bell of history must keep ringing.
quoteZh: 历史不应忘记，更不容歪曲，对中日双方来说，历史的警钟必须长鸣。

t: Continuously forming new growth points for expanding domestic demand
zh: 不断形成扩大内需的新增长点
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 9 February 2026, He Lilong takes up how China can keep generating new growth points for domestic demand during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Drawing on the Party's Recommendations for the plan and the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference, He argues that the content of demand expansion has changed profoundly. The key, in this account, is to identify emerging fields that make a significant incremental contribution, and to foster new demand and new supply that reinforce each other. He presents this as the supply-and-demand expression of developing new quality productive forces.

The piece is a short commentary organised in five sections. It covers a people-centred source of new demand, an innovation-driven consumption ecosystem, new investment tracks created by green transition, new market space opened by structural change, and a dynamic, time-sequenced cycle of growth. The examples range from artificial intelligence, the low-altitude economy and esports to energy storage, battery recycling, the silver economy and county-level markets.

He's central claim is that new growth points arise from people's rising aspirations for a better life combined with market innovation. On consumption, He cites Marx's point that production produces consumption and that consumption reproduces need, and reads innovation-led new scenarios as this dialectic at a higher level. On green investment, He cites National Energy Administration figures putting new-type energy storage capacity at 73.76 million kilowatts by end-2024, and power-battery recycling above 300,000 tonnes in 2024. Structural change, He argues, opens demand through population ageing, county markets (over 38% of retail sales in 2025, per the article), urban renewal with the urbanisation of migrant workers, and import substitution for technologies subject to Western restrictions.

He concludes that short-term and long-term policy must be balanced: modest counter-cyclical consumption incentives secure livelihoods and stabilise expectations, while long-term bets such as quantum technology and biomanufacturing build future competitiveness and create investment and jobs now. He calls for institutional innovation to activate market forces and for combining improvement of livelihoods and consumption with investment in both things and people. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register account of how economists frame domestic-demand growth under the 15th Five-Year Plan, with sector examples and figures.
quoteEn: Continuously forming new growth points for expanding domestic demand is a dynamic process that responds to the step-by-step, ever-upgrading levels of people's needs.
quoteZh: 不断形成扩大内需的新增长点，是一个响应人民需求层次递进、持续升级的动态过程。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovation rather than resource-heavy growth.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030.
The market for products and services serving older people.

t: Implementing the Party Central Committee's major decisions and plans more resolutely and effectively
zh: 更加坚决有力地贯彻落实党中央重大决策部署
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 9 February 2026, this commentary asks why and how Party members and officials should carry out the major decisions and plans of the Party Central Committee. Wu and Tan argue that these decisions are the "guiding principle" of all Party and state work, and that implementing them more resolutely and effectively is a basic guarantee of continued success. The piece takes its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025).

The article has three parts. The first defines the decisions and plans: major strategic decisions, policy measures and work arrangements across all fields, and documents from Party congresses and plenums. It treats Xi Jinping's instructions as the direction for carrying them out. The second part gives the historical and practical reasons for implementation. The third sets out four practical requirements for officials and for discipline inspection bodies.

The authors' central claim is that implementation is the core test of loyalty to the Party. They say it is the fundamental requirement of upholding the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership, and they call it a basic requirement of political discipline. They cite the Party's discipline regulations, which punish officials who merely voice support without acting, or who implement "with discounts" or "with workarounds". They also point to wartime telegrams from Xibaipo, the special economic zones and the Eight-point Regulation as examples of success that came from faithful implementation. They add that today's external pressures and weak domestic demand call for "honing internal skills", for which the decisions supply direction.

The authors call for four things. Officials should implement decisions without discount, grasping their spirit as a whole. They should implement them creatively, adapting them to local conditions rather than copying documents mechanically. They should hold a correct view of performance, working for the people instead of for show. Discipline inspection and supervision bodies should deepen political supervision that is specific, precise and routine, and should target formalism and bureaucratism. Read the original if you want a clear example of how official Party discourse links policy implementation to political discipline and supervision at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: The Party Central Committee's major decisions and plans guide the development of Party and state work, provide the overall basis for the work of all regions and departments, and are the "guiding principle" of Party and state work.
quoteZh: 党中央重大决策部署引领党和国家工作发展，为各地区各部门工作提供总依据，是党和国家工作的“纲”。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. It opened Xi Jinping's campaign to improve Party conduct.
The primary duty of discipline inspection and supervision bodies in Party usage: checking that Party organisations and officials carry out the Central Committee's line, policies and decisions.
Party terms for officials who go through the motions, stage shows or pile up paperwork instead of solving problems. The Party treats them as obstacles to carrying out central policy.

t: A problem-oriented methodology of reform
zh: 问题导向的改革方法论
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2026, Chen Yingtao asks how China's reform, now in what the article calls a critical stage and a deep-water zone, can deal with problems that involve many actors, factors and dimensions at once. Chen argues that linear thinking and Western frameworks cannot do this. The article proposes a problem-oriented methodology of reform drawn from Marxist philosophy and adapted to Chinese practice.

The commentary is organised in three parts, which Chen presents as an ontology, an epistemology and an axiology. The first treats the origin of complex problems in practice, the second the scientific modes of thought needed to handle them, and the third the value basis of reform. It ends with a short note on future tasks.

On the ontological side, Chen holds that complex problems arise from deepening reform and the movement of contradictions, and that they reflect the historical stage reached after the principal contradiction shifted in the new era. Solving them means changing their conditions through cultural guidance, institutional innovation and technological progress. Epistemologically, the author combines systems thinking, dialectical thinking and bottom-line thinking, illustrated by integrated reform of education, science and talent, by rural revitalisation and by financial-risk prevention. In terms of values, Chen contends that Western approaches rest on the logic of capital and compromise among interest groups, whereas Chinese reform places the people first, aims at common prosperity and offers contributions to a community with a shared future for mankind.

Chen concludes that complex problems will become more prominent, and calls for more philosophical research on them, for distilling practical experience into theory, and for responding to global governance problems with Chinese proposals. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-school-style Marxist philosophy is used to frame the methodology of reform in 2026.
quoteEn: The epistemological foundation of the problem-oriented methodology of reform is embodied in the organic unity of systems thinking, dialectical thinking and bottom-line thinking.
quoteZh: 问题导向改革方法论的认识论根基，集中体现为系统思维、辩证思维和底线思维的有机统一。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for shared security, development and governance among nations.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, emphasised under Xi Jinping, aiming at prosperity shared by all and at narrowing income and regional gaps.
A mode of thinking promoted by Xi Jinping that involves anticipating the worst outcomes and setting limits on risk, while striving for the best result.
A principle in current Party discourse that the people's interests are the highest standard for policy and for the Party's work.

t: The origins, wrong turns and reassessment of neoliberalism
zh: 新自由主义的滥觞、歧路及反思
paras: Liu Shiqiang, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2026, takes up the growing global development deficit: widening inequality, class antagonism and ecological crisis. The article argues that these are the result of neoliberalism's over-expansion since the end of the Cold War and reveal deep flaws in it as a political idea and development model. Understanding it, Liu says, is a precondition for rebuilding the global development order.

The piece is organised in three parts. It first traces neoliberalism from classical liberalism through Keynesianism to the Friedman-inspired Reagan–Thatcher turn, and sets out its core tenets. It then examines theoretical defects and present difficulties in the West, citing US data on income concentration and election spending. Finally it turns to the effects on developing countries and on global governance.

Liu summarises neoliberalism's core as full privatisation and free markets, multiparty democracy with checks and balances, and multiculturalism with individual primacy. The author treats these as one interlocking whole serving the free movement and unlimited accumulation of capital. In Liu's critique, this puts capital above economy, politics and society, producing monopoly, crisis, “veto politics”, commodified social life and, in the end, crises of state governance. Exported to Latin America, Eastern Europe and Asia, it brought stagnation and unrest, and Liu describes “liberal democracy” promotion as cover for hegemony and capital expansion. Liu reads populism, protectionism and Trump's tariffs as products of its failure.

Liu concludes that the world must move beyond the binary of laissez-faire and closed conservatism. The author calls for a dynamic balance between market efficiency and social fairness, checks and government capacity, and individual rights and social values, and for respect for other states' legitimate rights in building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese academic commentary frames the critique of neoliberalism and the Western model.
quoteEn: In short, the core problem of neoliberalism is that it puts capital in a supreme position, comprehensively governing economic, political and social order, which over time will inevitably bring a crisis of state governance.
quoteZh: 质言之，新自由主义的核心问题在于将资本置于无上地位，全面统摄经济、政治和社会秩序，久而久之必将带来国家治理危机。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, presenting international relations as based on cooperation, shared interests and mutual respect.

t: The decline of neoliberalism in the United States is irreversible
zh: 美国新自由主义式微不可逆转
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 January 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary asks whether successive US administrations could rescue neoliberalism after its systemic decline. Zhang argues that, whether through partial repair or wholesale sublation, neoliberalism's decline in the United States cannot be reversed.

The article moves through three presidencies. It treats Obama's post-2008 reforms, Trump's populist variant of neoliberalism, and Biden's economic policy, then closes with a section on neoliberalism's historical end.

Zhang contends that Obama's rescue measures stabilised the economy briefly but left financial monopoly and unequal wealth distribution untouched, and so fed Occupy Wall Street and populism. Trump, in this account, abandoned neoliberal globalisation through tariffs and "America First" but intensified tax cuts, deregulation and privatisation, serving big capital under a populist cover. Biden's policy, marked by Jake Sullivan's 2023 Brookings speech and the "new Washington consensus", is read as a sublation of neoliberalism and a return to Keynesianism, though it keeps a "limited liberalism".

Zhang concludes that neoliberalism is essentially social Darwinism and cannot resolve polarisation, social division or industrial hollowing-out. In this reading, US governments treat any "-ism" as a tool for protecting national interests, hegemony and global capital returns, and neoliberalism has completed its mission. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese academic view of how recent US economic policy is interpreted as the end of neoliberalism.
quoteEn: In the final analysis, the decline of neoliberalism is the inevitable result of capitalism's inherent contradictions becoming ever more prominent without being resolved.
quoteZh: 归根结底，新自由主义的式微是资本主义固有矛盾不断凸显而不得其解的必然结果。

glossary.explanation: A set of market-oriented policy prescriptions, such as liberalisation, privatisation and fiscal discipline, formulated around 1989 and promoted internationally. The article treats it as the policy face of neoliberalism.
A Hegelian-Marxist term (Aufhebung) for negating something while retaining some of its elements. Zhang uses it for Biden's policy shift away from neoliberalism.

t: Milei economics: the extreme alienation of neoliberalism
zh: 米莱经济学：新自由主义的极端异化
paras: Xie examines the economic programme of Argentine president Javier Milei, which the article calls "Milei economics". It argues that this programme fuses Austrian-school market fundamentalism with right-wing populism and is an extreme distortion of neoliberalism, produced by a global conservative revival and Argentina's economic crisis.
The commentary first sets out Milei's ideology, theory and policy platform. It then reviews three long-term costs of the reforms and closes with three warnings for developing countries.

Xie describes Milei's creed as hostility to Marxism, social justice, the welfare state and Peronism. His theory treats the state as the "enemy of freedom", rejects market failure and dismisses Keynesianism and the developmentalism of the UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean. His platform of privatization, liberalization and dollarization works like "shock therapy": cuts to the federal bureaucracy, deregulation, planned sales of 41 state firms, and 30-year tax breaks for foreign investors in lithium and shale. Xie says the short-term gains rest on damage to the economy's foundations. Disputes over resource revenue have set the federal government against provinces such as Chubut. Poverty fell from 52.9% to 31.6% between mid-2024 and mid-2025, which Xie attributes mainly to lower inflation and regards as unsustainable. Heavy debt, including IMF and US support packages of 20 billion dollars each, is said to have eroded Argentina's economic sovereignty.

Xie draws three warnings: avoid ideologizing economic theory, avoid extreme policies lacking social buffers, and avoid theoretical dogmatism that ignores national conditions. Developing countries, the author concludes, should seek a balance between market and government, build their own development theory and defend economic sovereignty. Read the original if you want a short Chinese academic assessment of Milei's economics and the lessons it draws for developing countries.
quoteEn: The core of Milei economics is a deep fusion of Austrian-school market fundamentalism and right-wing populism; it is an extreme alienation of neoliberalism against the backdrop of Argentina's political and economic crisis.
quoteZh: 米莱经济学的核心是奥地利学派市场原教旨主义与右翼民粹主义的深度融合，是新自由主义在阿根廷政治经济危机背景下的极端异化。

t: Standards and practical paths for building a system of identifiers of Chinese civilization
zh: 中华文明标识体系的构建标准与实践路径
paras: Following the call of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) to build a system of identifiers of Chinese civilization, this Guangming Daily commentary asks how such a system should be defined and constructed. Xu argues that the key is a clear set of standards, and that these must be paired with concrete practice if the identifiers are to unite national spirit and display cultural appeal.

The article first sets out three pairs of standards, then four practical dimensions: excavation, interpretation, dissemination and innovation. Its examples come mainly from archaeology and early texts, including the Taosi gnomon, the Erlitou turquoise dragon-shaped object, the He zun bronze inscription and the Han-dynasty brocade armguard.

The standards are authority with leadership; irreplaceability with public recognisability; and general acceptance with ease of understanding. Xu holds that an identifier must express the roots of the civilization and integrate diverse cultural elements. It must also carry values that other cultures cannot copy, be known across class, region and age, and convey deep meaning in simple form. The dragon totem is offered as an example, as is the idea of harmony in diversity, which Xu says has become a principle in international relations after creative transformation.

For practice, Xu calls for archaeological projects such as the Project to Trace the Origins of Chinese Civilization and for the protection of intangible heritage. Xu also wants creative interpretation of identifiers for present needs, wider reach through museums and digital media, and new artistic and design expressions. Read the original if you want a short, example-led statement of the official criteria for cultural identifiers in current Party discourse.
quoteEn: The key to building and establishing the system of identifiers of Chinese civilization lies in setting scientific and clear standards.
quoteZh: 构建和树立中华文明标识体系，关键在于确立科学清晰的标准导向。

glossary.en: system of identifiers of Chinese civilization
glossary.explanation: A concept in the Fourth Plenum's decision (2025), meaning a structured set of symbols, relics and ideas taken to represent Chinese civilization. The article treats it as an organic whole with internal logic and levels.

glossary.en: Project to Trace the Origins of Chinese Civilization
glossary.explanation: A long-running state-backed interdisciplinary research programme that uses archaeology to study the origins and early development of Chinese civilization.

t: Providing economic-law support for the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 为新质生产力发展提供经济法支撑
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2026, asks how economic law can support new quality productive forces. Pazliya Yusup argues that economic law, as the body of law adjusting state intervention in the economy, must respond institutionally. The author proposes a sound legal support system that gives technological innovation and industrial change stable market expectations and legal protection.

The piece begins from the Party's proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan and the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference. It first explains why economic law's twin functions fit new quality productive forces, then lists institutional shortcomings during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, and ends with three reform directions.

Yusup argues that macro-control law (fiscal, tax and industrial law) can correct market failure in basic research and disruptive technology, while market-regulation law (anti-monopoly and anti-unfair-competition) can remove barriers so that all business entities use production factors on equal terms. The author names three shortcomings: inconsistent policy orientation and departmentalism in strategic emerging industries; unsettled legal rules on data ownership, trading and security; and regulation that lags behind artificial intelligence and biomanufacturing. The author describes the needed shift as one from a 'law of management' to a 'law of incentive and empowerment'.

Yusup proposes three measures: revising the Law on Progress of Science and Technology and building long-term tax incentives under the new-type whole-nation system; building a nationally integrated legal system for the data-factor market, with pilot schemes and fault-tolerance; and combining local flexibility with legal consistency assessment, filing review and fair-competition review of policies. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese legal scholar links economic law to the Fifteenth Five-Year Plan agenda.
quoteEn: To bring about a paradigm shift in economic law from a purely 'law of management' to a 'law of incentive and empowerment'.
quoteZh: 实现经济法由单纯的“管理之法”向“激励与赋能之法”的范式转变。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for growth driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and higher total factor productivity rather than by resource input.
An official term for mobilising state and social resources nationwide, combined with market mechanisms, to achieve major scientific and technological goals.

t: Advancing the construction of China's autonomous knowledge system through a "revolution in terminology"
zh: 以术语革命推进中国自主知识体系构建
paras: This is a newspaper feature in which two reporters interview scholars in philosophy, Marxist theory, economics, classical literature and literary theory. It asks what a "revolution in terminology" is, what value it has, how it is playing out across disciplines and where it should go next. The piece presents the revolution as an emerging path for reducing dependence on Western discourse, asserting the agency of Chinese scholarship and raising cultural soft power, and as a basis for China's autonomous knowledge system.

The report is organised in four sections: the essence and value of terminological revolution; innovation in individual disciplines; the need to balance innovation with standardisation; and paths for deepening the process. Interviewees include Chen Xudong (Shanghai University of Finance and Economics), Tian Pengying (Northeastern University), Pei Yajun (China National Committee for Terminology in Science and Technology), Zhong Weimin, Luo Shijin, Zang Fengyu, Zhao Tao and Luo Dongqing.

Drawing on Engels's phrase in the preface to the English edition of Capital, the interviewees treat renewing core terms as a way of changing a theory's core, mode of thinking and research paradigm. Chen distinguishes terms (symbolic carriers) from concepts (units of thought), and cites "socialist market economy" and "new quality productive forces" as terms that framed theory and policy. Pei argues that Western-rooted knowledge faces an "interpretive crisis" and "discourse deficit" in explaining China, and Tian presents "a new form of human civilisation" as a break from capitalist modernity as the sole reference point. On disciplines, the article lists economic terms, Party-theory terms, and new literary-studies terms such as "event poetics". Pei reports that, by the end of 2025, the national committee had approved over 600,000 standard terms, nearly 40,000 of them in the humanities and social sciences. Several interviewees warn against coining concepts for their own sake. Zhong opposes both discarding current terms and returning blindly to traditional ones, and Pei calls for a dynamic balance backed by stronger standardisation mechanisms.

The interviewees conclude that terminological innovation must be anchored in practice and guided by the Two Integrations, while remaining open to other civilisations' achievements and willing to cross disciplinary boundaries. Luo Shijin adds that good terms come from long scholarly accumulation, not wordplay. Zang argues that the autonomous knowledge system should reflect the "great logic" of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a snapshot of how Chinese scholars and editors currently describe terminology-building as part of constructing an autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: "Terms are not invented out of thin air, nor are they a mere display of verbal technique; they are intellectual results condensed from close observation of practice and systematic study of problems."
quoteZh: “术语不是凭空臆造，也并非文字技巧的简单展示，而是深入体察实践、系统研究问题后凝结而成的思想成果。”

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation, the digital economy and green transition.
An official goal of building Chinese philosophy and social science with its own concepts and discourse, rather than relying on Western frameworks.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A Party term for the civilisation said to be created by Chinese modernization, presented as an alternative to the Western modernization path.

t: Accelerating the development of "Chinese national community studies" as an academic discipline
zh: 加快推进中华民族共同体学学科建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 13 January 2026
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2026, argues that a dedicated discipline of Zhonghua minzu gongtongtixue (studies of the Chinese national community) should be built up quickly. Ma Yutang presents it as a requirement of Chinese modernization and as the theoretical base for forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation. The discipline, in Ma's account, would supply the source theory for an autonomous Chinese system of philosophy and social science and support high-quality development of the Party's ethnic work.

The piece is organised in five parts: the significance of the project for the present era, the results achieved so far, the key links in building the discipline, and the institutional guarantees it needs. Ma draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on ethnic work and on the call for a scientific and complete theoretical system of the Chinese national community. Ma lists official measures since the 14th Five-Year Plan period, including national cultural projects on the history of exchanges and integration among the Chinese nation's peoples, 28 approved research bases, a new journal at Minzu University of China, interdisciplinary pilot units and a textbook introducing the Chinese national community.

Ma's central claim is that the discipline must be built on three Chinese-controlled systems: historical materials, discourse and theory. The historical-materials system would be compiled through general histories of the Chinese nation and used to guard against historical nihilism, cultural nihilism and narrow nationalism. The discourse system would cover political, theoretical and everyday language.
