glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping from 2012–13 as the aim of Chinese foreign policy. It stresses shared interests, cooperation and a more equitable international order.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
A term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to frame China's solidarity and development cooperation with them.
The official body of ideas guiding China's foreign policy under Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
Zheng's preferred term for what Western scholarship calls the tributary system of imperial China. He argues the usual term is a Western imposition.

t: Using a law-based business environment to help the private economy develop steadily and over the long term
zh: 以法治化营商环境助推民营经济发展行稳致远
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in September 2025, asks how a law-based business environment can support the healthy, high-quality development of the private economy. Wu Xiaoyan, head of the NDRC's business environment centre, argues that the rule of law is an inherent requirement for private firms to grow. Citing Xi Jinping, Wu holds that a socialist market economy is in essence a law-governed economy and that the rule of law is the best business environment.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why a law-based business environment matters, under four headings: protecting lawful rights, stabilising expectations, supporting innovation, and the legal basis for equal treatment. The second reviews progress in legislation, law enforcement, the judiciary and the cultivation of law-abiding awareness. The third lists four priorities for further work. It builds on the Private Economy Promotion Law, which took effect in May 2025.

Wu's core argument is that equal legal protection and predictable rules reduce uncertainty for entrepreneurs and so encourage investment and innovation. Wu says that the Two Unwaverings require all forms of ownership to have equal access to production factors, fair competition and equal legal protection, with property rights as the foundation. Wu cites figures to show progress: private firms produce over 70 percent of technological innovation results, and 3,952 'no penalty for first or minor violations' items had been issued by the end of 2024. Over 6,500 improper enforcement actions were corrected through administrative review in 2024, and more than 97 percent of firms in a World Bank survey judged Chinese courts fair and reliable in commercial disputes. Wu also argues that clear limits on government power, under the principle that officials may act only where the law authorises them, stabilise expectations and let the market play the decisive role in allocating resources.

Wu concedes a gap remains between current conditions and what private firms need, and calls for continued reform using rule-of-law thinking. The proposals are stronger protection of property and lawful rights, including equal liability for infringements and limits on seizing assets. They also cover more standardised enforcement against firms, faster dispute resolution and bankruptcy handling, and a government that sets an example, including clearing arrears owed to small firms and punishing official breaches of trust. Read the original if you want an official statement of how Chinese policymakers link legal reform, the private economy and innovation, with the policy measures and statistics cited.
quoteEn: The rule of law can ensure that all types of enterprises enjoy substantive fairness in entry conditions and operating rules, and can supervise law enforcement and the judiciary so that they strictly follow the substantive and procedural rules set by law, protecting enterprises' lawful operating and property rights.
quoteZh: 法治能够确保各类企业在准入条件、经营规则等方面享有实质公平，并监督执法和司法严格遵守法律规定的实体规则与程序规则，保护企业合法的经营权利和财产权利。

glossary.explanation: A Party principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It is used to justify equal treatment of different ownership forms.
A law that took effect in May 2025. According to the article, it first defines the legal status of the private economy and protects private firms' rights in market access, innovation and financing.
An official goal that emphasises the quality and sustainability of growth, including innovation and efficiency, rather than speed alone.

t: Promoting innovation in urban grassroots governance through joint consultation and joint governance
zh: 以共商共治推动城市基层治理创新
paras: Zhang Ge, writing as Party secretary of Beijing's Haidian District, asks how urban grassroots governance can be renewed in a megacity. The commentary, first published in the People's Daily in September 2025, answers that consultation and joint governance, led by Party organisations, offer the route. It takes as its guide Xi Jinping's remarks on consultative democracy and grassroots governance, and the Central Urban Work Conference of July 2025.

The piece presents Haidian's "Let's Work It Out Together" deliberation mechanism, built on the city's "respond to complaints" reform. It describes a four-part practice: Party building as leadership, consultation, work centred on the grassroots, and joint building of a better home. The author reports that after about two years of practice, complaint volumes have fallen, the resolution rate has risen and satisfaction has improved. The text has three main sections: Party leadership, institutional design, and people's satisfaction as the yardstick.

First, Zhang argues that Party building gives consultation its political direction. Grassroots Party organisations set the agenda and mobilise resources, and Haidian has a five-tier organisational system running from sub-district Party committees to model Party-member households. Second, institutional design must move the focus of governance downwards: the district cut paperwork and meetings for grassroots cadres, set up a five-step procedure (collect, discuss, act, supervise, assess) and created more than 650 deliberation platforms. Zhang links the mechanism to the "Fengqiao experience", presenting consultation as a way of resolving conflicts early, and says 79 long-standing problems have been resolved since 2023.

Third, Zhang treats consultation as the practical form of whole-process people's democracy. Residents, new social organisations, new forms of employment, volunteers and professionals take part in deciding what is done, who does it, how, and how it is judged. The author cites over 9,000 long-standing problems, such as property management, meals for the elderly and parking, solved since 2023, and concludes that consultation is the foundation while implementation is the key. Read the original if you want a first-hand official account of how a Beijing district presents its consultation mechanism and results.
quoteEn: In \"Let's work it out together\", the foundation is \"working it out together\" and the key lies in \"getting it done\"; the two are united in the process of solving the pressing problems that concern the people.
quoteZh: “大家商量着办”，基础是“商量”，关键在“办”，二者统一于人民急难愁盼问题的解决过程之中

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019 describing Chinese democracy as covering all stages of political life, not only elections. Official sources contrast it with electoral democracy in Western systems.

glossary.literal: act immediately on receiving a complaint
glossary.explanation: A Beijing municipal reform in which citizens' complaints, received mainly through a hotline, must be answered and handled by local authorities within set deadlines and are then assessed.
A model of grassroots conflict resolution from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, dating from the 1960s. It stresses relying on the masses to resolve disputes locally; the Party has promoted a "new era" version.
A formula meaning that Party organisations at the grassroots take the lead in governance and in coordinating other actors.

t: Some reflections on the development of artificial intelligence
zh: 关于人工智能发展的几点思考
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2025, Gou Husheng asks how China should steer the rapid rise of artificial intelligence, especially large models. Gou argues that a Chinese path of AI development depends on handling four dialectical relationships: innovation and openness, development and security, government and market, and industrial application and social governance. The piece is framed by Xi Jinping's remarks on AI and by the State Council's recent opinion on implementing the "AI Plus" initiative.

The commentary is short and built in four parts, one for each relationship. Each part states a principle, then illustrates it with examples from China, the United States and the European Union. Cases include DeepSeek, lidar and autonomous driving, the Eastern Data, Western Computing project, ChatGPT's funding history and International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates on jobs.

On innovation, Gou holds that self-reliant innovation is the "root", without which openness becomes dependent development. Openness, through open-source frameworks, talent exchange and global governance, keeps China from becoming a technological island. Gou describes the US as using technological hegemony and the EU as relying on legislation, while China promotes "technology sharing and capacity building". On security, Gou lists risks such as deepfakes, data poisoning, algorithmic bias, academic junk and data-compliance problems, and says China should neither brake out of fear nor accelerate recklessly. On the state and the market, Gou says government fills gaps in basic research and coordinates infrastructure, data and standards, while the market drives commercialisation, which is the synergy expected under the socialist market economy. On governance, Gou cites price discrimination, "information cocoons" and job displacement, and calls AI a tool that augments human capabilities.

Gou concludes that AI should serve high-quality development and social fairness while strengthening China's position in global competition. The author calls for a dynamic balance between efficiency and fairness, innovation and security, and commerce and people's livelihood. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a senior state-enterprise official presents official AI policy thinking in a Party journal.
quoteEn: The essence of AI is a \"tool for augmenting human capabilities\"; if only efficiency maximisation is pursued without constraint, technological development will depart from its original purpose of \"serving humanity\" and may even provoke social conflict.
quoteZh: 人工智能的本质是“增强人类能力的工具”，若只追求效率最大化而不加约束，会导致技术发展背离“服务人类”的初衷，甚至引发社会冲突。

glossary.explanation: An official economic goal, prominent since the late 2010s, that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth alone.
A State Council programme, set out in an opinion issued in 2025, to integrate AI deeply into sectors of the economy and society.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system, which combines market allocation of resources with a leading role for the state and public ownership.
A national project to build computing centres in western China to process data generated in the more developed east.

t: Strengthening Global South studies to gather the mighty strength of the Global South
zh: 加强全球南方研究 汇聚全球南方磅礴力量
paras: This short commentary argues that China needs to strengthen research on the Global South. Xu Yanling starts from the claim that the century's great changes are accelerating, that the balance of global forces is shifting, and that the collective rise of the Global South is an irreversible historical trend. In Xu's view, better scholarship would raise the Global South's voice and influence, help gather its strength, and advance building a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the strategic significance of Global South studies. The second reviews existing Chinese work and identifies gaps in its depth and breadth. The third proposes how scholarship can contribute to unity among Global South states. Xu draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements at the BRICS+ dialogue, the Beijing summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation and elsewhere.

Xu says such research serves three purposes: shared prosperity and a firmer basis for cooperation, exchange of experience on modernization, and world peace and multipolarity. On existing work, Xu credits Chinese scholars with progress on the concept of the Global South, on different countries' views of it, and on discourse and communication systems. Xu then finds the research lacking in depth. It centres on changes to international order and the community with a shared future, while other dimensions of the Global South's rise, the question of who represents it, and challenges such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence receive little systematic study. Research on Global South modernization is also described as lagging.

Xu's recommendations are to balance the differences among Global South countries against what they share, mainly through area studies. Xu also calls for research on China's role, responsibilities and practical paths within the Global South, and for building the field's internal momentum. That means policy guidance, project-based research, field surveys, support for small-language specialists, Global South research centres and a government–think tank–university training mechanism. Xu presents this as providing theoretical reference for China's foreign policy toward the Global South. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics frame the research agenda on the Global South in line with official foreign-policy language.
quoteEn: The differences among Global South countries are the precondition for South-South cooperation and mutual learning, so research on specific fields in each country should be done well to provide intellectual support for bilateral cooperation.
quoteZh: 全球南方国家的差异性是南南合作和交流互鉴的前提，应做好各个国家的细分领域研究，为双边合作提供智力支持

glossary.explanation: A term for developing and formerly colonised countries, now widely used in Chinese official discourse to refer to emerging and developing states as a collective force in international affairs.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, calling for shared interests, cooperation and common governance among states.
A field in Chinese academia studying particular regions and countries, promoted as a priority discipline in support of foreign policy.

t: Protect, pass on and spread the treasures of Chinese culture well
zh: 把中华文化瑰宝保护好、传承好、传播好
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Xi Jinping's instruction, given during a May 2025 visit to the Longmen Grottoes in Luoyang, that cultural treasures be protected, passed on and spread well. Xu presents the three tasks as a sequence: protection is the precondition, transmission gives the heritage its spirit, and dissemination extends the results of both. The author describes heritage as non-renewable and credits the Party leadership with historic achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The piece is organised in three sections matching the three verbs. It draws on examples such as the Longmen Research Institute's digital archive, the Dazu district's talent recruitment in Chongqing, Shanxi University's joint graduate school for grotto culture, Dunhuang VR, the game Black Myth: Wukong, and the Sanxingdui VR exhibition.

On protection, Xu proposes combining technology, talent training and legal safeguards, and notes that the revised Cultural Relics Protection Law took effect on 1 March 2025. Xu adds that open questions remain, including ownership of digital heritage and rules for private capital. On transmission, the author says digital tools and "cultural heritage +" industrial brands can bring heritage into contemporary life. On dissemination, Xu argues that short video, livestreaming and immersive exhibitions have turned one-way communication by museums into two-way cultural co-creation.

Xu concludes that such work expresses and strengthens cultural confidence and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author calls for strengthening protection, deepening transmission and widening dissemination so that heritage continues across generations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links heritage policy, digital technology and cultural industries to Xi Jinping's formulations.
quoteEn: If protection is about preserving the form, then transmission is about forging the soul: through creative transformation and innovative development, it awakens the civilisational genes sleeping in cultural treasures and adapts them to contemporary society and culture.
quoteZh: 如果说保护是“存其形”，那么传承便是“铸其魂”，通过创造性转化与创新性发展，激活沉睡在文化瑰宝中的文明基因，使其与当代社会文化相适应。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream". It refers to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
A Party term for confidence in China's own cultural tradition and values. It was added by Xi Jinping to the earlier "three confidences" and is often linked to heritage and national rejuvenation.

t: Vigorously pass on and promote Lingnan culture
zh: 大力传承弘扬岭南文化
authors: Publicity Department of the CPC Guangdong Provincial Committee
paras: This commentary by the Guangdong provincial Party publicity department, published in Qiushi (2025, no. 17), asks how Guangdong can protect and pass on Lingnan culture, the regional culture of south China, while the province develops rapidly. It opens with Guangdong's Yingge dance and dragon-boat racing as signs of cultural confidence. Citing Xi Jinping's remark that diverse local traditions together make up Chinese civilisation, it presents Lingnan culture as an important branch of Chinese culture. Its answer is to preserve it, display it and pass it on.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first, "Why Lingnan", traces the region's history from archaeological finds of 600,000 to 800,000 years ago through the Nanyue kingdom and the living city of Chaozhou. The second describes protection work, covering heritage sites, museums, archives and research. The third sets out the "new mission" of passing the culture on and out. It ends by tying Guangdong's efforts to Xi Jinping's thought on culture and to building a culturally strong country.

In the article's account, Lingnan culture was formed from three sources: Central Plains culture brought by northern migrants, maritime civilisation, and local traditions. Its core is said to be patriotism and loyalty, shown in figures such as Lady Xian, the "Three Loyalists of Lingnan", Lin Zexu and Sun Yat-sen, and in a practical, hard-working popular character. On protection, the authors cite authentic restoration of the Nanfeng ancient kiln, the suspension of a Dongguan urban-renewal project to preserve a Ming-era wall, regulations to keep old city districts, and 412 registered museums. They report that the province allocated 193 million yuan to intangible heritage in 2019–2024 and set up special research projects.

Transmission, the authors say, rests on four things: integration into daily life (the micro-renovation of Yongqingfang in Guangzhou), succession through new generations of heritage bearers, shaping popular sentiment through works such as the dance drama Yingge and red-culture events, and exchange and mutual learning. In the last of these, Guangdong acts as one of the "two important windows" on reform and opening up, using its overseas Chinese ties and the Qiaopi (remittance letter) archives to spread Chinese culture abroad. The authors conclude that Guangdong will contribute to a culturally strong country. Read the original if you want an official Party-media example of how a provincial leadership frames regional heritage policy within national cultural strategy.
quoteEn: The key to cultural transmission lies in integrating it into daily life.
quoteZh: 文化传承之要，在于融入生活。

glossary.literal: culture south of the mountain ridges
glossary.explanation: The regional culture of the area south of the Five Ridges, centred on Guangdong and neighbouring areas. It includes Cantonese opera, Chaozhou traditions and a long record of maritime trade and overseas migration.
A formulation attributed to Xi Jinping describing Guangdong as a window for showing China's reform and opening-up achievements to the world, and for the world to observe them.
An official body of ideas on cultural work, formally articulated in 2023, which guides Party policy on culture and the building of a culturally strong country.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978. Guangdong was an early testing ground.
Living cultural practices such as opera, crafts, festivals and folk performance, protected through national and UNESCO listings.

t: The rise of the Global South and China's role
st: An interview with the Indian-American scholar Vijay Prashad
zh: 全球南方的崛起与中国角色
zhSub: 访印度裔美国学者维杰·普拉萨德
paras: This is an interview conducted by Zhao Dingqi, a reporter for the journal, with Vijay Prashad, an Indian-American scholar. Prashad is executive director of the Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research and chief correspondent of Globetrotter. The interview asks why the Global South has risen, what that rise means, and what part China plays in it. Prashad presents China as a country that escaped dependency and now helps others do so.

The interview has three parts. The first covers Prashad's path to Marxism and the social contradictions of India: caste, unequal growth and a weakened communist movement. The second covers the origins of the term Global South, neocolonialism and dependency, China's development path, the Belt and Road Initiative and the 'experimental' character of socialist construction. The third covers the implications of Donald Trump's return to the White House in January 2025.

Prashad traces the term to the 1980 Brandt Commission and the 1989 South Commission. He argues that the South has moved from an 'era of protest' against IMF austerity to an 'era of construction', marked by BRICS and the New Development Bank. Neocolonial structures persist through debt and low wages, which he calls a reproduction of colonial structure. In his reading, China escaped this because of the 1949 revolution and Mao Zedong-era socialist construction, which made the post-1978 reforms possible. He names 1949, 1978 and 2013 as the key years for understanding Chinese modernization. In 2013 the Belt and Road Initiative marked a turn from dependence on Northern markets towards building Southern ones. Prashad says the success of China's industrialisation has encouraged Indonesia, Bangladesh and African states. He describes socialism as experimental: flexible, willing to allow restricted private enterprise, and aimed at people's welfare and harmony between humans and nature.

On Trump, Prashad argues that the United States has dropped 'idealism' for a Kissinger-style right-wing realism. In his view the imperialist structure is unchanged, Trump is no ally of the Global South, and Washington will try to block China's and other Southern states' development. He calls on the South to stay vigilant and organise, strengthening South–South cooperation and regional institutions. He also asks that cooperation be harmonious, so that even the weakest states benefit. Read the original if you want a Marxist scholar's account of the Global South, as presented to a Chinese academic readership, with views on China, the Belt and Road Initiative and US policy under Trump.
quoteEn: The 'experimental' nature of socialism lies in using pragmatic mechanisms to advance human society, which requires us to stay flexible and open and to avoid rigidity.
quoteZh: 社会主义的“实验性”就体现在运用务实的机制推动人类社会进步，这就要求我们保持灵活性和开放性，避免僵化行事。

glossary.explanation: A collective term for developing and emerging-market countries. In this interview Prashad traces it to the 1980 Brandt Commission and the 1989 South Commission, and Chinese official discourse now uses it widely.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond through investment and lending.
The official name for China's path of development under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Security of mainstream ideology in the digital-intelligence era: challenges and countermeasures
zh: 数智时代主流意识形态安全：挑战与对策
paras: Li Huijuan and Wan Xiaopeng ask how mainstream ideology can be kept secure in the "digital-intelligence era", their term for a period shaped by big data, artificial intelligence and networked platforms. Citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called national security an important foundation for Chinese modernization, they treat ideological security as part of national security. Their thesis is that digital technologies have created new conditions and pressures for mainstream ideology, and that these call for Party leadership, technological adoption, talent building and stronger internet legislation.

The article has three parts. It first describes four new conditions: information sources becoming decentralised, content fragmented, media carriers diversified, and communication effects maximised. It then sets out four challenges, and finally proposes four basic strategies. It draws on statements by Xi Jinping and on the Opinions on accelerating the deep integration of media development.

On conditions, the authors argue that when the public both produces and receives information, mainstream media and authoritative bodies lose their monopoly on the microphone. Shallow, entertainment-led content, multimodal tools such as voice cloning and emotion recognition, and recommendation algorithms are said to trap individuals in "information cocoons" and "echo chambers". From this the authors derive the challenges: competing currents of thought that test Marxism's guiding position; mainstream media needing livelier discourse that keeps authority; the need for new propaganda platforms using 5G, big data, AI and blockchain; and a governance system able to break cocoons and algorithmic discrimination through legislation and technical improvement.

The authors' strategies start with upholding Party management of ideology, with leading cadres taking responsibility and top-level design. They also call for applying digital technology to risk monitoring, content production, dissemination and feedback, and for training specialist talent, including influential opinion leaders, given a young online population led by the post-2000 generation. Their final strategy is stronger legislation, building on the Cybersecurity Law and on specific penalties such as those for defaming heroes and martyrs, because the internet is not a place beyond the law. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-aligned scholars frame ideological security and governance of digital media.
quoteEn: The internet is not a place beyond the law; governing the online sphere requires not only "soft" means, namely strengthening the ability to guide and contest public opinion, but also "hard" means as a supplement.
quoteZh: 互联网不是法外之地，网络领域治理，不仅要注重“软性”手段的运用，即加强思想舆论的引导、斗争能力，也要辅之以“硬性”手段。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese official discourse, the dominant body of ideas led by Marxism and Party theory, which the state seeks to keep in the leading position in public opinion.
A principle that the Communist Party leads and controls work in the ideological field, including media and online opinion.
The official term for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.
A term for the narrowing of a person's information intake when algorithms feed them only content that matches their existing preferences.
A Chinese expression combining digital technology and artificial intelligence, used to describe the present stage of technological change.

t: The Western model of modernization and its contemporary predicaments
zh: 西方国家的现代化模式及当代困境
paras: Wang Wei asks how Western countries modernized and why their model now faces systemic difficulties. The article argues that Western modernization was capital-centred rather than people-centred, that it produced great wealth alongside polarisation, ecological damage and colonial plunder, and that its internal flaws now surface as governance crises. Developing countries, Wang concludes, may learn from the West but should not treat it as a model.

The piece has three parts. It first traces the rise of Europe from the British Industrial Revolution through the second and third industrial revolutions, the spread of industrialisation to Germany and the United States, and the formation of a world economy with a core and a periphery. It then describes the shared features of the Western model, with examples from Britain and the United States. Finally it surveys contemporary governance problems, including deindustrialisation, populism and identity anxiety.

Wang's central move is to define Western modernization as capital-centred. In this account capital concentrates wealth and political power, replaces personal dependence with dependence on things (materialism, utilitarianism, fetishism), selects technology for surplus value rather than ecological reasons (illustrated by Manchester's air and water pollution), and drives colonial expansion on which Western development is said to have depended. Wang cites Marx, Engels and Xi Jinping to support this reading, and says it was the Chinese modernization path that broke the equation of modernization with Westernization. A second move links the model's flaws to its later stages: as deindustrialisation hits workers and townspeople, wage stagnation and inequality feed populism, such as Brexit, the Yellow Vests and American economic and white nationalism. Wang reads these as signs of government failure, market failure and social disorder, with governments, markets and society all revolving around capital.

Wang concludes that world modernization began in the West but will not end with its flawed model. Conditions for latecomers differ sharply from earlier times, and Wang calls on developing countries to find paths suited to their own circumstances rather than copy Western experience. Wang adds that Western states which deflect attention outward instead of examining the roots of their problems risk deeper internal crises. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese academic account presents the historical development and current difficulties of Western capitalism for a general Party-journal readership.
quoteEn: This model of modernization is capital-centred modernization, not people-centred modernization.
quoteZh: 这种现代化模式是以资本为中心的现代化，而不是以人为中心的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from the Western model and as a people-centred alternative.

t: An outline of the factors that generate the modern strength of Chinese civilization
zh: 中华文明的现代力量生成因素论要
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's remark that Chinese modernization endows Chinese civilization with modern strength, while Chinese civilization gives Chinese modernization its deep foundations, Yang Zengdong and Huang Shize ask how this "modern strength of Chinese civilization" came into being. They argue that it is not accidental but the necessary result of historical development, and that it arises from four interacting factors. Understanding these factors, they say, matters for strengthening cultural confidence and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised around the four factors, each treated in its own section. The first is the outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization, the second is the leadership of the Communist Party of China, the third is the Second Integration, and the fourth is the conscious action of the Chinese people. A short closing section compares China with Latin America, Africa and the West.

The authors first claim that the modern strength is a historical and indigenous force, formed through continuity rather than rupture. They contrast Chinese civilization with the "fractured" civilizations of the West and say it is endogenous, active and self-aware. They tie its five characteristics (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) to the Party's leadership: through revolution, ideological guidance and mass organisation, the Party liberated the people and created a new form of human civilization. They then present the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, as the cultural main line. In their account it sublates the dross of tradition, dispels Western-centrism, consolidates cultural subjectivity and answers earlier currents of cultural restorationism and wholesale Westernisation. Finally they locate the subjective driving force in the people's historical initiative, cultural confidence, theoretical consciousness grounded in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and strong national identity.

The authors conclude that the generation of this strength is both a historical and a contemporary question. In their reading, Latin America and Africa once had brilliant civilizations and faced similar outside interference but did not rise as China has. The West, though it entered modernity early, lacks later momentum because of its limitations. The strength, they say, springs from the practice of the people and will advance through it. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party-affiliated scholars link civilizational distinctiveness, Party leadership and the Second Integration within current official discourse on Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The modern strength of Chinese civilization arises from the practice of the people, and it will necessarily advance with great strides through that same practice.
quoteZh: 中华文明的现代力量是从人民群众的实践中生发出来的，也必然会在人民群众的实践中阔步向前。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been elaborated in Party documents since the early 2020s.

Xi Jinping's formulation (2023) of combining the basic principles of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the first being with China's concrete realities.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase describing the civilization that Chinese modernization is said to create. It stresses material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development.
Five features (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness, peacefulness) that Xi Jinping set out in 2023 as marking Chinese civilization.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, which it presents as restoring China's historical standing and strength.

t: Raising the quality and efficiency of producer services to support the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 以生产性服务业提质增效有力支撑新质生产力发展
paras: Zhou Haichuan takes up a policy question set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): how producer services, meaning R&D, design, information, consulting, logistics and after-sales services for production, can support new quality productive forces. The article argues that high-quality development of these services is a key link in cultivating such forces, but that China's producer services still have four weak points that need targeted remedies.

The piece is a short policy commentary in four steps. It first explains why producer services matter, then identifies four shortcomings in China's current position, and finally sets out five lines of action. It draws on statistics for 2023 and on examples from smartphones, industrial internet platforms and AI talent supply.

On the first point, Zhou assigns producer services four roles: a key link in innovation, a catalyst for new production relations, a support for high-grade production factors, and an accelerator through digital platforms. As evidence, the article says intangible services such as operating systems, software and chip-design patents account for about 55% of a smartphone's value. The four weaknesses are weak science and technology service capacity, poor transfer of research results, shallow integration with industry, and insufficient high-end professional services. Zhou cites figures: research and technical services made up only 7.2% of the revenue of large producer-service firms in 2023; subscription models were 15% of industrial internet platform revenue; and the shortfall in AI talent exceeds 5 million.

Zhou calls for supporting innovation platforms and key laboratories, building full-chain transfer services centred on pilot-scale testing, and deepening the integration of advanced manufacturing with producer services. Zhou also proposes cultivating data, talent and technology-finance factors, and opening services further, including negative lists for cross-border services trade and a bigger role in international standard-setting. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-aligned economic commentary links the sectoral policy of producer services to the new quality productive forces agenda, including the figures it cites.
quoteEn: Producer services cover R&D and design, the transfer of scientific results, intellectual property and related legal services, and touch many stages in the development of modern and advanced technology; they are a key link in stimulating scientific and technological innovation and cultivating new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 生产性服务业涵盖研发与设计服务、科技成果转化服务、知识产权及相关法律服务等，事关现代科技、先进技术发展的多个环节，是激发科技创新、培育新质生产力的关键一环。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading, often linked to digital technology and AI.
The official economic goal since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Services that serve production rather than final consumers, such as R&D, design, logistics, finance and consulting.

t: Deepening the understanding of the laws governing the relationship between aggregate supply and aggregate demand
st: Reflections on studying Volume I of Selected Economic Works of Xi Jinping
zh: 深化对总供给与总需求关系的规律性认识
zhSub: 学习《习近平经济文选》第一卷的体会
paras: Written as a study note on Volume I of Selected Economic Works of Xi Jinping (published March 2025), this article asks how Xi Jinping's economic thought treats aggregate supply and aggregate demand, which of Marxist political economy's principles it develops, and how the two should be balanced in future. The authors argue that this body of thought treats supply and demand as a unified whole within the cycle of social reproduction. They contrast this with the Western tradition, which in their account separates supply-side from demand-side analysis.

The article opens by situating the topic among the five "must balance" relationships set out by the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference. It then gathers Xi's statements into three core views, derives four "laws" or regularities, and ends with policy proposals for supply, demand and the links between them. The authors, writing from Nankai University, cite scholars such as Li Xuesong, Chen Yulu and Guo Kesha as earlier work on the theme.

The central move is to read supply and demand through Marx's schema of social reproduction, in which production and consumption sit at the two ends and distribution and exchange connect them. Smoothing the circulation of the national economy is therefore, the authors say, the substance of balancing supply and demand. They claim Xi's thought extends Marx's reproduction theory in four ways: it moves from a closed to an open economy by distinguishing domestic from international circulation; it refines supply and demand structures, including the need to keep non-productive sectors such as finance and real estate in proportion to productive ones; it balances short-term growth with long-term development under high-quality development; and it combines an effective market with an effective government under socialist market economy institutions.

The authors propose action on three fronts. On the supply side, they call for cultivating new quality productive forces and building a modernised industrial system. On the demand side, they call for expanding consumption, investment and external demand to build the new development pattern. For linking supply and demand, they urge improving the livelihood system and building a unified national market. They conclude that this reasoning offers a method for building an independent Chinese system of economic knowledge. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Xi Jinping Thought on the economy is framed in terms of Marx's reproduction schemes, along with a full list of the policy measures the authors propose.
quoteEn: The essence of balancing aggregate supply and aggregate demand is to keep the circulation of the national economy unobstructed.
quoteZh: 统筹总供给与总需求关系的实质是畅通国民经济循环

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and digital and green transformation.
The official goal of the current development stage, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
The official name for China's economic system since the 1990s, combining public-sector dominance with market allocation of resources.

t: Changes in the structure of legally protected interests under digital capital
zh: 数字资本的法益结构变迁
paras: Wang Lipei asks how law should respond to digital capital, which the author defines as a new capital form existing in digital shape, built by accumulating and processing data and invested in the digital economy for returns. The article argues that data combines personality elements and property elements, so the traditional split between personality rights and property rights no longer fits. Wang sees early signs of a composite "personality–property right" in China's Personal Information Protection Law and the EU's Digital Markets Act.

This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (22 July 2025) moves in four steps. It first describes the distinct character of digital capital, then the limits of the traditional property-centred legal order, including the EU's GDPR. It then lists institutional bottlenecks and proposes a new framework, and ends with a general conclusion.

Wang argues that digital capital is marked by a "dual alienation" of personality and property. Data carries users' behavioural traces and emotional preferences, yet platforms turn it into tradable commodities, convert unpaid user activity into monopoly assets and widen distributive injustice. In Wang's account, consent rules, weak priority rules between dignity and data utility, fragmented legal tools and the platforms' technical advantage keep existing law from responding. Wang proposes a "three-dimensional" structure. It has a layered, independent right of digital personality, a tiered model for sharing data revenue with data trusts, and coordinated rules including antitrust duties, algorithm transparency, algorithmic impact assessment and a "digital supervisor".

Wang concludes that the shift is the legal projection of the move from industrial to digital civilisation. Law should move from absolute ownership to "digital symbiosis", from freedom of contract to "algorithmic justice" and from private-right protection to "digital human rights". Wang calls for balancing efficiency gains against inalienable personal dignity. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese legal-theory proposal on data rights, platform power and algorithms.
quoteEn: Law must reconstruct its value coordinates: from \"absolute ownership\" to \"digital symbiosis\", from \"freedom of contract\" to \"algorithmic justice\", and from \"protection of private rights\" to \"digital human rights\".
quoteZh: 法律必须重构其价值坐标系，从“所有权绝对”转向为“数字共生”，从“契约自由”升级成“算法正义”，从“私权保护”进化至“数字人权”。

glossary.explanation: A capital form that exists in digital shape and is built by accumulating and processing data, then invested in the digital economy for returns. The author uses it to analyse platform power and data value.

glossary.literal: composite right of personality and property
glossary.explanation: The author's proposed right form that treats data as a unity of personality and property elements, rather than as either a thing or information.
A proposed arrangement in which an independent third party manages public data assets to prevent platforms' private interests from eroding the public interest.

t: "Antagonism" and "harmony" in economic and social development, and their transcendence
st: A reading of Marx's "Bastiat and Carey"
zh: 经济社会发展中的“对抗”“和谐”及其超越
zhSub: 马克思《巴师夏和凯里》解读
source: Journal of Peking University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2025 no. 2
paras: Nie Jinfang offers a close reading of "Bastiat and Carey", the opening section of Marx's 1857–1858 manuscripts (the Grundrisse), which he says scholars have largely neglected. Drawing on the MEGA2 edition, Nie criticises existing studies for extracting fragments to fit external frameworks rather than reconstructing Marx's own reasoning. The article argues that the text, written in response to the 1857 crisis, shows Marx treating "antagonism" and "harmony" as relative, coexisting conditions, and that it still bears on present-day problems.

The article first sets out the crisis of 1857–1858 and Marx's survey of the political economy of his day, which he divided into four unproductive types: eclectic compendia, mere accumulation of material, repetition of old policy disputes, and careerist extension of classical authors. It then examines Marx's account of Henry Carey and Frédéric Bastiat as the two exceptions. Nie goes through the American context of Carey's thought, the contrasting national settings of the two men, and Marx's remarks on Bastiat's chapter on wages. A final section draws four lessons for the present.

Nie argues that Marx credits the two men only for rejecting the classical economists' theoretical expression of bourgeois society. Carey, shaped by a bourgeois society that began "from itself" in North America, blames the state for disturbing harmony, yet ends up demanding protective tariffs. Bastiat, writing from backward France, places harmony in an imagined, ideal form found only in England and America and favours free trade. Marx judges both to be unhistorical and bound by a single national outlook. Nie then follows Marx's rebuttal of Bastiat's claim that wages are a "fixed income": it takes one side of a relation as the whole, and it ignores the instability and the risk that wage labour brings. Nie also reads the later five-part plan of the Introduction as evidence that Marx gave the state's economic functions a place in political economy.

Nie draws four lessons. Antagonism and harmony coexist, and antagonism should be a means to sublate itself, neither concealed by talk of harmony nor made an end in itself. State functions are shifting from political coercion towards economic roles, and they should respect economic laws and avoid "statism". Thinkers must combine a national standpoint with historical awareness and a global outlook. Lasting theory also grows out of major events and hard intellectual labour, as the Grundrisse did. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-based commentary on a little-studied opening of the Grundrisse and its link to the 1857 crisis.
quoteEn: Antagonism is a means, not an end; its purpose is to use antagonism to sublate and transcend antagonism, and gradually to reach a state of social progress and harmony.
quoteZh: 对抗是手段，而不是目的，对抗的目的是借助对抗扬弃对抗、超越对抗，逐步达致社会进步和和谐之境。

glossary.explanation: The second Marx-Engels Gesamtausgabe, the historical-critical complete edition of Marx and Engels. Its Part II, completed in 2012, publishes Capital and its preparatory materials.

t: Advancing Asian economic integration from the new starting point of Asia's overall revitalisation
zh: 站在亚洲整体振兴新起点上推进亚洲经济一体化
paras: This newspaper commentary, written against the background of US protectionism, asks how China should use its ties with its Asian neighbours to respond to an uncertain world economy. Ouyang Yao argues that speeding up Asian economic integration is both a necessary answer to unilateralism and protectionism and the route to building a community with a shared future with neighbouring countries and to Asia's overall revitalisation. The piece opens with Xi Jinping's description of Asia as standing at a new starting point.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why good-neighbour relations matter, drawing on a cyclical account of hegemonic rise and decline and on three trends in Asia's economy. The second discusses how to deepen integration through the ASEAN way, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) and a China–Japan–South Korea free trade area. The third lists four advantages China can contribute: market size, technological innovation, industrial leadership and infrastructure capacity.

Ouyang contends that rising hegemons favour free trade and multilateralism, while declining ones turn to protectionism and trade barriers. Against this, the author cites Asia's 49 per cent share of global GDP in 2024, its growing manufacturing base and complete industrial chains, and rising intra-Asian trade dependence. Asia's stability can therefore counter global uncertainty. The author presents the ASEAN model of consultation, with no fixed leading country, as suited to Asia's diversity, and cites RCEP's effects: intra-regional trade up about 3 per cent in 2024, and intermediate goods at roughly 66 per cent of trade in 2023.

Ouyang proposes that RCEP members shorten zero-tariff transition periods, remove non-tariff barriers, move towards negative-list commitments, make rules of origin easier to use, and add operational detail on digital trade and intellectual property, together with dispute-settlement channels. The author also urges China to import more from ASEAN, export high-tech goods and invest abroad to spread technology, lead a multipolar "flying geese" production network, and build railways and ports, citing the Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. The goal is for the fruits of Chinese modernization to benefit Asian countries. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese economist links Asian regional integration, RCEP and Belt and Road-style infrastructure to China's response to US trade policy.
quoteEn: Using the stability and certainty of the Asian economy to meet the instability and uncertainty of the world economy is undoubtedly a wise choice for solving today's world economic problems.
quoteZh: 以亚洲经济的稳定性和确定性应对世界经济的不稳定性和不确定性，无疑是破解当今世界经济难题的明智选择。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Chinese Communist Party's model of national development, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as a path with distinct features rather than a copy of Western modernisation.

glossary.zh: 区域全面经济伙伴关系协定
glossary.pinyin: Qūyù quánmiàn jīngjì huǒbàn guānxì xiédìng
glossary.explanation: A free trade agreement signed in November 2020 by 15 Asia-Pacific countries including China, Japan, South Korea and the ASEAN members. It entered into force on 1 January 2022.

A model from development economics in which industries shift in sequence from more advanced to less advanced economies, like geese in formation. The article argues that Asia has moved from a Japan-led pattern to one with several lead economies.

t: Techno-feudalism: meaning, controversies and responses
st: An interview with the French economist Cédric Durand
zh: 技术封建主义：内涵、争议与应对
zhSub: 访法国经济学家塞德里克·迪朗
paras: This is an interview conducted, translated and edited by Zhao Dingqi of the journal World Socialism Studies. The interviewee is the French economist Cédric Durand, professor at Paris 13 University and author of Techno-féodalisme (2020), described as the first systematic political-economy study of the topic. The interview asks why the internet's early promise of liberation gave way to monopoly power, and what 'techno-feudalism' means as a description of capitalism under digital technology.

The conversation has three parts. The first traces the 'Californian ideology', fictitious capital and the origins of the concept. The second covers the features of techno-feudalism and three kinds of criticism. The third asks whether techno-feudalism has replaced capitalism and how resistance might be organised. Durand also places his book in relation to earlier work: cyberpunk-era uses of the term, McKenzie Wark, Yanis Varoufakis's 2024 book, Marx's 'industrial feudalism' and Habermas on the refeudalisation of the public sphere.

Durand argues that control of data and of the tools of social coordination now takes priority over production, much as control of land did under feudalism. In his account, platform owners extract 'rents' from users' data and set rules for social life, which blurs the line between economic and political power. He answers three criticisms. First, techno-feudalism differs from feudalism: production is not small-scale and labour is more socially interdependent than ever, but the monopolised asset is appropriated predatorily. Second, the concept does not flatter capitalism, because anti-capitalist critique stays valid whether or not the hypothesis proves right. Third, on the depth of change in production relations, he treats it as an open historical question. He says the trend is towards control investment with zero-sum returns.

On resistance, Durand backs digital commons and free software but considers them insufficient. He does not favour restoring full competition. He proposes revived digital public utilities under the UN or other international cooperation, modelled on the Universal Postal Union. He adds two caveats: the ecological footprint of AI, and the fact that digital collaboration cannot alone secure emancipation, which also depends on people's collective agency. Read the original if you want a first-hand statement of Durand's techno-feudalism thesis, his replies to critics and his policy proposals, as presented to a Chinese Marxist audience.
quoteEn: As under feudalism, the logic of plunder and control takes precedence over the logic of production.
quoteZh: 与封建制度一样，掠夺和控制的逻辑优先于生产的逻辑。

t: Advancing the building of a community with a shared future with neighbouring countries
zh: 深入推进周边命运共同体建设
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's state visits to Vietnam, Malaysia and Cambodia on 14–18 April 2025, Zhai Kun, a professor of international relations at Peking University, argues that China's work with its neighbours should be organised around building a community with a shared future with neighbouring countries. The commentary, published in the People's Daily theory section, presents this as the guiding line set by the Central Conference on Neighbourhood Work in April 2025. Zhai holds that the aim serves regional stability and, in turn, the broader goal of a community with a shared future for mankind.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the long-term strategic positioning of neighbourhood work and the "historic achievements" since the 18th Party Congress (2012), comparing the 2013 symposium on neighbourhood diplomacy with the 2025 conference. The second examines the working framework that supports the project. The third describes the system of values behind it: a shared vision, guiding principles and an "Asian values" foundation.

Zhai makes three main moves. First, he reads the change in name from "neighbourhood diplomacy work" to "neighbourhood work", and from "symposium" to "work conference", as showing that neighbourhood affairs now span domestic and foreign, economic, political and diplomatic fields and receive fuller Party attention. He describes development and security as the "two wheels" of this work, with the Belt and Road Initiative as the main platform (the article cites agreements with 25 neighbours and China as largest trading partner of 18) and an "Asian security model" as strategic support, which he contrasts with Western great-power hegemony. Second, he traces the evolution of the values system: the "five homes" vision (peace, tranquillity, prosperity, beauty, friendship), the addition of "a shared destiny" to the principle of amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness, and the affirmation of peace, cooperation, openness and inclusiveness as Asian values.

Zhai concludes that relations with neighbours are at their best since modern times, but that regional and global change are now closely linked and bring serious challenges. He says China has reached a consensus on a shared-future community with 17 neighbours, forming two "clusters" in the Indochina Peninsula and Central Asia. Continuity of policy, he argues, gives China the confidence and strategic resolve to deepen the project. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese commentators frame the 2025 neighbourhood policy line and its value language.
quoteEn: Development and security are the \"two wheels\" of neighbourhood work, which must keep the two in balance in a complex environment, promoting security with development and development with security.
quoteZh: 发展与安全是周边工作的“两个轮子”，周边工作需要在复杂的环境中保持发展与安全的平衡，促进有发展的安全、有安全的发展。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future with neighbouring countries
glossary.explanation: A Chinese foreign-policy aim of closer political, economic and security ties with bordering and nearby states, derived from the broader concept of a community with a shared future for mankind.

glossary.en: amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness
glossary.explanation: A principle for neighbourhood diplomacy put forward by Xi Jinping at the 2013 symposium on neighbourhood diplomacy.
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013, linking China with countries across Asia, Europe and Africa.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international order based on shared interests and cooperation, now a core slogan of Chinese foreign policy.
A high-level Party meeting held in April 2025 that set the goals and approach of China's policy towards neighbouring countries.

t: Pushing the international order towards greater fairness and rationality
zh: 推动国际秩序朝着更加公正合理的方向发展
paras: Writing in a Guangming Daily commentary on the eve of the 80th anniversary of the United Nations, Gao Zugui asks how the postwar international order should be sustained and improved. The author argues that the UN-centred framework has survived repeated tests and still underpins peace, development and security, and that China is working to make it fairer and more rational.

The piece first traces the order's origins in the UN Charter of 1945 and its value to developing and smaller states. It then identifies two pressures: United States unilateralism and a turbulent world of overlapping security, economic and environmental crises. The second half sets out China's positions on Security Council reform, human rights, regional and international organisations, and global governance.

Gao contends that the greatest challenge to the order is the United States, which, after the Soviet collapse, tried to make it an instrument of its own hegemony and has more recently left international mechanisms and breached international law. Gao also notes that US power to dominate alone has weakened, while other centres of power and non-state actors have grown in influence. Against this background, the author presents China as standing on the side of fairness and justice, defending the UN system, international law and the multilateral trading system. Gao describes China's support for Security Council reform that gives more weight to the Global South and Africa, for human rights suited to national conditions, and for bodies such as the BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, the New Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, which are said to complement existing institutions.

Gao concludes that China's advocacy of equality among states, opposition to hegemony, a multipolar world, the Belt and Road Initiative, a community with a shared future for mankind and the global initiatives on development, security and civilisation is guiding the improvement of the current order. Read the original if you want a concise, official-leaning statement of how a Central Party School scholar presents China's role in UN-centred global governance in 2025.
quoteEn: This is the greatest challenge facing today's international order.
quoteZh: 这是当今国际秩序面临的最大挑战。

glossary.explanation: A term for developing countries, mostly in Asia, Africa and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse uses to describe a group whose representation in global institutions it says should be strengthened.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, presented as China's vision of international relations built on shared interests and cooperation.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Practising true multilateralism
zh: 践行真正的多边主义
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of the United Nations (2025), this commentary asks what multilateralism genuinely requires and why it is under strain. Chen argues that the UN-centred international system and multilateralism built on coordination and cooperation remain the best way to solve global problems. In Chen's account, a few Western countries pursue hegemonism and unilateralism while using a "rules-based international order" to dress up "pseudo-multilateralism".

The article opens with a short history of multilateralism, from the Peace of Westphalia (1648) and the Concert of Europe after 1814–1815, through the International Telecommunication Union and Universal Postal Union and the League of Nations, to the UN. It then sets out three defining features of true multilateralism, lists the current challenges, and ends with three proposals. Chen treats the rise of the Global South and of forums such as the G20, BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation as new momentum for the system.

Chen defines true multilateralism by three features: interdependent interests and indivisible security, so that decisions start from collective rather than individual interests; equal rights for all states regardless of size or wealth, with sovereign equality as the first principle of the UN Charter; and universal rules reached by consultation and applied without exceptionalism or double standards. Against this, Chen charges that a few Western states launch tariff and trade wars, build exclusive "small-circle multilateralism" such as an "Asia-Pacific NATO" and a "chip alliance", impose sanctions and decoupling, place domestic law above international law, and block IMF quota reform. Chen concludes that today's troubles arise because the Charter's principles have not been implemented, not because they are outdated.

Chen calls for rallying consensus under the banner of a community with a shared future for mankind, practising the principle of extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, and upholding international rule of law without exceptionalism or double standards. Chen frames the choice as one between a unipolar hegemony and an equal, orderly multipolar world, and cites Xi Jinping's call to practise true multilateralism. Read the original if you want an authoritative Chinese official statement of how Beijing defines "true" multilateralism and contrasts it with the policies of the United States and its allies.
quoteEn: The challenges facing today's world are not due to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter having become outdated, but precisely to their not having been effectively implemented.
quoteZh: 当今世界面临种种挑战，并不是因为联合国宪章宗旨和原则过时了，而恰恰是由于这些宗旨和原则未能得到有效履行

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It holds that countries' interests and fates are intertwined and calls for joint responses to global challenges.
A term for developing and emerging countries, which Chinese official discourse presents as a rising collective force in global governance.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: joint consultation, joint construction, joint sharing
glossary.explanation: A principle of global governance promoted by Xi Jinping and linked to the Belt and Road Initiative. It stresses that rules be agreed jointly and benefits be widely distributed.

t: Consolidating the civilizational foundations for building China's independent knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences
zh: 夯实构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系的文明根基
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2025, asks how China's independent knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences can be given a firm civilizational base. Zhang and Zang answer that it must rest on the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and be oriented towards a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remarks on the continuity of Chinese civilization and on the need to adapt its cultural genes to modern society. It then runs in two parts: first on deepening the integration of Marxism and traditional culture, then on how a knowledge system built around a community with a shared future for mankind can promote exchange and mutual learning among civilizations.

The authors argue that over a century the Two Integrations have activated the vital elements of traditional culture and produced a new organic cultural entity, strengthening Chinese cultural subjectivity and cultural confidence. They call for scholarship that answers the questions of China, the world, the people and the times, and that develops academic propositions, concepts and discourse suited to Chinese modernization. Zhang and Zang present the idea of harmony and unity (hehe) as the core of the community with a shared future for mankind, citing traditional notions such as "harmony yields new things" and "harmony without uniformity".

They conclude that civilizational exchange should replace estrangement, mutual learning replace conflict, and coexistence replace claims of superiority. They also urge study of the overseas transmission of Chinese civilization, so that the world better understands "China in philosophy and the social sciences" and the Chinese contribution to human civilization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars link cultural subjectivity, the Two Integrations and global civilizational dialogue in current official discourse.
quoteEn: The idea of a community with a shared future for mankind embodies the essence and foremost value of the thought of harmony and unity in China's fine traditional culture.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体理念体现了中华优秀传统文化中和合思想的精髓和首要价值。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Party theory for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was emphasised under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, calling for shared interests and cooperation among states.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.
A term stressed in recent Party discourse for China's cultural self-awareness and independence in developing its own culture and knowledge.
A traditional Chinese idea of harmony and integration among differing elements, which Zhang Liwen has long developed as a philosophical concept.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Building a culturally strong nation requires upholding Marxism as the fundamental guiding thought
st: Interview with Sun Laibin, Party secretary of the School of Marxism at Peking University and special supervisor of the National Supervisory Commission
zh: 建设文化强国必须坚持马克思主义这一根本指导思想
zhSub: 访国家监委特约监察员、北京大学马克思主义学院党委书记孙来斌
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo jijian jiancha bao), 8 May 2025, p. 8
paras: This is an interview with Sun Laibin, Party secretary of Peking University's School of Marxism and a special supervisor of the National Supervisory Commission, conducted by a reporter from the discipline-inspection newspaper. It follows Xi Jinping's remarks at the 17th collective study session of the Political Bureau, which called for building a culturally strong nation by 2035 while upholding Marxism as the fundamental guiding thought. Sun argues that Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere is the precondition for that goal.

The interview has three questions. The first asks how to understand Marxism's guiding position in ideology; the second, where the theoretical advancement of the Chinese Communist Party lies in the new era; the third, what new demands the system of ideological work responsibility now faces.

Sun first argues that ideological security indicates the stability of state power, citing Marx's remark on the dissolution of forms of consciousness and the Soviet collapse and 'colour revolutions' as confirmation. Diversity of ideas, he says, is an objective result of diverse ownership forms and distribution methods, but it does not mean diversity of guiding thought, because the dominant ideology depends on the dominant ownership relations: the primary position of public ownership, the people's democratic dictatorship and Communist Party leadership. Sun then holds that a Marxist party's advancement lies first in its theory, and that upholding and developing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is, in contemporary China, genuinely upholding Marxism. On implementation, Sun calls for stronger responsibility for ideological positions, especially universities and the internet, and for combining 'establishing' (raising the Marxist banner) with 'refuting' erroneous trends. Problems should be sorted into political-principle, ideological-understanding and academic questions, handled respectively by firm opposition, persuasion and scholarly debate.

Sun concludes that Party members and cadres must deepen their study of Xi Jinping Thought and that ideological workers should both reason persuasively and be willing to confront statements that challenge the political bottom line. The text presents the basic system of Marxism's guiding role as a major institutional innovation first stated in 2019. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official ideological and cultural policy is explained to Party and supervisory audiences, including the handling of universities and online space.
quoteEn: Diversity of ideas is not the same as diversity of guiding thought.
quoteZh: 思想观念的多样化并不等同于指导思想的多样化。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts describe it as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
A Party system, formalised in 2015, that assigns Party committees and leaders responsibility for ideological work within their units, including universities and media.
An official goal of raising China's cultural strength and influence, with 2035 set as the target date for its achievement.

t: Establishing a correct view of the history of the Chinese nation
zh: 树立正确的中华民族历史观
paras: Wang Dong and Wang Yonggui take up what they call the correct view of the history of the Chinese nation (Zhonghua minzu), and argue that it should be firmly established. Their starting point is Xi Jinping's speech of September 2024 at the national commendation conference on ethnic unity and progress. There Xi said that China's peoples have jointly opened up the country's vast territory, founded a unified multi-ethnic state, written its history, created its culture and fostered its national spirit. The authors read this as the theoretical statement of the correct historical view and as a basis for historical confidence and for building the Chinese nation as a community.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out the meaning of a historical view built on the "five commonalities" (the five "jointly" formulations above). The second gives the principles and methods for establishing it. The third lists practical paths. It is a short Party-journal piece that relies mainly on Xi's statements and does not discuss specific historical cases.

In the first part, the authors argue that this historical view advances the adaptation of Marxist ethnic theory to Chinese conditions, drawing on the Two Integrations, especially the integration with traditional Chinese culture through ideas such as "all under heaven as one family". They also claim it supplies the ideological basis for forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation. In their account it shows the formation of a "pluralistic yet unified" nation as a historical necessity and supports the case for a community with a shared future for mankind. The second part names three principles: the historical-materialist method, which treats national unity as a historical inevitability; holding to the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity; and firm criticism of erroneous historical views. The authors say some people, under the banner of scholarship, dismember, distort and fabricate history.

For practice, the authors propose deeper historical research, including continuing the project to trace the origins of Chinese civilization and studying exchanges among ethnic groups. They also call for building a shared spiritual home through education, the national common language and standard national textbooks, and shared cultural symbols. A third proposal is to tell the story of the Chinese nation through media at home and abroad. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Party's official line on ethnic work and national history is framed and what practical measures it names.
quoteEn: The correct view of Chinese national history shows the history of how the various ethnic groups merged into the pluralistic and unified Chinese nation; it not only shows that the formation of the Chinese national community was an inevitable result of historical development, but also fully confirms the possibility and feasibility of building a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteZh: 正确的中华民族历史观，展现了各民族交融汇聚成多元一体中华民族的历史，不仅说明了中华民族共同体的形成是中华民族历史发展的必然结果，也充分印证了构建人类命运共同体的可能性与可行性。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation that China's ethnic groups jointly opened up the territory, founded the unified multi-ethnic state, wrote the history, created the culture and fostered the national spirit. It is used as the basis of the official view of Chinese national history.

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A concept in Party ethnic policy, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), that aims at a shared identity among all ethnic groups. "Forging" (铸牢) the sense is described as the main thread of ethnic work in the new era.
The Party's formula of integrating Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023.
A term from recent Party discourse, stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023, meaning that the Chinese nation should hold to its own cultural identity and creativity when it draws on other cultures.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, presented as a vision of cooperative global governance.

t: Forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
paras: Pan Yue sets out the official case for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation (铸牢中华民族共同体意识), the principle that Pan says is now the main thread of the Party's ethnic work. The article, which first appeared in Qiushi, presents the principle as a major original judgement of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Pan argues that it enriches Marxist ethnic theory and consolidates the path of resolving ethnic issues with Chinese characteristics.

The text has four parts. It traces how the formulation developed between 2014 and 2024 through Xi Jinping's speeches and explains its meaning and importance. It then sets out the principle's theoretical sources in Marxism, Chinese civilisation and a century of Party ethnic work. Finally, it lists practical requirements in theory-building, education, narrative and ideology.

Pan's core argument is that the principle responds to specific present conditions. These include uneven development in ethnic regions, growing population movement and mixing among ethnic groups, and what Pan calls sharp ideological struggle in the ethnic sphere. Pan describes the shared consciousness as a reflection of an objectively existing historical community. Four relationships are to be handled correctly: commonality takes the lead over difference, and the shared national consciousness takes precedence over the consciousness of individual ethnic groups. Chinese culture is the trunk and ethnic cultures the branches, and material development does not automatically produce unity. Pan grounds all this in the Two Integrations, especially the integration of Marxism with traditional Chinese culture. Pan also cites the ideas of great unification and 'harmony without uniformity' as part of that heritage.
