Pan's practical proposals include building an autonomous Chinese ethnic-theory knowledge system, distinct from Western ethnic theory, and a discipline of Chinese national community studies. They also include making the principle part of Party-building and performance assessment, and promoting the national common language and nationally compiled textbooks. Pan further calls for telling the story of the Chinese national community, rebutting foreign criticism of ethnic policy, and opposing historical nihilism, extreme nationalism, religious extremism, Han chauvinism and local nationalism. Pan concludes that only a firmly forged sense of community can gather the strength for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of current Party doctrine on ethnic policy, with its stated rationale and policy agenda.
quoteEn: The sense of community for the Chinese nation is the reflection in people's minds of the objective historical existence of the Chinese national community, and is the shared psychological consciousness of the Chinese nation formed in the course of building that community.
quoteZh: 中华民族共同体意识是中华民族共同体这一历史客观存在在人们头脑中的反映，是中华民族共同体建设过程中形成的中华民族共同心理意识。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: to forge firm consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping introduced in 2014 and in 2021 made the main thread of Party ethnic work. It stresses a shared national identity that takes precedence over ethnic-group identities.
The principle of integrating Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration, with traditional culture, was added in 2023.

t: China's proposal for promoting exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
zh: 推动文明交流互鉴的中国方案
paras: This short commentary presents the Global Civilization Initiative, which Xi Jinping first put forward on 15 March 2023 in a keynote speech at the CPC in Dialogue with World Political Parties High-level Meeting. Zhai argues that the initiative offers a Chinese answer to how different civilizations can coexist, and that it breaks with the Western narrative of civilizational conflict. Together with the Global Development Initiative and the Global Security Initiative, it forms what the author calls a logically tight system of global initiatives.

The article first criticises two Western paradigms of civilizational interaction, then explains how the initiative goes beyond them, and finally sets out how it might be put into practice. The first paradigm is Samuel Huntington's "clash of civilizations"; the second is a "civilizational superiority" view that the author describes as a hierarchy of civilizations.

Zhai contends that Huntington's 1993 thesis presupposed conflict, exaggerated the danger of cultural difference, divided the world crudely into seven civilizations, and served to give the United States a new enemy for sustaining hegemony. The "superiority" view, in the author's reading, treats Western political and economic models as universal standards and exports them one way, which invites confrontation. Against these, the initiative follows Xi's formula of exchange over estrangement, mutual learning over conflict, and inclusiveness over superiority. It "unbinds" relations between civilizations from relations between states, denies that civilizations can be ranked, and offers the common values of all humanity in place of "universal values". The author cites the UN General Assembly's designation of 10 June as International Day of Dialogue among Civilizations.

Zhai calls on governments to reject exclusive, values-based diplomacy and to support cultural exchange. The author also asks international organisations to practise genuine multilateralism, and says China will provide institutional and financial support. The author presents the creative transformation of traditional cultures as the route to a shared spiritual homeland for humanity. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese official commentary frames the Global Civilization Initiative against Huntington and Western claims of civilizational superiority.
quoteEn: The Global Civilization Initiative does not exclude or belittle any civilization; it holds that civilizations are not higher or lower, superior or inferior, and, whatever the size, strength or wealth of countries, it gives all civilizations an equal opportunity for dialogue.
quoteZh: 全球文明倡议不排斥或贬低任何一种文明，主张文明不存在高低优劣之分，不论各国大小、强弱、贫富，为所有文明提供平等对话的机会。

glossary.explanation: A proposal announced by Xi Jinping on 15 March 2023. It calls for respecting the diversity of civilizations, advocating common human values, valuing heritage and strengthening international cultural exchange.
A Chinese initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2021 that focuses on international development cooperation. The author treats it as one of three linked global initiatives.
A Chinese initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2022 setting out China's approach to international security. It is the third of the three global initiatives the author lists.

glossary.literal: common values of the whole of humankind
glossary.explanation: A formula used in Chinese official discourse, usually listed as peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. It is presented as an alternative to Western "universal values".

t: Leading the development of new quality productive forces with scientific and technological innovation to build a modern industrial system
zh: 以科技创新引领新质生产力发展 建设现代化产业体系
paras: Qu Yongyi takes up one of the key tasks set by the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference: using scientific and technological innovation to lead the development of new quality productive forces and to build a modern industrial system. The article argues that this task deepens the Party's understanding of the laws of economic work and sets a direction for high-quality development. Qu holds that it requires breakthroughs in technology, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial upgrading.

The article is organised in three parts. The first deals with innovation: basic research, key core technologies, major science and technology projects and national strategic science and technology forces. The second covers industry: transforming traditional industries, developing emerging industries and nurturing future industries. The third turns to the institutional and policy system, including finance, market competition and opening up.

On innovation, Qu cites figures showing that China ranked 11th in the 2024 Global Innovation Index but that basic research accounts for under 7 per cent of R&D spending, against more than 15 per cent in the United States and Europe. The author links this gap and Western technological containment to a call for stronger state investment, a new-type whole-nation system for core technologies, and clearly defined roles for national laboratories, research institutes, universities and leading firms. On industry, Qu stresses that traditional industries, over 80 per cent of manufacturing, can also generate new quality productive forces through digital and green retrofitting. The author also proposes large-scale demonstration of mature new technologies, and strategic patience for future industries such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing and the metaverse, whose paths are uncertain.

For institutions, Qu proposes multi-level financial services built around patient capital, tolerance of failure for state-backed venture funds, and legal and self-regulatory measures against involution-style competition by firms and local governments. The author also calls for deeper opening up, both through cooperation with developed countries and through joint building of industrial chains and governance rules with emerging and developing countries. Read the original if you want a compact policy-oriented reading of how the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference links innovation, industrial upgrading and institutional reform.
quoteEn: The upgrading of traditional industries must aim at digitalisation, intelligentisation and greening, so as to climb towards the high end of the industrial value chain.
quoteZh: 传统产业改造升级要瞄准数字化、智能化、绿色化的发展方向，实现向产业价值链高端攀升。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in contrast to growth based on resource consumption.
A goal put forward at the 20th Party Congress (2022): an industrial structure that combines advanced manufacturing, digital and green technologies and the real economy.
The official economic objective since about 2017, prioritising efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
An approach to mobilising national resources for strategic science and technology goals, combining state coordination with market mechanisms.
Intense, low-value competition such as destructive price cutting, which the authorities have criticised as harming market health.

t: On the disciplinary system, academic system and discourse system of Marxist theory and their interrelations
zh: 论马克思主义理论学科体系、学术体系、话语体系及其相互关系
source: Studies on the Discipline of Marxist Theory (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Yuan Yinchuan and Yu Fang ask how the three systems that the 20th Party Congress (2022) told scholars to build for philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics (disciplinary, academic and discourse) should be understood in the field of Marxist theory, and how they relate. Their thesis is that the three form an integrated whole in an "one body, two wings" pattern: the disciplinary system is the fundamental support, the academic system the core and bridge, and the discourse system the basic carrier.

The article opens by citing Xi Jinping's speeches and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on building an autonomous knowledge system. It then takes each system in turn. The disciplinary system is traced from Marxist theory education to the creation of the first-level discipline of Marxist theory in 2005, with its sub-disciplines and supports (courses, textbooks, teaching staff, scholarly style). The academic system is analysed through its epistemology, axiology and methodology. The discourse system is analysed through its subjects, objects, themes and methods.

In the authors' account, the academic system rests on knowledge about the nature, origins and content of Marxism, on a value orientation of "for the people", and on dialectical and historical materialist methods. The discourse system asks who speaks, to whom, what is said and how, and the authors argue that good discourse unites political, academic and popular language. On the relations, they say the discipline is a "fundamental support" but not an "absolute precondition". They hold that Marx's "revolution in terminology" before the formal discipline existed shows academic and discourse systems can precede it. Without academic substance, discourse is empty symbols and the discipline is rootless. Yet discourse is the final outlet, and academic ideas can run ahead of their matching vocabulary.

The authors conclude that the three systems are mutually dependent, interpenetrating and convertible, and together aim to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. They call for stronger leadership by the Marxist theory discipline, and for internationalising its discourse so that the world knows "academic China" as well as popular images of China. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how Marxist theory scholars conceptualise the "three systems" and the sub-disciplines and institutional supports of the Marxist theory discipline.
quoteEn: The disciplinary system is the fundamental support, the academic system is the core and bridge, and the discourse system is the basic carrier; the three complement, permeate, promote and transform one another, together forming an inseparable organic whole.
quoteZh: 学科体系是根本依托，学术体系是核心和桥梁，话语体系是基本载体，三者相辅相成、相互渗透、相互促进、相互转化，共同构成了一个密不可分的有机统一整体。

glossary.explanation: The authors' image for the three systems: the disciplinary system is the body, and the academic and discourse systems are the wings.

t: Western perceptions of new quality productive forces: main views and assessment
zh: 西方关于新质生产力的主要认知与评析
paras: Since Xi Jinping put forward the concept of new quality productive forces, Western media, think tanks, politicians and scholars have followed it closely. Zhang Lisi sets out to map how the West understands and judges the concept. The article argues that most Western commentary is positive, while a minority of views misread it and are driven by anxiety and interest. Zhang presents the survey as useful for understanding Western opinion contests and for deepening research on high-quality development and Chinese modernization.

The article draws on statements by outlets such as Reuters, the BBC, CNN, the Wall Street Journal, the Economist, Deutsche Welle and Bloomberg, and by scholars and officials from Europe, the United States, Australia, Japan and South Korea. It has four parts. The first sorts Western readings of the concept's meaning into four angles: development strategy, development philosophy, form of productive forces, and essential attribute. The second covers Western accounts of why the concept emerged. The third covers Western affirmations of its significance, plus a few cautions. The fourth is Zhang's own assessment.

Zhang reports that Western commentators see the concept as a response to China's need for economic revitalisation, a step to a new stage of productive forces, a continuation of the new development philosophy, a key to building a modernized socialist country, and a support for international competitiveness. Many are said to expect new momentum for China and the world and to treat the concept as a development of Marxist productive-force theory. Zhang then explains the attention by China's achievements and by Western anxiety over technological rivalry. Zhang characterises the minority of critical views as four moves: the "overcapacity" theory as a theoretical trap, linking the concept to national security, attaching ideological labels, and zero-sum thinking.

Zhang concludes that Western opinion is mostly objective and favourable, and that this is based on China's economic record. Zhang calls for better external communication to tell the story of new quality productive forces, high-quality development and Chinese modernization. The article also calls for a calm analysis of the roots of bias, a readiness to rebut smears, and a search for shared interests with other countries. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-school scholar's classification of Western commentary on the concept, and the official framing of foreign criticism as ideological and zero-sum.
quoteEn: Positions fixed in advance and the pursuit of interest are the reasons behind some Western misreadings and one-sided views of new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 立场先行、利益主导是西方对于新质生产力的一些误读和片面观点产生的原因。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new production factors and industrial upgrading, and is tied to high-quality development.
An official goal that shifts emphasis from rapid growth to quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability in China's economy.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A set of five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) set out in 2015 to guide China's development.

t: Accelerating an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences as a strategic force for building a leading education nation
zh: 加快构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系 打造教育强国战略引领力量
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, Chen Yulu takes up the newly issued Outline of the Plan for Building a Leading Education Nation (2024–2035). The Outline names the construction of an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences as a strategic force for strengthening higher education. Chen argues that universities should take the lead in this task, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

This short commentary has three parts. It first sets out why an autonomous knowledge system matters, then explains the advantages universities hold, and finally proposes five routes for building the system.

Chen contends that new phenomena arising on the path of Chinese modernization require systematic explanation from the social sciences. The article also links the project to international discourse power, cultural confidence and the training of talent. Universities are said to have three advantages: strength in basic research, a broad and interdisciplinary range of disciplines, and their role as a window for exchange with the outside world. The five routes are to strengthen moral education and the cultivation of talent, autonomous training of personnel through "new liberal arts" and AI-enabled programmes, theoretical innovation rooted in Chinese practice, policy advice through university think tanks, and strategic communication abroad.

Chen concludes that Chinese philosophy and social sciences should move from solving Chinese problems to contributing to global ones, offering "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese solutions" within global education governance. Read the original if you want a university president's official-line account of how higher education is expected to carry out the Party's agenda for philosophy and social sciences.
quoteEn: The key to building an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences lies in taking root in Chinese soil and innovating China's own concepts, theories and methods.
quoteZh: 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系，重点在于扎根中国大地、对中国自主的概念、理论和方法进行创新。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Xi Jinping's call for China to build its own concepts, theories and disciplines in philosophy and the social sciences rather than relying on Western frameworks.
An Education Ministry initiative to reform humanities and social science education through interdisciplinary programmes and integration with technology.

glossary.en: moral education and the cultivation of talent
glossary.explanation: The official fundamental task of education, combining moral and political formation with the training of students.

t: Several foundational questions for theoretical innovation in the digital economy
zh: 数字经济理论创新的几个基础问题
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, this commentary asks which basic questions must be settled before economic theory can be renewed for the digital economy. Hong and Shi argue that three issues come first: the nature of data as a factor of production, the measurement of data's value and of its contribution to growth, and the changes that data and artificial intelligence bring to relations of production. They treat recognising data as a new factor as only the starting point of theoretical innovation.

The authors first set out the properties of data: it is non-consumable, non-exclusive and highly mobile, and it takes effect only when combined with labour, capital, technology and management. They then turn to valuation and pricing, to the measurement of data's contribution to growth, and finally to four shifts in production relations: AI replacing labour, asymmetries on platforms, the digital divide and cross-border data competition.

On value, Hong and Shi apply Marx's labour theory of value. Data's value is condensed human labour: labour in forming raw data, transferred objectified labour in collection and processing, and the living labour of data workers. Because data combines with other factors in non-linear, context-dependent and time-sensitive ways, they say its value creation extends the labour theory of value. They note that non-exclusivity challenges the scarcity assumption of conventional theory, and that free digital services are hard to explain with it. Fully competitive market prices could in principle reveal data's value, but such markets do not yet exist. The authors point instead to market design theory, experimental economics and simulation, and they warn that hasty recognition of data assets on balance sheets could produce a 'data asset bubble'. Drawing an analogy with the 'productivity paradox', they say that better measurement of intangible capital is needed to capture data's role in growth, which calls for a production function suited to the digital economy.

The authors conclude that economic growth theory, measurement and statistics all need innovation, and that production relations deserve equal study alongside the growth of productive forces. They call for evidence-based research tied to digital practice. They also call for scientific grounds for a fairer and more inclusive model of growth, since without good governance gig workers, small firms and consumers are weak against platform capital. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language agenda linking Marx's labour theory of value to data pricing, growth measurement and platform labour relations.
quoteEn: Treating data as a new type of factor of production is an important theoretical innovation, but it is only the starting point of theoretical innovation in the digital economy.
quoteZh: 将数据视为一种新型生产要素是一项重要的理论创新，但这只是数字经济理论创新的起点

glossary.en: data as a factor of production
glossary.explanation: Official Chinese policy and academic term for treating data as a production factor alongside land, labour, capital and technology. Chinese policy documents have promoted it since around 2019–2020.
Marx's theory that the value of commodities derives from socially necessary human labour. Chinese authors often cite it as the guiding framework for analysing new economic forms.

glossary.en: recognition of data assets on balance sheets
glossary.explanation: The accounting practice of recording data resources as assets in company financial statements. Chinese regulators began to allow this in 2024.
A Marxist term for the social relations, above all ownership and class relations, into which people enter in production. It is contrasted with productive forces.

t: The threefold logic of building an independent knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences
zh: 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系的三重逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 17 February 2025
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's remark during a visit to Renmin University of China that building Chinese philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics ultimately means building China's own independent knowledge system, He Xiying asks what logic underlies that project. The article, a newspaper commentary, answers that the system rests on three logics: a knowledge logic, a strategic logic and a world logic. In He's formulation, the foundation lies in "knowledge", the core in "strategy" and the key in "the world".

The piece is organised in three sections, one per logic, each with three sub-arguments. The knowledge logic treats the system as an expression of the subjectivity of Chinese culture, of the national spirit and of the spirit of the times. The strategic logic links it to national subjectivity, to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to Chinese modernization. The world logic links it to a reshaped view of human civilisation, a reshaped global knowledge order and a rewritten world history.

On knowledge, He argues that the Communist Party, as heir to Chinese cultural subjectivity, is the main force behind the system. In the author's view, the information age calls for a new system in which autonomous knowledge production prevails over dependent production. On strategy, He holds that the system should rest on critical reflection on the Western frameworks formed in Western modernization. The author also holds that the system should turn new theory from the rejuvenation process into knowledge, because academic discourse is said to lag behind China's comprehensive national strength. On the world, He presents the project as a dialectical unity of "breaking" and "establishing": it sublates existing disciplinary and discourse systems under the principle of "putting ourselves first and drawing on others for our use", and aims at "Eastern learning spreading west".

He concludes that the system is more than self-production and self-consumption. In the author's account, it offers original Chinese contributions to the sum of human knowledge, and concepts such as Chinese modernization, common values of humanity and a community with a shared future for mankind already embody it. He treats it as a key support for rewriting world history and for securing China's standing among nations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary frames the official call for an independent knowledge system.
quoteEn: Building an independent knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences is by no means simply \"producing and consuming for ourselves\"; its aim is to make an original Chinese contribution to \"the sum of human knowledge\".
quoteZh: 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系绝非单纯的“自产自销”，其目的在于为“人类知识的总和”提供中国人的原创性贡献

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's own path of modernization, promoted in Party documents especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022), as distinct from Western models.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's calls to build Chinese philosophy and social sciences on China's own concepts, categories and discourse rather than on Western frameworks.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A core official goal of the Party, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations built on shared interests and cooperation, and a central slogan of Chinese foreign policy discourse.
An official formulation put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015, usually listed as peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom.

t: A theoretical examination of building an original academic system for Chinese philosophy
zh: 构建中国哲学原创性学术体系的学理审视
paras: Wu Xiangdong takes up the task of building an independent body of knowledge in Chinese philosophy and social science, which he treats as resting on an original academic system for Chinese philosophy. Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Wu argues that the task can only be advanced by first clarifying three concepts in the formulation: "academic system", "originality of Chinese philosophy" and "construction".

The article proceeds through these three keywords in turn. It first separates the academic system from the discipline system and the discourse system. It then grounds the originality of Chinese philosophy in the question of autonomy and subjectivity, drawing on Xi Jinping's remarks on the matter. Finally, it asks who should do the building and by what method.

Wu defines the discipline system as the institutional platform, the academic system as the core content (an organic whole of concepts, categories, propositions and methods) and the discourse system as its form of expression, which also carries discourse power. Philosophy, in Wu's account, is the theoretical self-awareness of a nation's practice, so China's own path of Chinese modernization requires a philosophy of its own. Wu cites Fairbank's later revision of his "impact–response" model as support for the view that China's modernization has internal sources. On method, Wu names the Two Integrations as the main route and applies them to three relations. In the relation of past and present, Wu calls for critical inheritance of traditional philosophy so that Marxism becomes Chinese and tradition becomes modern. In the relation of China and the West, Wu calls for openness and mutual learning. In the relation of theory and practice, Wu holds that China's philosophy must come from the practice of Chinese modernization, be tested in it, and be expressed in language the people understand.

Wu concludes that Chinese philosophers, as the agents of construction, must be encouraged to develop their own subjectivity. Wu notes that philosophy and social science in China still have numbers but lack top-level masters, and calls for more effort to cultivate them. The piece is a programmatic statement of how the official goal of an autonomous knowledge system could be understood in philosophy. Read the original if you want a concise Party-aligned account of how Chinese philosophers conceive the relation between academic system, discourse and the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: The discipline system is the institutional platform, the academic system is the core content, and the discourse system is the form of expression.
quoteZh: 学科体系是建制性平台，学术体系是核心内容，话语体系是表达形式。

glossary.explanation: A formula stressing the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It is presented in Party discourse as the key method for adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
In the Party's three-part scheme (discipline, academic and discourse systems), the body of concepts, categories, propositions and methods that makes up a discipline's knowledge.
The system of terms and expressions through which a field's ideas are stated and made influential. The author treats it as both a form of expression and a kind of discourse power.
A slogan in recent Party discourse for philosophy and social sciences built on China's own experience rather than on Western frameworks.

t: Building a Chinese discourse system of logic
st: Lessons from Western research on ancient Chinese logical thought
zh: 构建中国逻辑话语体系
paras: Li Dubai and Wang Kexi ask how contemporary China can build its own discourse system of logic, and argue that tracing Western scholarship on ancient Chinese logic offers useful guidance. They treat Chinese logic as one of the three source traditions of world logic, alongside Greek logic and Indian hetuvidya (yinming), and as basic to Chinese philosophy. Their thesis is that Chinese logicians should draw on Western research while grounding their work in Chinese cultural and historical context and avoiding uncritical "interpreting China through the West".

The piece, a commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (25 January 2025), surveys Western research in broad phases. It begins with missionary sinology and James Legge's translations, then the early twentieth century, when Hu Shi and Feng Youlan mediated Chinese thought to the West. It moves on to the 1950s–60s, when professional philosophers took over and the "China has no logic" view prevailed, and then to the 1970s onward, when scholars such as A. C. Graham, Chad Hansen, Chung-Ying Cheng and Christoph Harbsmeier advanced the field. It ends with twenty-first-century work.

The authors make three main moves. First, they say early Western and Chinese-émigré scholarship either overlooked logic or, as with Hu Shi, explained Mohist ideas by analogy with Western deduction and inductive methods, which they judge did not bring out Chinese logic's distinctiveness. They quote Bochenski and others to show that the 1960s denial of Chinese logic rested on a narrow, Aristotelian idea of logic. Second, they credit later scholars with recognising its richness: the 1973 New Encyclopaedia Britannica entry, Cheng's three levels of study, Ian Johnston's 2009 complete translation of the Mozi, and interdisciplinary and culturally situated approaches. Third, they criticise formalising studies that presuppose a rigorous two-valued extensional system, ignoring the language and cultural setting, and note the concentration on the pre-Qin period at the expense of later developments, including the reception of Indian and Western logic in China.

The authors conclude that Western studies give Chinese logic a reference frame and an "other" perspective, and that China's growing international standing offers a chance to spread Chinese logical thought globally. They call for research that pursues modern transformation vertically and mutual learning between China and the West horizontally, producing a three-dimensional model linking past and present, China and the West. They also urge cultural confidence and a base in local history. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-scholarly overview of Western sinological work on Chinese logic and of how Chinese logicians propose to respond to it.
quoteEn: In building a contemporary Chinese discourse system of logic, one must base oneself on China's own cultural and historical background, maintain cultural confidence, and avoid blindly \"interpreting China through the West\" by relying on Western interpretive frameworks.
quoteZh: 在当代中国逻辑学话语体系建设中，要立足中国本土的文化历史背景，保持文化自信，避免依赖西方的解读框架盲目“以西释中”

glossary.explanation: The Indian Buddhist tradition of logic and debate, transmitted to China; the article counts it as one of the three source traditions of world logic.

glossary.literal: using the West to explain China
glossary.explanation: The practice of explaining Chinese thought with Western concepts and frameworks, which the authors caution against when it is done uncritically.
A term prominent in Party discourse since the 2010s, stressing confidence in China's own cultural traditions; here it is applied to logic scholarship.

t: Accelerating the building of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics from a new starting point
zh: 在新的起点上加快构建中国特色哲学社会科学
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 8 August 2024, Xu Yanguo takes up the question of how to speed up the building of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, eight years after Xi Jinping's symposium on the subject (2016). Xu argues that the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) has again called for an innovation project in the field and for an independent Chinese knowledge system. The commentary holds that the field should review the past eight years and act from a new starting point.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the value of this work in the new era. The second lists four tasks for accelerating it. The third discusses how to pool the forces involved. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks on the field, including that the task is a systematic project needing top-level design.

Xu offers three reasons for the work's importance: it provides theoretical support for Chinese modernization, it gives scholarly backing to the Party's theoretical innovation, and it is a lofty mission for the field. On the last point, Xu argues that Chinese philosophy and social sciences largely came from the West and carry the imprint of Western social systems. In Xu's account, such theories struggle to explain Chinese practice, especially in strongly ideological disciplines. The four tasks are research oriented to practice, summing up the laws behind China's successful practice, scholarly interpretation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and building an independent knowledge system, starting from signature concepts.

On coordination, Xu calls for stronger planning across the 'five armies' of researchers: universities, Party schools, military academies, research institutes and Party and government research bodies. Xu also proposes guiding research topics, adjusting course design and giving more weight in academic evaluation to work that builds the field. Each institution type should play to its strengths, and disciplines should merge, including with the natural sciences and artificial intelligence. Read the original if you want a short, official-line outline of the priorities and institutional measures proposed for building Chinese philosophy and social sciences after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The fundamental problem in building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics in the new era is to shift the focus of research towards practice.
quoteZh: 新时代构建中国特色哲学社会科学的根本问题，是要解决研究重心向实践倾斜的问题

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A slogan for building Chinese-originated concepts and theories in the humanities and social sciences, rather than relying on Western frameworks. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2022 and 2024.
Academic elaboration of Party theory in disciplinary terms, so that official ideas become systematic scholarship.

A shorthand for the five groups of social science researchers: universities, Party schools and administrative colleges, military academies, research institutes and Party and government research bodies.

t: The originality requirements for building China's independent knowledge system
zh: 建构中国自主知识体系的原创性要求
paras: This commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks what originality means for building China's independent knowledge system (自主知识体系). Huang and Xiang define that system as one composed of original concepts, theories and methods, and present its construction as the fundamental task of building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. Their thesis is that originality must be built on materialist-dialectical methodology, following four standpoints Xi Jinping has named: practice, history, dialectics and development.

The article is organised in four sections, each pairing one standpoint with a requirement. These are: drawing original results from the practice of Chinese modernization; a people-centred orientation; an open, inclusive attitude towards other bodies of knowledge; and continuing to write a new chapter in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Xi Jinping's speeches are quoted throughout as the guiding framework.

In the first section, the authors argue that knowledge comes from practice. Scholars should therefore find original questions in the practice of Chinese modernization, distil regularities from it, and test their theories against it. Huang and Xiang describe the relationship between theory and practice as a "double helix". On the people-centred orientation, they say the system should express the people's will, serve their spiritual needs, and be judged by their satisfaction, and they call on scholars to leave the "ivory tower". On openness, they say Marxism, fine traditional Chinese culture and foreign scholarship must be unified through the Two Integrations. Foreign ideas are to be sifted critically and never applied wholesale as a "sole standard". The authors say this ends the "apprentice" status of Chinese scholarship.

The authors conclude that theoretical innovation never ends, because practice keeps raising new questions. They hold that contemporary China is undergoing an unusually grand practical innovation that poses many unanswered problems. They call for a system that shows subjectivity, originality and scholarly rigour, centred on "what we are doing", and that answers questions of China, the world, the people and the times. In their account, this will open new horizons for contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official methodological criteria now applied to knowledge-system building in Chinese social science.
quoteEn: Building China's independent knowledge system means thoroughly changing the \"apprentice\" status of Chinese philosophy and social sciences.
quoteZh: 建构中国自主知识体系，就是要彻底改变中国哲学社会科学的“学徒”状态。

glossary.explanation: A slogan stressed by Xi Jinping from 2022 onwards. It calls for Chinese philosophy and social sciences to rest on their own concepts, theories and methods rather than on Western frameworks.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western modernization. It was formally elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping put it forward in 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
A principle in Xi Jinping's thought that policy and scholarship should serve the people's interests. Here it is applied to the aims and evaluation of academic research.

t: Upholding cultural subjectivity to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚持文化主体性 构建中国特色哲学社会科学
paras: Writing in China Social Sciences Today (7 August 2024), Lin Yahua asks how China should build a philosophy and social sciences system of its own. The author argues that this requires cultural subjectivity. Without it, Lin holds, a country cannot achieve intellectual independence or maturity, nor gain discursive power and initiative in international dialogue. The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's 2016 symposium speech on philosophy and social sciences.

The commentary is organised around three requirements. The first is to take root in fine traditional Chinese culture. The second is to rest on the great practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The third is to face the prospect of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and strengthen the reach and influence of Chinese culture. A short closing paragraph ties the three together under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On tradition, Lin presents the continuity of Chinese civilization as the basis of the project. Lin cites the 20th Party Congress (2022) list of traditional ideas and Xi's claim that they connect with communist and socialist ideals. Lin's examples are the moves from minben (the people as the root of the state) to democracy and from enriching the people to common prosperity. On practice, Lin argues that China's transformation is not a copy of its past, of Marxist blueprints, of other socialist states or of Western modernization, so scholars cannot analyse it with Western theoretical systems or value-laden discourse. Lin points to the socialist market economy, whole-process people's democracy and socialist ecological civilization as innovations that research should explain. On communication, Lin calls for new concepts and categories that connect Chinese and foreign audiences. Lin also calls for research on translating political discourse, and for approaching ordinary people's lives in a confident, calm and inclusive spirit.

Lin concludes that only by doing so can China break the cultural hegemony of "Western centrism" and hold the power to interpret its own development. The new system should explain the sources of China's peaceful development in tradition, refine Chinese experience through practice, and set out the historical significance of the Chinese path and the comparative strengths of its institutions. It should also offer ideas and solutions for problems humanity shares. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official case for cultural subjectivity as the basis of China's philosophy and social sciences.
quoteEn: Building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics must be grounded in the great historical and contemporary practice of the Chinese nation, using Chinese reasoning to sum up Chinese experience and raising that experience into Chinese theory, neither blindly following dogmas nor copying foreign theories, so as to achieve intellectual independence.
quoteZh: 构建中国特色哲学社会科学，必须立足中华民族的伟大历史实践和当代实践，用中国道理总结好中国经验，把中国经验提升为中国理论，既不盲从各种教条，也不照搬外国理论，实现精神上的独立自主。

glossary.explanation: A term in recent Party discourse for a nation's capacity to think and act from its own cultural foundation rather than depending on outside frameworks. It is closely linked to cultural confidence.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping. It stresses people's participation at every stage of governance, not only in elections.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping and the Chinese Dream.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has emphasised in the past decade as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist market economy and Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

t: On the holistic wholeness of Marxism
zh: 论整体的马克思主义整体性
source: Collected Papers on Marxism in the New Era
paras: Yu Bin asks what it means to grasp the wholeness (zhengtixing) of Marxism as a whole. The article argues that most existing studies of Marxist wholeness fail to do so, because each takes one feature, theme or angle and treats it as the key. Yu proposes instead a "holistic" wholeness that covers the whole of Marxist theory and the whole of its practice.

The article opens with a survey of Chinese scholarship on the question. It sorts the positions into groups: those that identify a core (scientific worldview, scientific socialism, critique, practice); those built on a unifying theme (abolishing private property, human liberation, critique of the logic of capital); those that use one or several perspectives or dimensions; those that stress unity of several aspects; and those that stress completeness. Yu then develops two parts of the author's own account: the wholeness of Marxist theory, and the wholeness of theory and practice.

Yu argues that the three component parts of Marxism (philosophy, political economy, scientific socialism) cannot be linked by a neat formula, such as philosophy guiding economics. Citing Engels on the "negation of the negation" in Capital and on the separate routes by which the English, French and Germans reached communism, Yu holds that the parts are independent and complementary, and valuable for their differing content. On this view, wholeness means mastering all the classic works, including Engels's military writings and Marx's mathematical manuscripts, so that useful parts can be found when new problems arise. On practice, Yu holds that unity of theory and practice means using practice to realise truth, not using theory to explain reality. The article offers Lenin's New Economic Policy and Deng Xiaoping's "second leap" in rural reform as examples. It also defends the agreement of logic and history against Meng Jie.

Yu concludes that the holistic wholeness of Marxism covers Marx, Engels and Lenin's theory, plus later theories that practice has tested and the people have endorsed. The article lists Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Yu says it excludes work by parties or scholars that departs from basic Marxist principles, naming some Soviet leaders and some Western Marxists. Yu also contends that partial mastery of Marxism has weakened its ability to answer real problems and contributed to its marginalisation. Read the original if you want a critical map of Chinese debates on Marxist wholeness, or an argument for reading the Marx-Engels Collected Works in full.
quoteEn: Therefore, upholding the unity of theory and practice does not mean using theory to explain reality, but using practice to realise truth.
quoteZh: 因此，坚持理论与实践相统一，不是拿理论去阐释现实，而是要用实践去实现真理。

glossary.explanation: A long-running topic in Chinese Marxist scholarship about how Marxism's parts form a unified system. The article argues most accounts grasp it only partially.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, written into the Party constitution in 2007. It stresses balanced and sustainable development.
Theory associated with Jiang Zemin, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, adopted into the Party and state constitutions.

t: The mission and tasks of building the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems
zh: 学科体系学术体系话语体系建设的使命任务
paras: Qu Lindong, a historian, takes up the goal of building disciplinary, academic and discourse systems with Chinese characteristics, Chinese style and Chinese manner (the "three systems"). The piece appeared in the People's Daily on 2 August 2021. Qu argues that the three systems are distinct in emphasis but form one inseparable whole, and that building them is now a major task for Chinese philosophy and social science.

Writing mainly from the standpoint of history, Qu first traces the idea to Mao Zedong's 1938 call to give Marxism a Chinese form, and to Xi Jinping's later instruction on building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The article then takes the three systems in turn, using examples from historiography such as Li Dazhao, and Bai Shouyi's General Introduction to Historiography and his multi-volume General History of China.

Qu holds that the disciplinary system is strategic and holistic. It should be assessed and coordinated to suit social and scientific change, and it should foster a \"big discipline\" awareness and interdisciplinary work. The academic system is the middle link, in which theory matters most. Qu says that combining historical materialism with Chinese historical reality is the correct path for historical theory. The discourse system carries research results to society and underpins \"discourse power\". Qu proposes that traditional historiographical concepts, such as \"the relation between Heaven and humanity\" and \"talent, learning and insight\", can be creatively transformed and combined with Marxist historiography.

Qu concludes that the three systems are a grand undertaking that needs both ambition and painstaking work, and that scholars should advance it steadily. Qu calls for stronger cultural consciousness and confidence, especially regarding national character and continuity in discourse. Read the original if you want a short, official-media statement of how a historian links the three systems to Marxist historiography and Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Building the discourse system is a manifestation of the vitality of the academic frontier.
quoteZh: 话语体系建设是学术前沿活力的呈现

glossary.zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系
glossary.pinyin: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
glossary.literal: discipline system, academic system, discourse system
glossary.explanation: A formula, associated with Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences, for building a Chinese philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics, Chinese style and Chinese manner. It is often shortened to the "three systems".

t: The mission and tasks of building the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems
zh: 学科体系学术体系话语体系建设的使命任务
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in August 2021, historian Qu Lindong considers how to build a disciplinary system, an academic system and a discourse system with Chinese characteristics, Chinese style and Chinese manner (the "three systems"). Qu argues that the three have distinct emphases but form an inseparable whole, and that building them has become a major task for philosophy and the social sciences in the new era.

Qu writes from the standpoint of history as a discipline while keeping the whole field of philosophy and social sciences in view. The piece first traces the historical roots of the task, from Mao Zedong's 1938 call to make Marxism take on Chinese characteristics to Xi Jinping's present formulation. It then takes the three systems in turn, drawing examples mainly from Chinese historiography.

On the disciplinary system, Qu stresses overall assessment and coordination, so that disciplines can learn from one another and work across boundaries, citing Li Dazhao's and Bai Shouyi's accounts of history's links to other fields. The academic system, the middle link, is defined by each discipline's nature, and Qu holds that combining historical materialism with Chinese historical reality is the correct path for historical theory, as in Bai Shouyi's General History of China. The discourse system is the most concrete and complex link, because it concerns concepts and terms through which research reaches society. Qu proposes that traditional historiographical concepts, such as "the relation between Heaven and man" and "talent, learning and insight", be transformed creatively and combined with Marxist historiography.

Qu concludes that building the three systems is a grand undertaking that needs both ambition and meticulous work. Qu calls for stronger consciousness and confidence about national character and continuity in discourse, and urges scholars to carry the task forward. Read the original if you want a short, officially published statement of how a historian links the "three systems" agenda to Marxist historiography and classical Chinese conceptual resources.
quoteEn: Combining historical materialism with the actual history of China is the correct path for building the theoretical system of historical studies.
quoteZh: 唯物史观与中国历史实际相结合，是历史学理论体系建设的正确路径。

glossary.zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系
glossary.pinyin: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
glossary.literal: disciplinary system, academic system, discourse system
glossary.explanation: A formula from Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences, calling for these systems to show Chinese characteristics, style and manner. It is a central slogan in discussions of building a Chinese philosophy and social science.
The Marxist theory of history, treated in Chinese scholarship as the guiding principle of historical research.

t: On the wholeness of Marxism
zh: 论马克思主义的整体性
paras: Existing discussions of the wholeness (zhengtixing) of Marxism agree that it matters, but they disagree on how to define it. Many scholars try to ground it in philosophy, political economy or scientific socialism, the "three component parts" named by Engels and Lenin. Hou Huiqin argues that each choice has an unresolved weakness and that the discussion should change course. In Hou's view, the philosophical world outlook (dialectical and historical materialism) is the key to Marxism's wholeness, and the theme of human emancipation through working-class liberation is its core.

The article has three parts. The first holds that Engels's and Lenin's three-part scheme served popularisation. It traces the "new world outlook" reading through Marx's planned work on dialectics, Lenin's "single block of steel", Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. It also criticises the "post-metaphysical turn" of Western philosophy and of Western Marxism. The second part sets out why the world's material unity makes a whole worldview possible. The third part turns to the ideas that follow from this: the proletariat, the people and the real individual, and the theme of emancipation.

Hou argues that a whole worldview must solve three problems: the unity of nature, society and mind; the unity of past, present and future; and the unity of appearance, essence and being. Idealism, including Hegel's, and traditional materialism fail on these, whereas dialectical materialism, with contradiction as the source of self-movement, succeeds. From this Hou derives several claims. Political economy and scientific socialism are studies of the laws of history. Marxist categories are "contradictory concepts" that rest on experience but go beyond it. The proletariat is a scientific concept, not an empirical occupational group. Hou says Western social science rests on dogmatic assumptions about human nature. The unifying theme is that capital's polarisation and reification of people can be overcome only through the proletariat's world-historical role.

Hou concludes that this theme joins Marx and Engels to their successors and explains why basic Marxist principles have not become obsolete. It also marks the main thread of contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Hou ties this to the claim that upholding the Communist Party's leadership means upholding the leadership of the Chinese working class, and warns against "de-classed" talk of the people. Read the original if you want a worldview-centred account of Marxism's unity, with close use of Lenin, Mao and Deng and a sharp critique of Western Marxism and liberal social science.
quoteEn: The core of the wholeness of Marxism lies in its consistent theme, which has formed a theoretical tradition passed down in an unbroken line.
quoteZh: 马克思主义整体性的核心，在于它具有一以贯之的主题，形成了一脉相承的理论传统。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Chinese Marxist studies for the internal unity of Marxist theory. Debate centres on whether it rests on philosophy, political economy or scientific socialism.
Lenin's account of Marxism as made up of philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. It follows Engels's earlier division in Anti-Dühring.
The Marxist doctrine of socialism and communism, said to rest on historical materialism and the theory of surplus value. It is set against earlier utopian socialism.

The tradition of Marxist thought that began with Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci and includes the Frankfurt School. Chinese orthodox writers often criticise it for turning away from materialist worldview and class politics.

t: The scientific meaning of the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems and how they relate
zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系的科学内涵与相互关系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2020, Tian Xinming takes up Xi Jinping's call to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics through three systems: the disciplinary system, the academic system and the discourse system. The article asks what each system is and how the three relate. Tian's answer is that they form a dialectical unity: the disciplinary system is the overall framework, while academic and discourse systems are two inseparable but relatively independent aspects of every discipline.

The piece has three numbered sections. The first explains why philosophy and social sciences form a disciplinary system and what gaps remain in China's. The second shows that systematic theories make up the academic system and systematic concepts make up the discourse system. The third explains why building each of them still counts as a separate task. Tian draws on Mao Zedong's On Contradiction, Marx's 1859 Preface, Engels and Lenin.

Tian's core argument starts from materialist dialectics. Disciplines are separated by the particularity of the contradictions they study and linked by the universality those contradictions contain, so they form a layered system topped by Marxist philosophy. Knowledge moves from perception to concepts, which Tian calls the cells of thought. A discipline's concepts therefore express its theory, and a mature discipline unites both. Tian cites Marx's historical materialism and its categories as the model, and Engels's remark that new insights in a science bring a revolution in its terminology.

Yet the two are not identical. Tian says they develop out of step, as when Marx and Engels first voiced new ideas in Hegelian and Feuerbachian language. The same word can also carry different meanings in rival schools, as with profit and rent in Marxist and classical political economy, or Lenin's point about "experience". Ideological struggle thus appears as a contest over discourse and discourse power. Tian calls for upholding Marxist guidance in the discourse system, guarding against discourse infiltration, "discourse traps" and discourse hegemony, and coining signature concepts that international audiences can understand. He also urges stronger top-level design for neglected emerging and interdisciplinary fields. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official reasoning for treating discourse-building as a task separate from theory-building in Chinese social science.
quoteEn: The academic system is the systematic theory and knowledge that reveals the essence and laws of a discipline's object; the discourse system is the verbal expression of that theory and knowledge, the form in which the academic system appears and its linguistic carrier.
quoteZh: 学术体系是揭示本学科对象的本质和规律的成体系的理论和知识；话语体系是理论和知识的语词表达，是学术体系的表现形式和语言载体。

glossary.explanation: The capacity to set the terms and concepts in which issues are discussed. In Chinese official writing it is often tied to the aim of strengthening China's voice internationally.

t: Revisiting the integrity of Marxism
zh: 再论马克思主义的整体性
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu Sikao), 2017 no. 1
paras: Zhao Jiaxiang takes up a problem in Chinese Marxist teaching and research. Following Lenin, Marxism has three main components: philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. In Chinese universities these are usually taught in separate departments. Zhao argues that this split leaves scholars knowing only one component and weakens understanding of Marxism as a whole. The article contends that Marxism is a unified, internally connected system and should be studied as one.

The article builds its case in six parts. Four ask what shows Marxism's integrity: its social and historical conditions, its theoretical sources, the content of the theory, and the course of its historical development. A fifth examines the classic texts, and a sixth proposes ways of grasping and applying the whole. The text was published in 2017 and also notes recent institutional changes, such as the creation of Marxism as a first-level discipline in 2004.

Zhao's central move is to show that the three components arose from the same conditions and sources and interpenetrate in content. Industrial capitalism and the rise of the working class made the revolutions in philosophy, political economy and socialist theory possible together. German classical philosophy, British classical political economy and utopian socialism did not each feed one component alone. Zhao then reads works such as the 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology, Capital and Anti-Dühring as integrated texts. Zhao proposes that The German Ideology be described as marking the basic formation of Marxism as a whole, not only of historical materialism. The second move concerns method. Zhao calls for combining history, theory and classic works ("shi, lun, zhu"), drawing on the author's own studies of the "two never's" principle, the Asiatic mode of production and the debate on socialism in one country. Zhao also warns against a simplified, one-principle-per-problem view of linking theory and practice, saying complex problems need principles from all three components.

Zhao concludes that the current Marxist textbooks are still a "platter" of three separate parts rather than an integrated account. The author says that training teachers able to grasp Marxism as a whole is a long task, but that the work of integration cannot wait for it. Zhao offers the article as a spur to others and mentions more than a dozen of the author's own papers on Capital from this standpoint. Read the original if you are interested in how a senior Chinese Marxist philosopher argues for integrating philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism, and in debates on Marxist pedagogy and textual study in China.
quoteEn: The components of Marxism were born, and achieved their revolutionary transformations, under the same social and historical conditions and in the same epochal setting, which necessarily makes them an internally unified and complete theoretical system.
quoteZh: 马克思主义各个组成部分的诞生和所实现的革命变革，有同一的社会历史条件和时代背景，这就必然使它的各个组成部分构成内在统一的完整的理论体系。

glossary.explanation: The term for the Marxist theory of socialism and communism, set against the earlier utopian socialism. In Chinese teaching it is one of the three components of Marxism, alongside philosophy and political economy.
In 2004 Marxist theory was made a first-level academic discipline in Chinese higher education. Many universities then set up schools of Marxism.
Zhao's formula for studying Marxism: the history of Marxism, its basic principles, and the classic texts, studied together.
A concept in Marx's writings on pre-capitalist societies, long debated by Marxist scholars. Zhao has studied its place in Marx's and Engels's schemes of social formations.
